## 2026-09-29: Playtest-3 benchmark: the human out-expanded both the Hard AI and the Proxy
- **The same map is effectively one game.** Re-seeding every scripted brain's tie-break jitter (16 salts) left seat 0 identical through turn 136, and outcomes diverged only after about turn 150. To get a spread, measure across maps, not across brain seeds.
- **The human was far ahead of both bots in its own seat.** On the playtest-3 map a Hard AI in that seat had 3 cities and 2 VP at turn 136, against the human's 8 cities and 7 VP. It won 0 of 16 games. Proxy v4 won 16 of 16, but only at turns 229–238 and after founding just 3 cities.
- **The master gap is unchanged.** On 200 rotated Standard maps with barbarians on, Proxy v4 still beats 7 Hard AIs 63.0% of the time, the same as around playtest 2. G8's pacing levers only shorten games: 60.5%, with the median win moving from turn 211 to 190.
- **The largest macro gaps are expansion after the second city and Settler escorts.** The Hard AI's third city comes at turn 135 against the human's 65, and its Settlers spend 35 turns per game outside its borders with a military unit on the same tile only 7% of the time; the human's did 40%.
- **Coalitions form but don't fight.** All 26 AI alliances in the playtest named the human as the coalition target, but only 2 AIs declared war.
- **`legatum-sim` Proxy runs default to barbarians off.** Pass `--barbarians true` for current-rules numbers.
- Details: `~/LegatumData/analysis/playtest3/benchmark.md` and `crates/sim/examples/playtest_bench.rs` (replay a save and report macro metrics, play the save's map with any brain in seat 0, or run rotated maps).

## 2026-09-29: Playtest-3 AI post-mortem: barbarians still change builds, and the coalition never fights

- Replaying `playtest3-final-1849` with a fresh Hard `ScriptedBrain` on each seat's view reproduced all 945 taped AI turns exactly, so a playtest tape is a complete, re-runnable record of AI reasoning. `crates/sim/examples/playtest_ai_trace.rs` dumps per-turn state/events and checks this; test-only probes inside `production` and `diplomacy` print option values and war-declaration inputs at dumped turns.
- G10's "barbarians never change what a city builds" only covers `item_base_value`. `plan_emergency_production` still uses `ctx.threat` (barbarians included): 9 civilian builds were converted, including 291 Settler Production (Germany's first Settler at 147/190 at T50; it stayed at 1 city all game).
- `choose_item`'s time discount (`value × 60 / (turns + 60)` at Standard) makes a 50–64-turn Settler lose to a Workshop with lower value (Germany T81: 912 vs 1037). At the 3-Production floor the Settler rarely wins again.
- Hard leader pressure never arms an AI at Peace: `desired_army` only adds it with a reachable *enemy* (at-war) city. AIs willing to declare on the leader could not see it (scouts dead and never rebuilt), and the one that could reach it had aggression 25: two coalition wars, 0 battles.
- The AI Switzerland never built a Market in 136 turns; the human Switzerland built four. AI gross gold stayed at 1–5 per turn, below every 2×-cost purchase price, so "unspent gold" in these games is poverty, not hoarding.
Full analysis: `~/LegatumData/analysis/playtest3/ai-failures.md`.

## 2026-09-29: Playtest-3 release check fixes

- **A flex row of totals needs the totals rigid and one designated shrinker.** `.stockpiles { min-width: 0 }` let the Iron and Coal chips shrink under their content, so "Coal 30 (0)" drew over "Pop." and the research text ran into TURN at 1440, 1280 and 1024. Totals are now `flex: none` and only the research cell (`flex: 1 1 0; overflow: hidden`) shrinks. Media queries could not keep the research text readable, because the bar's content varies (0 to 2 stockpiles, the treasury warning, a one- or two-line plan): at 1440 the worst case was 21 px too wide while the common case fitted. `TopBar` measures instead: after each render it applies compaction steps (`TOP_BAR_COMPACTION`: stockpile names, the warning's detail, cell padding, incomes, the wordmark, the Research label, the Technologies button) until `.tb-stats` stops overflowing and the research text is whole, and only then truncates. The header's size never depends on the steps, so the ResizeObserver cannot loop. Phones got two separate fixes: two stockpiles share one 44 px cell (two 44 px chips stacked were 90 px in a 52 px bar), and the treasury warning moved into the Gold cell (as a grid item it pushed Research onto a second row). `e2e/topbar.spec.ts` checks both boxes and visible text for overlap at 1440, 1280, 1024 and 390 in both looks.
- **Chromium reports `net::ERR_ABORTED` for a 204 response whose body is never read**, after the fetch has already resolved (the archive POST). A release check that counts `requestfailed` events should match each one against the response status and filter 204 + `ERR_ABORTED`, or every turn looks like a failed request.
- **Core resolves Influence in a fixed order: income, then border claims (phase 10), then the diplomacy boundary** (breach fines, pact eligibility, signing costs). A forecast that compares the signing cost with the current pool is wrong whenever a border tile becomes affordable that turn: the Pact card said "go 1 into debt" and the pool went to −10. `boundaryInfluence` (influence.ts) is the first step of the same projection that gives border forecasts.
- **Found City stays validated at resolution only.** `validate_orders` sees the true state, so rejecting there would reveal hidden cities and borders, and a check against the player's view could reject an order that resolution would accept (a capture earlier in the same turn changes the tile's owner). The UI disables the button from the player's own knowledge (`foundCityBlocker`), and the report explains a Settler whose destination stopped being a legal site, since core keeps the move going.
- **A label and its click must come from the same decision.** The phone's "Next: Unit" label came from the CTA's decision while the click asked `nextDecision()` for whatever follows the selection, so with the last unit selected it opened Research. Next now calls the CTA's own action.

## 2026-09-29: UI clarity pass 2: names, places and screenshots across a merge

- **Core writes player names into its own text.** Even after every UI surface used `empireNameOf`, report lines still said "blocked by AI 3's Scout": MoveBlocked reasons are formatted in Rust with the raw player name. The report context now has `renamePlayers(text)` (your / "Switzerland'"), applied to core reasons. When changing how the UI names something, grep the event reasons core formats too.
- **A tooltip on a legend under a bottom-anchored panel pops by itself.** The lens panel grows upward when a lens with a longer legend is chosen, which slides the legend under a cursor that never moved; Chromium fires the hover and the tip covered the key. Place such tips beside the panel (`placement="right"`), not over it.
- **Anything drawn under unit tokens must avoid the token footprint.** The barbarian camp was drawn under units, so a guard hid its pennant completely. A guarded camp now stands left of the token with its pennant mirrored to fly left; an empty camp fills the tile. Check canvas marks with and without a unit on the tile, in both looks: the red dashed outline read on Atlas paper but not on Court's dark terrain until it got a light halo.
- **Hover cards and city banners.** `placeCard` already avoided DOM panels; banners are canvas, so `draw` now returns their rects (`bannerRects`) for the card anchor's avoid list.
- **Like-for-like screenshots across a rules-changing merge.** After merging G10, the pre-merge save no longer loads in the new engine. Keep a copy of the pre-merge `app/src/wasm-pkg`, and serve a `git archive HEAD app` snapshot with that old package (plus a cloned `node_modules`) on another Vite port: the after shots then use the exact save and states of the before shots. New-engine features (barbarians) get their own before/after pair from a post-merge save, with the merge commit as "before".

## 2026-09-28: UI clarity pass (G13): patterns that worked

Audit: `docs/ui-audit-2026-09-28.md`.

- **Name the target.** A primary button that names where it leads ("Respond to the offer", "Give the Soldier orders") beats a generic one ("Go to first decision"). "Keep planning" is the dialog's ✕ and Esc, not a third button: three equal buttons wrapped to two rows and had no visual hierarchy.
- **Rules go behind the action.** Hints and panels had become rule dumps: the capital hint listed Fortify, Sleep, Wake and Heal, and the Scout panel floated an italic rules paragraph over the map. One action sentence in view, rules in the tooltip or in the guide chapter the hint already links to. Every fact stays reachable; nothing is deleted.
- **One primary per screen counts across panels.** On phones the sheet's unit action and the turn row's Next were both filled primaries. Each component was correct on its own and wrong together. Decide the primary from the whole screen: while one of our units or cities is selected, the turn row steps back.
- **The default-focused button must be the visual primary, and it must be safe.** Game over focused "View the map" (showing a focus ring) while "Back to title" was filled, so both looked primary. Now the focused, safe choice is filled, and Return can never leave the game.
- **Destructive actions don't belong beside navigation.** The top bar's research "Clear" was styled like Victory and Technologies, and it also caused the research chip to clip at 1024. The panel's "Clear queue" is enough.
- **Stacking bugs only show when the menu is actually open at phone size.** The game menu was painted under the phone's VP strip and bottom sheet (all at the HUD's z-index), so Save and Exit were unreachable. A `.topbar:has(.menu-pop)` z-index raise fixed it without touching the other overlays.
- **Copy must follow the rules.** A hint said every other team is at war with you, after diplomacy made Peace the default. Hint copy that states a relation now reads it from the view (`hintCopy`).
- **One naming function for anything that names an empire in text.** "Switzerland (Swiss envoy)" came from gluing faction and player name together in three places (`empireTitle`, `empireLabel`, `format.ts`). `empireNameOf` now decides once: faction first, and the player name only when it adds information (not a seat default, doesn't restate the faction, or two teams share the faction). Surfaces that still print a raw player name (the victory race rows, unit possessives) are listed in the audit.
- **Map labels that share a hex need one geometry source.** The settle badge had its own "0.8 r above centre" and the resource medallion its own "top of hex", so they collided. `medallionTop(hexPx, city, stacked)` now tells the badge where the medallion ends. Likewise, the stack lift is a shared `STACK_LIFT` constant, not two 0.3 literals. When a case can't be found in a real save (a resource under Best spot, a stack on a resource), stage it by editing the local view in the browser: render only, no orders.
- **Tooling.** A save made by one core build may not load after a core change (G9 added unit XP), so keep a "before" save and server from the old commit: a `git archive` snapshot plus a symlinked `node_modules` on a second Vite port. After `scripts/build-wasm.sh`, the running dev server reloads, and screenshots taken during that reload time out, so re-run them.

## 2026-09-28: The minimap (playtest 3, G5)

- There was no free bottom-right corner. On wide desktops (> 1280 px, mouse) the unit command bar owns the whole bottom centre (384 px to width − 352 px) and the turn dock owns the corner, so the minimap takes the corner and the turn dock stacks directly above it (Civ 6 puts Next Turn over the minimap). At 1280 px and below, and on every touch tablet, the unit panel docks in the left column and the bottom row is free, so the minimap sits beside the turn dock. Phones get a 44 px Map button between the race strip and the lens toggle, opening a modal overview (`data-game-overlay`, so gameplay keys pause while it's open).
- The first cut clipped the player's own race row at 1440×900 (pillar 4) while leaving a ~50 px dead gap above the turn dock: the race had a fixed cap (`100% − 72px − 352px`) and the dock was capped by the race's bottom, so neither used the other's slack. Two fixed reserves can't share a column. Now the dock takes what it needs (capped only so the race keeps `--race-min`), VpTrack publishes the dock's measured `--dock-height`, and the race gets exactly the rest: one-directional, so no resize loop (a mutual race-bottom ↔ dock-height dependency drifts a few px per frame). The race's own row is `position: sticky; top: 0; bottom: 0` inside `.vp-rows`, so it stays in view whenever the rows must scroll (1024×768 touch rows are 62 px: eight can't fit). Off phones the Developed Empire line moved into your own row's breakdown, and the ≤ 860 px compact race rules now apply up to 960 px, which fits all eight rows at 1440×900 and 1280×800 in both looks, and at 1366×1024.
- A panel that hugs a fixed-aspect canvas should size from the canvas: fit the map into a max width and height, then let the panel shrink-wrap it. The first cut gave the panel the column's width and centred the map, which left dead margins.
- The main camera lived in a MapCanvas ref. `map/camera.ts` now exposes it: MapCanvas registers a host and calls `notifyMapCamera()` from its draw loop only when x, y, zoom or the canvas size changed, so the minimap redraws its frame on pans and zooms without polling or per-frame work. `centerOn(hex)` / `centerOnWorld(x, y)` snap; the store's `jumpTo(hex)` is still the eased focus pan.
- The map does not wrap horizontally: `tileIndex` returns −1 off the offset grid and `clampCamera` clamps x, so the minimap is a plain rectangle.
- On macOS's case-insensitive filesystem `Minimap.tsx` and `minimap.ts` in one folder are the same module to TypeScript (TS1261, and the import resolved to the wrong file). The pure half is `minimapView.ts`.
- `auditOverlaySlots` treats the map canvas as a slot, which is right on phones (the canvas is a reserved region) but on desktop and tablet the full-screen canvas intersects every HUD panel. `e2e/minimap.spec.ts` drops the canvas layers before asserting no overlaps.
- A Vite dev server started in an agent worktree whose `app/node_modules` is a symlink to the main checkout answers 403 for font files (they resolve outside Vite's allowed root), so screenshots silently use fallback fonts, and `e2e/lenses.spec.ts` (which runs its own Vite server and fails on any console error) fails all six cases. Clone instead of linking: `cp -cR <main>/app/node_modules app/node_modules` is an instant APFS copy-on-write clone. `e2e/staging.spec.ts` also needs `target/debug/legatum-server`, not just the release build.
- `src/mock/mockClient.test.ts` "keeps view() fast" failed in a full `vitest run` at load average 191 (other agents running) and passed alone. It is a wall-clock test; rerun it before treating it as a regression.

## 2026-09-29: Barbarians (G10): a reserved owner, and the cost shows up in AI expansion, not survival

- Barbarian units are ordinary units owned by a reserved `PlayerId::BARBARIAN` (u8::MAX) on `TeamId::BARBARIAN`, outside `GameState::players`. `GameState::player` returns a shared read-only record for it (neutral Japan unit stats); `player_mut` has none. Movement, combat, capture, sight and fog handle them unchanged, and they can never get Gold, VP, a brain or a diplomacy row. The crashes this approach exposed were all direct `players[owner.0 as usize]` indexing, in core `reset_turn`, AI `purchase_defense`/`military` and the TS mock. Always go through `player()`/`team_of()` (TS mock: `playerOf`/`teamOf`) for a unit's owner.
- Anything that holds per-team or per-owner state has to accept an owner outside `players`: threat memory (`threat_observations`), `PlayerView::team_of`/`faction_of`, the fuzz occupancy oracle, and the UI's `atWar`.
- Sims: a barbarian-free AI would have looked fine on eliminations (0.04 per game) and game length (unchanged). The real cost was 5 to 7% of empires never founding a second city. Traces showed three causes: a captured first Settler (the AI then waits for Workshop and Granary before retrying), defenders interrupting a Settler build in a 3-Production capital, and Settlers waiting on remembered danger. Two things helped: camps 6 from cities instead of Civ 6's 4, and not letting barbarian threat change city builds, since they never assault cities. It is still 3 to 5% versus 0 to 1% without barbarians. Always measure "never reached a second city" when adding any neutral threat.
- Staging settings are acknowledged by comparing JSON strings, so a new optional room field must either be sent by both sides or be compared normalized (`settingsAcknowledged`). Four LAN specs caught this after the server began echoing `barbarians: true`.
- Game-setup flags that default On for new games but Off for old saves: `serde(default)` plus `skip_serializing_if` false keeps Off setups byte-identical, so old tapes still hash. The new state (`GameState.barbarians`) is an `Option`, and saves carrying it are `save_version` 5, so older builds refuse them instead of silently dropping the camps.
## 2026-09-29: Map resources, increment 1 (G11 "Iron on the map")

- A guaranteed deposit isn't a usable one. With every start's Iron placed 3–5 hexes out, 23% of AI empires never owned an Iron source (24 Quick games, median first source turn 62): border growth ranks tiles by yield, so a ring-3 Hills tile was never picked, and rivals' second cities claimed deposits that faced them. Two changes fixed it (4.7% never, median turn 38 over 240 games): borders pull toward known unclaimed Iron/Coal (+3 on the deposit, +2 next to it; `resources::border_pull`, shared by both border paths and mirrored in the mock), and the guaranteed Iron prefers the ring-3 tile farthest from other starts. Test a placement guarantee by whether empires end up *owning* it, not by whether mapgen placed it.
- Start fairness survives resources only if every start gains the same quality. Guaranteed start bonuses are flat-land Food/Production types (+6 quality each start); strategic deposits are hidden at the start, so `site_quality` ignores them; other deposits keep out of radius 3 of every start. `placement::validate_rivals` rechecks the spread with resources.
- Pay-on-start with refunds needs one reconciliation hook, not per-path bookkeeping: `resources::switched(state, city, previous)` runs wherever `producing` changes (orders, queue advance, deferral, invalidation, bought buildings), and completion calls `release(.., false)`. Payments live on `Player.resource_paid`, so a captured city's paid build is simply dropped; the stale entry is ignored because it no longer matches the city's previous build. The cap limits income only, so a refund is never lost.
- A resource shortage is a *temporary* queue blocker (skip and keep, like a missing spawn tile), not a `production_blocker`: otherwise `can_produce` fails and players can't even queue a Trooper behind other work while the Iron accrues. SetProduction and the head of SetProductionQueue check it; later queue items pay when they start.
- Every AI brain goes through `Brain::orders`, now a provided method that hides resource-blocked options and drops orders beyond the stockpile (`crates/ai/src/stockpile.rs`); brains implement `plan`. Two cities starting Troopers on the last 10 Iron would otherwise fail validation, and several full-game tests assert every AI order validates.
- The settle advice (`app/src/map/settleAdvice.ts`) recognises breakdown lines by label prefix, so core's "Known radius 2:" label must keep that prefix when it changes.
- City banners are several hexes wide, so anything drawn at the top of a hex (resource medallions) is hidden on the city's tile and its same-row neighbours. `bannerRect()` (sprites.ts) gives the rect before drawing, and a covered medallion moves beside the unit token instead.
- The mock's turn resolution pre-validates unit orders, which would report a same-turn Iron shortage in validation wording; the mock leaves the Iron check to apply time so its OrderFailed text matches core.
- Playwright can edit a WASM save losslessly: quote integers of 16+ digits before `JSON.parse`, edit, drop `archive`, stringify and unquote, then `loadSave`. That builds a mid-game scenario (a city owning Iron, a known tech, a stockpile) without a Rust fixture. Screenshots taken right after `loadSave` catch the fading loading plate; wait for `.loading-screen` to be gone.
- Balance (240 games per speed, same seeds, master `6882b24` vs G11): best/worst faction win rate 3.46x → 3.50x at Quick and 2.53x → 3.19x at Standard; both were already far over pillar 8's 1.5x. Sparta is unchanged (~5–7%); Byzantium drops ~1.5 points at both speeds (within noise). See docs/sim-results/2026-09-29-g11-resources-increment-1.md.

## 2026-09-28: Civ-style yield icons (playtest G6)

- The yields lens drew a parchment chip with icon + digit per yield on every tile, plus a blue wash over the whole map; the player called it "way too busy". Now `app/src/map/yieldIcons.ts` draws each yield as its icon repeated per point (Civ stacks: 1, 2 side by side, 3 as a triangle, 4 as a square, 5+ one icon and a numeral), no chip, no wash, under units and banners. Icons at hex radius ≥ 18 px (zoom ≥ 0.5), one dot per type down to 11 px, nothing below (zoom < 0.31).
- The UI's `--y-*` tokens are deepened for Atlas paper, and at 10 px they sank into the painted terrain. On the map the icons use the bright (Court) hues in both looks with a 1 px dark rim, built once per size as a sprite (the tinted silhouette drawn at 8 offsets under the fill); `ctx.shadowBlur` per icon would cost a blur per draw.
- A tile with all five yields, or two collapsed numerals, is wider than its hex at the bottom, where a pointy-top hex narrows. The cluster shrinks its icons (to 60% at most) to stay within 1.2 r instead of spilling into the neighbours.
- The hover tile card read `TERRAIN_YIELDS` while the lens used `terrainYields(faction)`, so a Celts player saw 2 food 1 production icons on Hills but "2 production" in the card. The card now shows the faction-adjusted numbers with the base terrain as the breakdown. Any glance display and its detail card must read the same function.

## 2026-09-28: Diplomacy inbox as a decision card (playtest G4)
- What a PlayerView knows about another empire: `cities` holds visible and remembered (fogged) cities, `units` only those in sight this turn, tile owners come from memory. "Where is AI 4" (`app/src/empires.ts`) reads only these, so it can't leak fog; with nothing known it says "Location unknown: not met yet".
- "Show on map" (`jumpTo`) centers the whole viewport, and at 1440 and 1024 that point sits under the story-column inbox: the empire's city ended up half hidden behind the panel. Any control that jumps the map from an overlay must close the overlay (the pending offer keeps its "Respond to offer" CTA to come back).
- `.game.phone-game :is(button, summary…) { min-height: 44px }` makes every `.link` button 44px tall on phones, so its border-bottom underline floats ~20px below the words as a stray rule. For inline links in phone layouts, underline with `text-decoration` and enlarge the hit area with an absolutely positioned `::after`.
- The treaty terms (Pact 8-turn minimum and 2-turn notice, Alliance 12 and 3, breach 25/50 Influence, 3 guaranteed turns) were bare literals in `crates/core/src/diplomacy.rs` while the UI hard-coded "eight-turn" copy. They are now `TreatyKind::{minimum_turns, notice_turns, breach_cost}` and `GUARANTEE_TURNS`, exported to `app/src/rules.generated.json` by the ui_rules test, so definitions (`app/src/treaties.ts`) can't drift. Pure refactor: same numbers, no rule change.
- The desktop top bar has no spare width at 1024: a fifth stat (Influence) squeezed the research chip to a single "(". Between 701 and 1180px the stat cells tighten and "N stored" Science moves into the Science tooltip.

## 2026-09-28: Settle lens review (G1): passing specs, three visual defects

Astra's six settle-lens Playwright cases all passed on the first browser run, yet screenshots at 1440×900, 1024×768 and 390×844 showed three problems no assertion covered. (1) The desktop click inspector was a column from the first-game hint down to the dock, so it sat on the inspected hex and every unit near it; `assertDockClear` only checks panels against each other, never against the map point being explained. It now goes beside the hex. (2) Canvas badges are drawn under DOM overlays: at 1024×768 the first-game hint hid "Best spot" and "#2". `drawLens` now takes the panel rects MapCanvas already samples for the compass and moves a covered badge below its hex. (3) A reason keyed only on the label ("+ food-rich surroundings" for the land term) reads the same on Great and Poor sites; the land reason is now relative to the best reachable score. Lesson: for anything that explains a map spot, screenshot it and check that the explanation doesn't cover the spot and that a Poor example reads as poor.

## 2026-09-28: Promotions (G9): the fixtures never fight, and the mock's ranged phase had drifted

- The three 40-turn determinism tapes (and every other committed tape) came out byte-identical after adding combat XP: games start at Peace and nobody fights in 40 turns. A rule that only acts in combat needs its own tape; `crates/wasm/examples/promotion_tape.rs` starts two empires at War (`legacy_all_war`) and fights until both Soldiers promote.
- The mock's ranged phase used its own RNG stream (`this.rng([COMBAT, 1, id])`), reported a defender roll, and let a shot unit heal the same turn; core uses `Rng::derive(seed, [turn, COMBAT, stage 0, attacker, target])`, reports defender roll 0, and marks every damaged unit as having acted. Only the new mock/WASM promotion parity test (which compares whole results, not chosen fields) exposed it. Parity tests should `toEqual` both engines' full outputs for the scenario.
- AI games are sparse on fighting (65 battles per 8-empire Quick game, 117 at Standard), so with Civ 6's per-fight XP and thresholds (halved at Quick) only ~13% / 8% of surviving units are promoted at game end, mostly level 1. Battles per game do not double at Standard although thresholds do, so Standard promotes fewer units. Faction spread was unchanged within noise (Quick 4.20x → 3.54x, Standard 2.44x → 2.32x on 250 paired games; see docs/sim-results/2026-09-28-g9-promotions.md).
- Held-out coalition seed 910030 (`crates/sim/tests/coalition_stall.rs`) went from ending at turn 408 to 726 with promotions: any rules change reroutes it through the same title deadlock (0 captures, every team at 5–9 VP for hundreds of turns). Its 700-turn bound is now 900; the deadlock itself is the known long-game source, not a promotion effect.
- Fixture tapes must have distinct seeds: `replay_export.rs` exports the whole fixture directory and rejects two tapes with the same seed (the first promotion tape reused `u64::MAX - 10`, the production-queue tape's seed).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` passed while `npm run build` (`tsc -b`) failed on an unused private method: the build config is stricter. Run `npm run build` before committing app changes.

## 2026-09-28: Wake-on-sight makes Fortify a no-op next to a visible enemy

- `wake_threatened_sleepers` runs before the first movement round, so a unit re-fortified while an enemy military unit is in sight within its movement range wakes again in the same resolution. Played in a browser: a garrison Soldier and Scout two hexes from an enemy Soldier woke every turn ("woke: enemy military in sight within movement range"), and F could not keep them out of the cycle. Civ 6 only wakes Sleep/Alert, never Fortify. Resting defense is unaffected (it is separate state), so this is cycle noise, not a combat bug. Open design question, not changed yet.

## 2026-09-27: Playing the Civ 6 turn-flow controls in a browser (B1, B2, F9)

- The loading plate kept `data-game-overlay` through its 450 ms fade-out, so the first Return, F or arrow press after a load or new game was silently dropped. The fading plate is already `pointer-events: none`; it now stops blocking keys too. Four turn-flow specs written without a browser failed on exactly this.
- A keyboard-activated control keeps focus (so native Enter and Space work), which means after choosing production with Enter, Return re-pressed that production button and Escape did nothing; 12 Tabs reached the map. Escape on a plain focused control now hands focus back to the map (after a first Escape closes the focus tooltip, which Tip handles in the capture phase).
- Every unit order auto-advances to the next unit after a 120 ms timeout, which cleared the selection when no unit was left. Pressing Return within 120 ms of F (or B, H, a move) selected the idle city and then lost it, so Return looked dead. The advance now runs only if the selection hasn't changed since the order.
- The This Turn CTA names the decision after the current selection, so with the last idle unit selected it already reads "Choose production". Specs that looped "click N units need orders, Skip, until the label changes" stopped early; skip from the unit panel instead.
- Playwright specs written "correct by construction" without running a browser: 9 of 55 failed on the first real run. Run them before merging.
- A serialization-only core change (a new optional unit field) can be refreshed with a guarded example that proves clearing only that field restores every old hash (`crates/wasm/examples/standing_orders_tapes.rs`). The documented three-tape regeneration then reproduces the refreshed tapes exactly, which also proves the change altered no AI decision.

## 2026-09-27 — Celebrations hold the turn report, so report-reading e2e tests must skip them
In astra celebrate-ruins-2 the turn report drawer stays closed while the celebration sequence plays (up to three cards: 3.5 s notable, 5 s major, 6 s legendary, plus 1 s minor pulses), and opens when it ends or on any tap or Escape. A first-city Hot Seat turn (own major card plus the partner's) outlasts Playwright's 10 s expect timeout, so four existing game.spec/contrast checks failed on the first browser run. `game.spec.ts` now presses Escape (`skipCelebrations`) before reading the report, which is what a player does. That exposed a real bug: the game's Escape handler peels "the turn report first", and the report was still *requested* while held, so skipping a celebration with Escape also threw the report away. The lane now `preventDefault`s the Escape it consumes (`gameplayKeyAllowed` ignores prevented keys), so Escape peels one layer. The pressed "Show on map" accent label also fell below AA (3.81:1) under the shared `:active { opacity: .75 }`; it now darkens its background instead.

## 2026-09-27: The evolution film (tools/film): frame capture, narration and fact checks

- Deterministic video from a web page: draw every frame as a pure function of (scene, t) on a canvas (no `requestAnimationFrame`, no clock, no randomness; "random" is a hash of the index), then drive it from Playwright: `page.evaluate(FILM.frameJpeg(i, t))` returns `canvas.toDataURL("image/jpeg")`, piped into `ffmpeg -f image2pipe -c:v mjpeg -i -`. Frames can't drop because nothing runs in real time. Each scene encodes to its own H.264 file keyed by a content hash (scene JSON + renderer source + data), and `ffmpeg -f concat -c copy` joins them, so a rerun only renders what changed.
- A Playwright import from `.mjs` via `import()` of the CJS package gives `{ default: { chromium } }`, not `{ chromium }`. Agent worktrees have no `app/node_modules`; `tools/film/lib/pw.mjs` falls back to the main checkout's (found with `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`).
- `say` on this Mac has no Premium/Enhanced voices installed, only compact ones (Samantha, Daniel, plus the Eloquence set that sounds robotic). `say -o x.aiff` then `ffprobe` gives each sentence's exact length, so scene durations and captions follow the narration. `say` reads "–" as "en dash": replace dashes with "to" before speaking.
- Cormorant's figures are old-style (descending 3, 4, 5, 7, 9), which collide with labels under big numbers; data numerals go in Libre Franklin, as the app's tokens already say.
- Headless Astra works from a worktree: `codex exec -m gpt-6-astra -s read-only --output-schema` returned a storyboard in about 8 minutes for a 27 KB fact prompt. Structured-output schemas need every property listed in `required` (nullable instead of optional). The validator dropped one true sentence because "turn 150" only existed inside the key `ai_survival_t150`; metric names with `_t<N>` now count as turns.
- Node 26 has `zlib.zstdDecompressSync`, so readers open `.tape.json.zst` archives without the `zstd` CLI. `legatum-sim --replay-export` only takes the bare tape, so readers write the archive's `tape` field to a cache file first.
- Stand-in fitness saturates: with one game per candidate, "VP / top VP + 0.25 for a win" gives every generation's winner exactly 1.25, so the best-fitness curve is flat. The real run averages many games per candidate; the stand-in film is right to ignore that curve.

## 2026-09-27: Button contrast, popovers in scroll containers, and the lobby dock (playtest A1–A5)

- Measure contrast from pixels, not computed styles. `app/e2e/contrast.ts` forces each state with CDP `CSS.forcePseudoState` and diffs two screenshots per state: labels thickened with `-webkit-text-stroke` in their own colour (solid glyph cores, so anti-aliasing can't understate the ink) and labels made transparent (the real background). That catches opacity, `filter: brightness`, gradients and paintings, which a `getComputedStyle` walk misses. One screenshot pair per state for the whole screen keeps a game screen to a few seconds; a pair per label took minutes and timed the spec out.
- Wash-outs come from a generic `:hover` that sets a pale `background` on a control whose selected variant keeps pale ink. `.menu-pop button:hover` (0,3,1) beat `.seg button.on` (0,2,1): the game menu's selected Look went to 1.1:1 on hover. Same shape as the old Found City bug (`.act:hover` vs `.act.primary`). Selected/primary variants must restate their fill in their own `:hover`.
- `opacity` is the wrong way to disable: at 0.45 labels land near 2.5:1, and a `rise` entrance animation with `fill-mode: both` pins `opacity: 1` over `.btn:disabled`, so the title's disabled Continue looked enabled. Disabled controls now drop their fill and emphasis and keep muted ink at full opacity (≥5.8:1 in both looks); `e2e/contrast.spec.ts` holds disabled labels to AA too. The research tree's off-path "dimmed" techs (opacity 0.38, 1.9:1) got the same treatment.
- A popover positioned inside a scroll container follows its trigger when the container scrolls. If the trigger scrolls out of sight it ends up off-screen, so the faction picker now closes then, like a native select. Playwright's `hover()` scrolls every scrollable ancestor to centre the target, which scrolled the lobby behind the open list; the specs point by `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })` and `mouse.move` instead. `element.focus()` scrolls ancestors too: use `{ preventScroll: true }` and scroll only the list.
- Touch browsers focus a tapped button before its `click`. When focus also moves the highlight, "first tap previews, second tap chooses" can't read the highlight; it needs its own preview state.
- A flex item with `min-height: 0` and `overflow: auto` shrinks in proportion to its size, so a "the spacer gives way first" layout still cut a few pixels off the title menu (and above 820px, where the fan shows, it cut Settings in half). The menu is now `flex-shrink: 0` and a `::before` spacer above the wordmark takes the shortfall; `layout.spec.ts` checks for zero scroll, also with an extra Quit item.
- A sticky footer inside a scrolling column always reads as the next row, and content scrolls under it. The lobby's Start is now a full-width dock outside the scroll area (`LobbyFrame`'s `dock`).

## 2026-09-27: Game audio (first sound batch)

- ffmpeg's `aac_at` (AudioToolbox) encoder signals its start delay in the .m4a but not its trailing padding, so the decoded file ends with up to 1023 samples of digital silence: an audible gap at every music loop wrap. ffmpeg's native `aac` trims both ends. Fix in `tools/audio/build_audio.py`: make each loop a multiple of 1024 samples (drop a few ms of the decaying ending), then check decoded length equals the pre-encode length (docs/sound-qa.md).
- EBU R128 integrated loudness is undefined for clips under one 400 ms gating block (ffmpeg reports -70 LUFS). Measuring with 1 s of appended silence works because silent blocks fall below the absolute gate. Many Kenney clicks then hit the -1 dBTP ceiling before -20 LUFS; one (UI Audio `rollover2`) could only reach -28 LUFS and was swapped.
- Chromium's `decodeAudioData` trims AAC priming from these files, but sound.ts still skips leading near-silence at play time because WebKit behaviour differs; music uses media elements (a 7-minute stereo track decodes to ~150 MB of floats).
- Kenney's "Hit jingles" sit around A2–G3 (low orchestral hits) and "Pizzicato jingles" around C4–A#4; the Sax, Steel and 8-Bit sets were excluded by the brief. Key/mode estimates (pure-Python Goertzel chroma, no numpy on this machine) drove the major/minor choices; nobody has listened yet, so the dashboard Sound board collects verdicts.
- The dashboard `/api/state` crash noted under "App icon and favicons" is fixed: the state is built before `writeHead`, and a failure after headers destroys the socket instead of crashing.

## 2026-09-27: App icon and favicons

- `npx tauri icon` fills every `.icns` slot by downscaling the one 1024 master, so the 16 and 32 px slots (Finder lists, some menus) blur a detailed icon into a smudge. `tools/design/app-icon/build.mjs` runs `tauri icon`, then rebuilds `icon.icns` with `iconutil` from its own iconset, where the 16/32 px slots use a bolder small-size drawing. `tauri icon` also always writes `ios/`, `android/` and `Square*`/`StoreLogo` sets; the script deletes them until we ship those targets.
- Chrome takes the last `<link rel="icon">` that fits, so PNG fallbacks go first with explicit `sizes` and the SVG last; Safari ignores the SVG and uses the PNGs. With Vite's `base: './'`, absolute `/favicon.svg` links in `index.html` are rewritten to `./favicon.svg` and copied from `app/public/`.
- A favicon needs its own drawing, not the master scaled down: at 16 px only a self-contained parchment disc, one heavy ring, a bold A and the red star survive, and the disc keeps it legible on both light and dark tab strips.
- A lone four-point star at favicon size reads as the generic "AI sparkle", and a compass rose reads as a navigation app (Safari, Maps); that is why the mark is the wordmark's star-crowned A, not the house star alone.
- The dashboard server writes its 200 header before building `/api/state`, so an exception in `state()` (e.g. in a worktree with no `.progress/`) makes the catch call `writeHead` twice and crashes the process. (Fixed the same day; see "Game audio".)

## 2026-09-27: Ruin rewards are a string, so the UI cannot celebrate them truthfully

- (Superseded by astra celebrate-ruins: `RuinReward` is now a typed enum, and the roll is `range(0, 23)` with 8 Gold / 8 Science / 2 population / 3 map caches / 3 free Scouts; a Scout with no free adjacent tile, like population with no city, falls back to Gold.) Originally: `Event::RuinExplored.reward` was free-form text built in `explore_ruin` (`crates/core/src/rules/units.rs`), so the UI could print it but not fly the number to its counter, say what it buys, or tier the moment. The roll was `range(0, 2)` (inclusive), so Gold, Science and population were each one in three.
- Plan: a structured `RuinReward` enum (docs/design/hooked-loop.md, increment 1). This changes the event's data, not the rules.
- nirandfar.com returns a Cloudflare 403 to curl's default user agent. A browser User-Agent header fetches the pages.

## 2026-09-27: Tauri v2 on the iOS Simulator

- `npx tauri ios init --ci` needs no CocoaPods (the plugins' Swift code builds as Swift packages; the broken rbenv `pod` shim didn't matter). It installs `xcodegen` and `libimobiledevice` via Homebrew and adds the iOS rustup targets. `app/src-tauri/gen/` stays git-ignored: `scripts/build-ios-sim.sh` regenerates `gen/apple` when missing, and our iOS customizations live outside it (`tauri.ios.conf.json` is merged over `tauri.conf.json`; `Info.ios.plist` is merged into the generated Info.plist at build time). Config merges are JSON merge patch, so `app.windows` in the iOS file replaces the desktop array (that's how the 1100x700 minimums are dropped).
- `npx tauri ios build --debug --target aarch64-sim --ci` builds an unsigned simulator `.app` at `gen/apple/build/arm64-sim/Legatum.app` (no team needed); install with `xcrun simctl install`. The debug bundle is about 100 MB.
- In the iOS WKWebView the page is `tauri://localhost`, `.wasm` is served as `application/wasm`, and the desktop CSP applies unchanged (`ipc:` covers `ipc://localhost`). The iPad WKWebView sends a Mac user agent (`Macintosh ... Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7`) with `maxTouchPoints` 5, so detect iPad by touch points, never by UA alone.
- The dialog and fs plugins work on iOS: Save opens the "export to Files" picker and the chosen path is writable (the plugin leaves a 0-byte placeholder of the same name in the app's Documents), Load opens the document picker and reads the file (unregistered `.legatum` files are still selectable), Cancel resolves to `null`, and the `$APPDATA/autosave.legatum` mirror lands in `Library/Application Support/com.legatum.game/`. Closing the only window (`plugin:window|close`, our Quit) resolves OK but leaves a black screen with the process alive, so Quit is hidden on mobile (`canQuit()` in `app/src/tauri.ts`).
- `simctl` cannot rotate a simulator. Locking iPad to landscape in `Info.ios.plist` (`UISupportedInterfaceOrientations~ipad` plus `UIRequiresFullScreen`, which iPad requires for an orientation lock) makes it launch in landscape. `simctl io screenshot` then saves the raw portrait framebuffer, so rotate it with `sips -r 270`; the simulator control tool's taps also use portrait device points.
- To inspect the simulator's WKWebView from a script: `brew install ios-webkit-debug-proxy`, find the sockets with `lsof -aUc launchd_sim | grep webinspectord_sim.socket` (one per booted simulator), run `ios_webkit_debug_proxy -s unix:<socket> -c null:9221,:9231-9239 -F`, and send WebKit protocol messages to the page's `webSocketDebuggerUrl` wrapped in `Target.sendMessageToTarget`. WebKit's `Runtime.evaluate` has no `awaitPromise`; stash async results on `window` and read them in a second call.

## 2026-09-26: Hoverable tooltips must never cover their trigger

- The a11y pass made `.tip-bubble` take the pointer (`pointer-events: auto`, so WCAG 1.4.13 hover can cross into the bubble). The viewport clamp then laid right-placed bubbles near the screen edge over their own trigger: in the lobby's faction menu, focusing an option showed its bubble on top of it, the mouseup landed on the bubble, and the `click` (fired on the common ancestor) never reached the option. The staging e2e timed out with Alice stuck on the wrong faction. `placeBubble` in `app/src/ui/Tip.tsx` now flips to the next side (right→left→bottom→top) whenever the clamped bubble would intersect the trigger; `accessibility.test.ts` covers it.
- Hot Seat seats are now two buttons: seat selection (`aria-pressed`, name "<crest> <player> N orders") and a Ready toggle named "<player>: ready". A bare `/\bPlayer 1\b/` button locator matches both.

## 2026-09-26: Playwright e2e specs vs the real UI

- The turn report names every empire, the viewer included: "Player 1 founded Brasslock", never "You founded …" (only unit lines use "Your"). Assert founding lines by player name, scoped to the report drawer (the `complementary` holding the "What happened" heading).
- `/api/save` (and every saved game) writes `setup.seed` as a decimal string, not a number, so u64 seeds survive `JSON.parse` (`crates/wasm/src/json.rs`). Compare it with `'6'`, not `6`.
- LAN hosting no longer has a "Host the game" button when the server supports staging rooms: the host's lobby is the room, a guest takes a seat from Multiplayer > Join Game (seat N is `getByRole('row').nth(N + 1)`), names themselves and presses Ready, and only then is the host's "Start game" enabled. The old "Choose your seat" screen is only for joining a game already in progress.

## 2026-09-26: Title, fog, compass and WebKit performance

- Playwright's default Chromium is the headless shell, which rasterizes canvas in software: panning a 30-turn fogged 48x32 map at 2x DPR ran at 26 fps (35 ms map draws) there, but 118 fps (2.1 ms draws, 120 Hz vsync) in full Chromium launched with `channel: 'chromium'` and `--enable-gpu --use-angle=metal`. Measure frame rates with the GPU path, or the numbers mostly measure SwiftShader.
- Playwright WebKit (the engine family of Tauri's WKWebView) does not support `ctx.filter`, so the map takes the JS box-blur fallback (`canvasFilterSupported()` is false). It still pans at 58.6 fps with 2.8 ms average map draws; the worst frames (140–160 ms) are zoom-level changes that render new chunks. `?perf=1` (or Settings > Frame rate) shows fps, frame times and the active blur path; `?blur=js` forces the fallback in any browser.
- Real maps are mostly remembered terrain, so the mockup fog (55–80% desaturation plus a hatch) made most of the screen gray. Atlas now drains 20% of the color under a 34% paper wash (faded ink); Court uses 35% and a 30% lapis wash. To get a fogged mid-game state for renders, drive the WASM client from the page: give each unit a far `MoveUnit` target that passes `client.validate`, `endTurn` 30 times, then `loadSave` the result.
- Tauri v2 injects `__TAURI_INTERNALS__` even without `withGlobalTauri`, so the UI can close its window with `invoke('plugin:window|close', { label })` and no `@tauri-apps/api` dependency. `core:default` does not include closing: the capability needs `core:window:allow-close`.

## 2026-09-26: The painterly map in the real canvas renderer

- Everything that only changes on turn resolution (terrain, coast, relief, glyphs, towns, fog, territory, unexplored veil) is baked into 512 px chunks per zoom level (`app/src/map/terrain.ts`), about sqrt(2) apart in device-pixel scale. A frame is ~10–25 `drawImage` calls: 0.2–0.9 ms per frame and a steady 60 fps panning and zooming on a 60x40 map at 2x DPR (headless Chromium). A new turn diffs a per-tile signature and marks only nearby chunks stale; stale chunks keep showing until re-rendered within a 7 ms/frame budget, so turns never flash. Field rebuild per turn: ~25 ms.
- Coastline without per-chunk blurs: keep the land field as a JS float grid (4 world px), gaussian-blurred once per turn. For a straight coast the blurred field is Phi(d / sigma), so `sigma * probit(field)` is the signed distance to the coast. That gives crisp, anti-aliased coast and wave-ring lines at any zoom from one bilinear sample per pixel, and a summed-area table of "near coast" cells lets 16x16 blocks of pure land or sea skip the per-pixel work.
- Blurs inside a chunk fade at the chunk edge (the canvas filter treats outside as transparent), which shows as seams. Blur on a padded scratch canvas (72 px) and copy the middle.
- A look (Atlas light, Court dark) is one token block in `app/src/brand/tokens.css` under `:root[data-look]`. Even the panel frames are tokens: `--frame-image` is a 9-slice SVG data URI used as `border-image ... fill`, so the ink double rule and the notched deco corners (which a plain `border` + `clip-path` can't draw, since clipping removes the border along the notch) swap with the palette. `border-image-width` larger than `border-width` paints into the padding, which keeps content offsets identical across looks.
- Canvas text does not trigger `@font-face` loading; call `document.fonts.load()` for the faces the map uses and rebuild cached text sprites on `loadingdone`.

## 2026-09-26: UI type and map rendering (art-direction mockups)

- The CSS `font:` shorthand resets `font-variant-numeric`, so a `.num { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums }` class is silently undone by any rule that sets `font:` on the same element. Set `font-feature-settings: "lnum" 1, "tnum" 1` on `body` instead: `font:` doesn't reset it, and it inherits.
- Google's Cormorant / Cormorant Garamond serve old-style figures and ignore `lnum` in the served subset. Direction B sets all data numerals in its sans (Libre Franklin) for that reason.
- A hex map gets organic coastlines that still follow the hexes this way: blur the land-hex mask (6.5 px), threshold its alpha (`16a − 7.6`), and displace it with fractal noise (0.045, 11 px). Dilate-minus-mask rings then give the coast line and offshore wave lines. Terrain is static per game, so the app can render this once per zoom level to an offscreen canvas. Spec: `tools/design/directions.md`.

## 2026-09-26: Any number of human seats in the UI

- The UI's "seat" is an index into the local human seats (`store.humans`), not a player id; anything that talks to the engine (validate, forecast, end_turn keys, player colors) must go through the player id (`humans[seat]` or `view.me`). Before this, seat 0/1 happened to equal player 0/1, which hid several places that mixed the two.
- The web-target WASM package loads in Node/vitest with `init({ module_or_path: readFileSync('legatum_bg.wasm') })`; its default no-argument init tries to `fetch` a file URL and fails outside a browser. `src/store.test.ts` uses this to drive the real store against the real core (skipped when `wasm-pkg` isn't built).
- `GameState::hash` is FNV over the serde JSON of the whole state, setup included, so any new setup field changes every hash and breaks the determinism fixtures. `PlayerSetup.difficulty` uses `skip_serializing_if = is_normal` plus `serde(default)`: Normal games serialize byte-for-byte as before (fixtures and old saves unchanged), and only Easy/Hard games carry the field.
- `app/scripts/fake-lan-server.test.mjs` is a vitest file, but `npm test` only includes `src/**/*.test.ts`, so it never runs there (and `node --test` can't run it). Run it with a vitest config whose `include` is `scripts/**/*.test.mjs` until the app config includes it.
- Mapgen's start rules (7-hex spacing, 12 workable tiles) already fit 8 empires on a 40x26 map with rare retries; `crates/core/tests/map_sizes.rs` pins Small/Standard/Large for 2-8 players, so no proportional start-distance rule was needed.

## 2026-09-26: Cross-target replay coverage

- A matching final save hash does not verify continued play after loading. Both native and WASM tape checks now replay continuously and from a save/load at every turn boundary, including the initial and final states. Full saved-state equality and the recorded per-turn hashes are checked.
- The original WASM tape check returned only turn hashes, so it missed a wrong `initial_hash`. `Game.replay_tape` now verifies the initial hash too; the native fixture suite includes a deliberately corrupted initial hash to keep that rejection covered.
- Fixed mixed-brain tapes under `crates/sim/tests/fixtures/` pin 120 turns for seeds near `u64::MAX`, independently of subsequent AI changes. Their README documents intentional regeneration and cross-target checks.
- `wasm-pack` takes cache locks even when its binaries are already installed. In a restricted worktree, copy its existing cache into `target/` and set `WASM_PACK_CACHE` there; this keeps the normal optimized WASM build working without changing package metadata.

## 2026-09-26: Tauri desktop app

- `app/src-tauri` sits inside the root Cargo workspace's directory tree, so its `Cargo.toml` needs an empty `[workspace]` table or cargo refuses to build it ("believes it's in a workspace when it's not").
- Tauri adds nonces/hashes to the CSP it serves; per the CSP spec that makes `'unsafe-inline'` ignored, which would block React `style` attributes. `dangerousDisableAssetCspModification: ["style-src"]` keeps `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` working. The engine needs `script-src 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`. Verified by loading `app/dist` in Playwright WebKit with the same CSP header and starting a game: no violations.
- Agent sandboxes lack macOS Screen Recording permission: `screencapture -l <id>` and `-R` fail with "could not create image". Window ids are still readable via `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` (a small Swift script), but capturing needs a human or the permission granted.
- The Playwright browser cache can hold a WebKit build that doesn't match any installed playwright-core; launching a mismatched build via `executablePath` hangs. Install the matching one with `node <playwright-core>/cli.js install webkit`.

## 2026-09-26: Native LAN hosting

- `Session`'s `Box<dyn Brain>` must be `Send` to put the authoritative game behind an `Arc<Mutex<_>>` in an axum server. The stateless scripted/random brains already satisfy this; `Brain: Send` makes that requirement explicit while preserving the shared AI seeding and per-player-view logic.
- Explored cities remain in `PlayerView.cities` when fogged. LAN event filtering must check `CityView.visible` across the pre- and post-turn views, rather than treating every remembered city as currently visible. The server adds a regression fixture for this distinction.
- A reclaimed seat needs connection-identity checks on both incoming orders and disconnect cleanup. Otherwise the previous socket's late disconnect can detach its replacement. The server removes the old identity atomically and compares it again during cleanup.

## 2026-09-26: First large balance probe

- The default AI army target at four cities is five combat units; assigning one garrison per city leaves only one free unit, below the two-unit marching minimum. Matched knob experiments substantially increase captures without changing city rules. See [the balance probe](analysis/balance-probe-1.md) for evidence and proposed experiments; gameplay defaults remain unchanged.
- Simulator elimination averages are rounded: “0.00” in the 1,000-game report represents four eliminations. Keep event counts and denominators when drawing balance conclusions.
- Faction confidence intervals should resample whole games because the same faction occupies multiple competing seats. The requested mixed mode also fixes brain type by seat parity; a matched parity swap confirms the large scripted-versus-random gap.

## 2026-09-26: Determinism and WASM

- Never cast a `u64` seed or hash to `usize` in game logic: `usize` is 32-bit on wasm32, so `seed as usize` truncates there and native and WASM diverge (found in `GameSetup::standard`/`all_ai` faction assignment, which also overflowed in debug for large seeds). Reduce in `u64` first, e.g. `(seed % 3) as usize`.
- On wasm32-unknown-unknown, `catch_unwind` compiles but catches nothing: a Rust panic surfaces in JS as `RuntimeError: unreachable`, with the real message only in the panic hook's `console.error`. The UI must recover by rebuilding the `Game` from its last save.
- Save JSON contains `u64` bitset words as plain JSON numbers. JavaScript must treat the save string as opaque (never `JSON.parse` and re-serialize it) or precision is lost.
- `wasm-pack build --out-dir` is relative to the crate directory, not the current directory.
- Integer rounding: apply percentages to the result, not the delta (`total * 75 / 100`, not `total - total * 25 / 100`), or small values escape the modifier entirely. Found by the Astra core review in the Japan penalty and tech diffusion.

## 2026-09-26: Map generation

- Setting sea level by percentile (sort tiles by elevation, take the top N%) gives an exact land share every time, and rank-normalizing climate noise over land tiles turns terrain thresholds into shares. Together they made terrain tuning predictable.
- A global flood fill per candidate mountain tile is fast enough (<1 ms per 48x32 map in release) and guarantees ridges never split the continent.

## 2026-09-26: Testing the rules

- Test states with more than 2 military units pay upkeep, and a broke empire disbands a unit per turn. Fund the treasury in spawn and stacking tests, or units silently vanish.
- Two single-empire teams can never reach their VP targets on the same turn with the current numbers (each can bank at most 7 VP without titles, and there are only 5 titles), so simultaneous-winner tiebreak tests need teams of 3+.

## 2026-09-26: Web UI

- A zustand v5 selector that returns a fresh `[]`/object on every call puts React in an infinite render loop. Return stable references (module-level empty constants) or use shallow equality.
- Calling `setTimeout` as a method of another object (e.g. `obj.setTimeout = setTimeout; obj.setTimeout(...)`) throws "Illegal invocation" in browsers; bind it to `window`.
- Remember a LAN seat per tab (sessionStorage), not per browser (localStorage): shared storage made two tabs steal one seat back and forth.
- `scripts/build-wasm.sh` must run before `npm run build`/`tauri build`, or the app silently falls back to the mock client.

## 2026-09-26: Icon SVGs

- An SVG loaded through `<img src>` or CSS `url()` ignores the page's `color`, so `currentColor` renders black. To tint per player, icons must be inlined (for example a Vite `?raw` import injected as markup) or used as a CSS `mask-image` with a `background-color`. For the same reason, `app/src/assets/icons/preview.html` inlines every SVG.
- The icons avoid `id` attributes (no `<mask>`, `<clipPath>`, or `<defs>`), because inlining the same icon many times would create duplicate IDs. Cutouts use `fill-rule="evenodd"` instead.

## 2026-09-26: Agent tooling

- `pkill -f <pattern>` matches full command lines, including other programs' arguments: restarting the LAN server with `pkill -f target/release/legatum-server` also killed an Astra (codex) worker whose prompt text contained that path. Match the process name exactly (`pkill -x legatum-server`) or kill by saved PID.

- Worktree-isolated agents are sandboxed: Bash commands using `source`, `$HOME`/`$VAR` in paths or `$(...)`, and compound commands mentioning git can be refused, and the Write tool can't write outside the worktree. Call `$HOME/.cargo/bin/cargo` directly with literal paths, write files inside the worktree and `cp` them out, and give agents literal-timestamp examples for progress logs.
- `git add -A` in the main checkout picks up `.claude/worktrees/*` as embedded repos. They're now in `.gitignore`.

## 2026-09-26: Project setup

- In a repo with no commits, `git rev-parse HEAD` prints the literal `HEAD` to stdout before failing, so `$(git rev-parse HEAD || echo none)` yields `HEAD\nnone`. Use `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`. This broke the first version of the learnings Stop hook.
- `git diff` ignores untracked files, so fingerprinting changes with it misses edits to new files. The Stop hook hashes file contents instead.

## 2026-09-26 — Wordmark: kern the open pairs by eye, at display size
The hand-built `logo-legatum.svg` spaced every letter about 13 units apart. Equal gaps look even only between straight-sided letters. A–T (a diagonal next to an overhanging bar) read as a hole about twice as wide. My first fix pulled T left 13, which put the bar directly over the A's foot, and the user rightly said it was too tight. Settled values: G–A −3, A–T −8, T–U −2 (the T's stem is centered, so its right side is open too), then recentered. The rule's star and gap follow the A's star. Judge kerning on the real title screen at full size, with a range of options side by side, never one jump. Keep the 236×50 viewBox, because `Wordmark` and the title CSS hard-code that aspect ratio.

## 2026-09-26 — The server keeps its own faction list
`crates/server/src/staging.rs` `FactionChoice` duplicates `Faction` and adds `Random`. The factions merge added five factions to core and the UI but not here, so rooms returned HTTP 400 and wouldn't start. Random also rotated `% 3`. A unit test now round-trips every `Faction::ALL` name through `FactionChoice` and checks Random against the app's `aiFaction` rotation. When you add a faction, run `cargo test -p legatum-server`.

## 2026-09-26 — Phase-1 choices must not change the same turn's battles
City orders apply in phase 1, before ranged combat and movement. Attack forecasts can only see the state the turn started from, so if a phase-1 order changes anything combat reads (city or unit strength), the battle no longer matches its forecast. When you add an order that changes rules, check whether phases 2–5 read what it changes; if they do, apply it after combat or have combat use the pre-turn value.

## 2026-09-26 — Removing a state field keeps old saves loading
`GameState`, `Player` and the view structs don't use `deny_unknown_fields`, so serde ignores a field that no longer exists. Removing Recovery charters left old saves with a `"doctrine"` key; they still load and the key disappears on the next save (`research_tree_is_exposed_and_old_charter_saves_still_load` in `crates/wasm`). Removed order types don't get this grace: old order JSON naming them fails to parse, which is what we want. The three 40-turn determinism tapes came out byte-identical after the removal, because at Standard speed no AI chose a charter within 40 turns. Identical tapes after a rule removal mean the fixtures never exercised that rule, not that nothing changed.

## 2026-09-26 — Vitest only ran `.test.ts`, so `.test.tsx` suites were silently skipped
`app/vite.config.ts` included only `src/**/*.test.ts`. Two component suites (`CityPanel.test.tsx` and `SeatRelease.test.tsx`) had never run and were broken: tooltips portal into `document.body`, not the render container, and happy-dom has no `window.confirm` to spy on, so use `vi.stubGlobal('confirm', …)`. The include pattern is now `src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`. When adding a new test file type, check that the runner actually counts it.

## 2026-09-26 — Sim JSON reports are committed gzipped
Each 1,000-game report JSON is 11–20 MB, and `docs/sim-results` had reached 108 MB. Raw `docs/sim-results/*.json` is now gitignored. Commit the `.md` report and a `gzip -9` copy (`*.json.gz`). The dashboard (`tools/dashboard/server.mjs`) reads either and prefers the plain file when both exist. `*-analysis.json` summaries stay plain.

## 2026-09-27 — AI stalemates came from policy gates, not impossible scores
The rare games stuck at 9 of 10 VP (about 1–2 per 1,000) were AI policy stalemates:
- Army quotas blocked buying a title-flipping unit.
- Campaigns ignored remembered (fogged) cities.
- Scouting stopped after the opening.
- The Relay needed every city threat-free.
- Settlers vetoed legal sites near borders.

Fixing crates/ai alone (`ai-endgame-pursuit`) removed every stall: 0 in 2,000 calibration games and 0 in 1,000 held-out Quick games (seeds 910001+). Founding distance (3) exceeds unit sight (2), so border settlers need reconnaissance to avoid repeated failed foundings. Always validate AI tuning on seeds it wasn't calibrated on.

## 2026-09-27 — The TS mock drifts from core rules; test parity, don't patch cases
`app/src/mock` duplicates the rules for UI development and tests (real games use the WASM core). Its purchases completed instantly in the order phase, while core funds production and completes it during city processing, where a blocked spawn waits. Three consecutive reviews found validation edge cases that came only from that mismatch, and each patch exposed another. The fix is structural: the mock follows core's phase model, and a parity test runs the same scenarios through both engines. When the mock needs a rule, mirror core's model and add a parity case instead of a special-case projection.

## 2026-09-27 — Never append to an Astra task that may have started
The runner moves task files from `.progress/astra-queue/pending/` to `running/` when a worker picks them up. Appending (`cat >>`) to the pending path of a task that already started creates a new, header-less file that the runner would treat as a malformed task, and the running task never sees the addition. Before amending a task, check that it's still in `pending/`. Otherwise queue a follow-up task (or put one in `hold/` until the first merges). This happened twice in one day.

## 2026-09-27 — Tooltips: hover is for reading, click is for breakdowns
The playtest's "tooltips cover things and block clicks" had three causes in `Tip.tsx`: bubbles took the pointer (so a bubble clamped over a neighbour swallowed its click), they opened instantly on any pass of the pointer, and rich breakdowns (five yield tables) opened on hover at full size. Now hover tooltips are `pointer-events: none`, wait 450 ms (instant once one is open), and content containing a breakdown table shows a one-line summary on hover and opens pinned on click (or an ⓘ beside a control, since the control's own click must stay the action). `placeBubble` scores each side by overlap with the trigger's panel, the unit actions, the This Turn panel and the top bar, including "escape" positions just outside the panel. Detecting "rich" walks the React element tree for `BreakdownTable`/`YieldSourceTable`/`YieldsAfter`/`.bd`, so a new breakdown component must be added there or it will open as a big hover bubble again. Content inside a closed rich tooltip is no longer in the DOM, so tests that read it must pin it first.

## 2026-09-27 — `upgrade_cost: null` means "can't now", not "not in territory"
The view's `upgrade_cost` is `check_upgrade(...).ok()`: null for a missing technology, for standing outside your own tile, and for too little Gold alike. The unit panel inferred "Only inside your territory" from null and misled a player with 59 of 60 Gold. The UI now checks each requirement itself in the engine's order (tech, `tile.owner === me`, then `upgrade_breakdown.total` against Gold). Treat any nullable engine convenience field as a summary; derive reasons from the underlying data.

## 2026-09-27 — Docked panels move absolutely positioned children off screen
The unit notes stack is `position: absolute; bottom: calc(100% + 12px)` to float above the bottom command bar. At ≤1280 px and on touch the unit panel is `position: static` inside the left dock, so the stack anchored to the dock and sat above its top edge, invisible, while stale touch rules still targeted the old per-note positioning. When a panel has two layouts, check every absolutely positioned child in both; `e2e/clarity.spec.ts` now asserts the notes are on screen and never intersect at 1280×800 and 1440×900.


## 2026-09-27 — Resolving a conflict by taking one side drops the other side's attributes
Merging the UI-2 branch, I resolved the `Action` button conflict in `UnitPanel.tsx` by taking UI-2's version wholesale. Master's side had added `aria-pressed={active}` for the Auto-explore toggle, so both auto-explore e2e tests broke (caught by the Astra master review, not by vitest). When one side restructures a block, diff each side against the merge base (`git diff :1:file :2:file`, `:1: :3:`) and carry every attribute the other side added, then run the e2e specs that cover both features.

## 2026-09-27 — A hand-maintained progress plan goes stale; derive progress from the living queue
The dashboard showed "0% complete" next to "✓ all done" and a burn-up of the finished v1.0 plan a day later. It read `.progress/plan.json`, which someone had to update by hand; after v1.0 nobody did, and its last history entry was an event row with no `pct`, so `history.at(-1).pct ?? 0` read 0. The real, constantly edited source of truth was `plans/playtest-feedback.md`. The dashboard now parses that queue (`tools/dashboard/release.mjs`; status keyword → weight: done 1, review 0.8, implemented 0.7, in progress 0.4, queued/held 0), `.progress/release.json` only names the release and its start, and the server appends to `.progress/release-history.json` when the numbers move (seeded from git with `--first-parent`; without it, older copies of the file on merged side branches make the curve jump back and forth). Any status display should read the file people already keep current, never a second copy. Queue rows sometimes miss or add a cell (C4 had no Owner, D4 an extra one), so the parser takes the Status column if it parses, else the last cell that does.

## 2026-09-27 — Different thresholds for ending and starting a relationship make AIs oscillate
Diplomacy gave notice on pacts when the partner reached 70% of its victory target but still proposed and accepted pacts below 75%. VP moves in steps of 10% on a 10-VP target, so every team at 7 VP triggered sign → notice → minimum term ends → re-sign, up to about 250 pacts in one game; pact count correlated with game length at r = 0.75, and each cycle's "honored" trust suppressed wars. Any AI rule with a start and stop condition needs one shared threshold plus hysteresis (a lower re-entry bar or a cooldown), and the sim report should flag per-pair repetition counts.

## 2026-09-27 — A long-running Astra merge branch goes stale while it works
`merge-diplomacy` took about 40 minutes; by the time it finished, master was 49 commits ahead (auto-explore, sound, UI fixes), so the verified branch couldn't be merged as is. For integration tasks, tell the worker to merge master again right before finishing and rerun the checks, and review with `git merge-tree` against current master before trusting its results.

## 2026-09-27 — Settle scoring: travel turns and threat reach (from astra settle-lenses)
Turns-to-reach a site must count movement left unused at each turn boundary (a unit with 1 of 2 moves left can't spend a 2-cost tile this turn, so it loses that point), or the forecast undercounts by a turn on rough routes. And an enemy ranged unit's threat is measured from the tile it stands on now, before it moves, the same way combat resolves, not from where it could end up.

## 2026-09-27 — Centered overlays at the top of the map collide
Three features independently put absolutely positioned panels "top, centered" over the map (the first-game hint at 76px, the lens switcher at 62px, the VP track), and the hint silently covered the settle-recommendation buttons on turn 1, the moment they matter most. Give every map overlay a named slot (top bar, top-center hint, bottom-left tools, bottom dock) and test each new overlay with the first-game hint visible on desktop, iPad and phone.

## 2026-09-27 — A remembered route must be re-checked every turn, like a fresh path
Movement-contention made every multi-hex human move a confirmed `MoveUnitPath` and replayed its steps blindly on later turns. Anything that appeared on the route afterwards changed the meaning of the order: an enemy on the path turned the move into an unforecast attack, and a parked friend blocked it forever (MoveUnit repaths around both). A stored route is advice, not an order to enter whatever is there: validate each step with the same avoid rules as the pathfinder and repath when it fails. Also: waiting automation must advance by the unit's actual position, not by a round counter, because contention can hold it in place.

## 2026-09-27 — Compare against current master, not the baseline the branch started from
Movement-contention reported captures going 1,402 → 1,471 → 1,059 over 500 games. The drop wasn't the change: the last two cohorts were built on a master that had since merged AI combat response (scouts flee, garrisons counterattack), which cuts captures. Against current master on the same seeds the change was +22 captures, within noise. Every A/B must build both sides from the same master commit.

## 2026-09-27 — Astra can't run browsers; Claude reviews must
Astra's Codex `workspace-write` sandbox (macOS seatbelt) kills Chromium, WebKit and Firefox before a page opens, so every Astra UI branch (settle-lenses, production-queue-buy, celebrate-ruins) arrives with its Playwright specs written but never run, and the first real run found failures (the lens panel hidden under the first-game hint, a macOS `<select>` keyboard step). Loosening the sandbox to full access isn't worth the risk. Instead, every Astra branch that touches app/ gets a Claude review that runs the full Playwright suite and looks at screenshots before merging.

## 2026-09-27 — Private rewards and reveals leak through side channels (from astra celebrate-ruins)
Three fog leaks the ruin work had to close: (1) a rival who can SEE the finder must not see what the ruin gave (the `RuinExplored` event is team-private, in core `event_visibility.rs` and the mock); (2) a map reveal must write terrain and ruin markers only, never live ownership, cities or units, and the mock city view must use remembered observations (`knownCities`), not live city data on explored-but-unseen tiles; (3) a "research threshold" celebration must use the actual per-turn Science income, not a projected one. ## 2026-09-27 — `RemoteClient.validate()` sends orders to the LAN server
In app/src/remote.ts, `validate()` is also the sync path: it calls `setOrders` → `pushOrders`, so the server's copy of the seat's orders is replaced and the seat is un-readied. Its only callers pass the seat's real order list, so it isn't a live bug, but any preview or "what if" call over LAN would silently overwrite the player's orders. Never call it with hypothetical orders. On the production-queue-buy-2 branch it is split: `syncOrders()` sends, `validate()` only reads cached errors, and the store calls `syncOrders` before validating the seat's real list.

## 2026-09-27 — Endgame stalemates: gold piles up while no one takes the last VP
Long Quick games (555 and 596 turns against a ~150 target) share a pattern: the tech tree ends around turn 280, all eight AIs sit at 5–9 of 10 VP in a war of attrition, and gold goes into endless military purchases (783 in one game) or sits unspent (Celts at 9 VP on 5,033 gold). The AI needs an endgame plan that converts resources into the nearest VP source; buying defenders "whenever threatened" makes it worse.

## 2026-09-27 — First strategic-diversity measurement: Economic has no counter
480 Quick games with six forced scripted strategies (docs/sim-results/strategy-diversity-2026-09-27.md): every strategy wins some games (winner entropy 0.97), but Economic finishes ahead of each other strategy 57–71% of the time, and Rush loses to all five. Natural (unforced) AI play has winner entropy 0.68, below the proposed 0.80 floor. Caveats: scripted policies only (a weak Rush script may understate Rush), 16 seeds per matchup, no diplomacy yet. Note: a 12-turn game has no VP winner, so diversity tests must let games finish.

## 2026-09-27 — A benchmark opponent must first reproduce the result it stands in for
The first human-proxy opponent won only 24% against 7 Hard AIs (18% vs Normal, 40% vs Easy) at Standard, while the human it models beat 7 Hard AIs easily by turn 197. Measuring AI improvements against it would have said "the AI is already competitive" when it isn't. Calibrate a stand-in opponent until it reproduces the real observation (here: ≥70% wins vs Hard) and freeze it with a version number before using it as the yardstick. Also: Proxy vs Normal scored lower than vs Hard, a hint that difficulty tiers don't order monotonically against outside opponents.

## 2026-09-27 — Astra branches can carry committed conflict markers
movement-contention-2 merged cleanly into master yet brought `<<<<<<<` markers inside plans/playtest-feedback.md, committed on the branch by its own master merge. A clean `git merge` doesn't mean clean content. Before merging any branch: `git diff --check master...<branch>` and `git grep -n '^
## 2026-09-27 — Endgame stalls came from AI goal-keeping, and sim artifacts stay out of git
The long Quick games (up to 596 turns) were the AI failing to finish, not a rules gap: routine fighting spent the gold a cash-goal title needed, emergency purchases stopped investment scoring, and no one planned multi-building title routes. Fixing endgame pursuit (astra quick-long-games) cut games over 250 turns from 28 to 13 in 2,000 Quick seeds (max 470 → 308), with no turn limits. Keep the report, summary JSON and small evidence in `docs/sim-results/`; large artifacts (tapes, multi-MB JSON) go to `~/LegatumData/sim-artifacts/<run>/` with a pointer in the report. ## 2026-09-27 — Verify by exit code, never by the tail of the output
I merged the settler threat-memory fix after a verification run whose summary I read with `tail`: the cargo line "scripted_orders_all_validate_and_succeed_in_a_real_game --- FAILED" was above the tail, so a red master went unnoticed until a reviewer hit it. Every verification step must check its exit status (`cmd; echo "exit $?"`, or `set -e`) and grep for `FAILED|error|panicked` over the whole log, and cargo runs use `--no-fail-fast` so one failure doesn't hide others.

## 2026-09-28 — Frozen state snapshots must hash the schema they were archived in
AI regression tests that load an archived `GameState` (campaign_memory.rs, defense_retreat.rs) pin its hash for provenance. Adding a serialized field (the city `production_queue` and `last_purchase_turn`) changes `state.hash()` even though the archive is unchanged, so after a schema change strip the new default-valued fields from the JSON before hashing (`state::fnv1a`) instead of re-pinning a new hash; the counterfactual turns then check current-schema save/load separately.

At master `78d81d1`, `legatum-sim --games 3 --seed 18446744073709551613 --turn-limit 40 --brain mixed` produces different orders from turns 8, 9 and 10 than the committed tapes: later defense-AI changes were refreshed with the order-preserving `standing_orders_tapes` example, which keeps old orders and only rewrites hashes. production-queue-buy-2 caps each AI at 4 or 6 military purchases per game (`Player.military_purchases`, and wars are permanent) and only buys non-military items the city is already building. `npx --prefix app playwright test -c app/playwright.config.ts` from the repo root failed 18 of 72 specs (the title screen never rendered: the config's web server and paths resolve against the working directory). `cd app && npx playwright test` passes 72/72 on the same commit. I stopped the Ops-queued tasks lan-disband-purchase-preview and purchase-tape-decoder as duplicates of production-followups, because I had appended those items to production-followups' task file. ## 2026-09-28 — When Astra hits its usage limit, the work continues on Claude agents
At 02:10 Astra hit its ChatGPT usage limit ("try again at Oct 4"); the limit watcher parked the five running tasks in hold/ with their branches intact. Critical-path tasks moved to Claude agents that continue the same branches from the task files in hold/; the AI-evolution coach uses the Claude CLI headless in read-only mode (`command claude -p ... --allowedTools "Read,Grep,Glob"`) with Astra as an optional provider.
