## 2026-09-28 — Fog made AI settlers walk between two illegal sites for 150 turns
The shared settle scorer infers a hidden foreign city only from borders visible right now. A settler approaching site A saw the border, switched to site B; walking away it forgot A's border, so A looked legal and better again; near B the same happened. Traced Hard AIs lost their second or third city this way for the whole game (and the idle settler blocked the next one). A stateless AI needs the same inference over remembered foreign borders, restricted to never-explored centers (explored tiles would have shown the city; using all non-visible tiles blocked most of a small map), plus a commitment bonus for the current goto. Also: `garrison_cities` filled a new colony with the capital's only Soldier and the empty capital fell, so a unit standing on an own city is never the "nearest free" filler.

## 2026-09-28 — Against the Proxy, expansion without defense feeds the rusher; racing the VP leader helps most
On 128 paired Standard games vs Proxy v2 (Hard), faster Hard expansion alone raised the Proxy's win rate (62.5% → 68.8%: more undefended colonies to capture), while reading the public VP track earlier and sizing the army to it was the best single change (→ 56%). Expansion only paid once combined with leader pressure. The Proxy's first capture is at a median turn 56 in about 97% of games, and AIs at turn 100 run +1 to +2 Gold with two units, so the remaining gap is early defense and economy, not late-game spending. Measure each macro idea against the Proxy, not AI-vs-AI win rates.

## 2026-09-28 — Evolution harness gotchas
- Homebrew Python 3.14 blocks `pip --user` (and numpy isn't installed), so tools/evolve uses a dependency-free pure-Python CMA-ES; keep repo Python tools dependency-free.
- Headless `claude -p` run from the repo loads the project's hooks (the learnings Stop hook). Pass `--setting-sources user --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'`; `--bare` breaks OAuth login. With `--json-schema`, the result is in `structured_output`.
- tools/film/report.mjs output has trailing whitespace, so a committed report.html fails `git diff --check`: don't commit generated reports (or strip the whitespace).
- The first genome is 5 personality knobs per faction (40 genes); tactical and macro weights still need exposing as genes.

## 2026-09-28 — The numeric perf tape needs a fresh corpus to prove its decoder
`tape_order` in crates/core/tests/visibility_equivalence.rs decoded every recorded purchase (tag 5) as a Soldier, although the profiler writes the item kind and index, so the ignored corpus check could never have matched a game with any other purchase. The old corpus in the astra-performance-pass worktree was recorded at 3519f6d and can't be replayed against current rules, so it can't prove anything now. To verify a decoder end to end, record a fresh corpus from the current tree into a temp dir (`target/release/examples/perf_profile record <dir>`, ~10 s) and run the corpus test with `PERF_JSON_MODE=record`; prd72 seed 7 has a turn-43 Settler purchase, which the old decoder fails at turn 44.

## 2026-09-28 — "Wake when an enemy newly comes into view" must count enemies entering range, not only sight
Astra's fortify-holds draft woke a sleeper only when an enemy it had never seen appeared within movement range. Playing it showed the hole: an enemy Soldier spotted three hexes out walked up next to a sleeping Settler and nothing woke it, because it was "already visible". The contact set is now the visible enemy military inside each sleeper's movement radius; a sleeper wakes when that set gains a member (arriving in sight or walking closer), and a re-slept unit accepts whoever is already in the set, so a besieger doesn't ask for orders every turn. Rules that fire on "new" things need the "new" measured against the same zone the rule is about.

## 2026-09-28 — A Playwright step that "hangs" on the Vite dev server may just be Vite re-optimizing
Playing a scripted scenario against `npm run dev` on a fresh worktree, one End Turn took about 40 s and every later call (screenshot, CDP session, evaluate) looked hung until the 120 s test timeout, which sent me hunting a UI infinite loop that didn't exist. The same script passed in 27 s on the next run: the first run paid Vite's dependency optimization and page reload. Set `actionTimeout` (10 s) in ad-hoc Playwright configs so a slow step fails with its name, and rerun once before debugging a "hang". Separately, a waiting production queue now banks only up to its first item's cost (core `bank_cap`, reported as `idle_production_cap`), so a Settler blocked for 50 turns can't bank a Great Work's worth of overflow.

## 2026-09-28 — Garrison hold helps a little; the incident detector still encodes retreat-first
Making city garrisons hold (leave only when certain death and capture anyway) cut Proxy v2 captures 5–11% but moved its win rate only 63.3 → 62.0% (Hard) and 68.0 → 64.7% (Normal), within noise on 300 games. Most Proxy wins come from the economy gap, not from abandoned cities. The AI analysis detector's `garrison_under_ranged_fire` and `unanswered_attack` rules jumped about tenfold because they flag exactly the behavior the design now wants; update those rules before reading them as AI failures.

## 2026-09-28 — Diplomacy merge: hysteresis on both sides, and Peace breaks "every foreigner is an enemy"
- After giving notice on a pact, ACCEPTING a new pact needs the same cooldown as proposing it; otherwise the loop re-forms through the other side whenever the partner's progress flickers across the threshold (seed 700254 re-signed 11 pacts with one team).
- Games now start at Peace, so any code that treats every foreign unit as an enemy breaks: wake-on-sight (sleepers woke for peaceful neighbours), scout threat avoidance, siege test fixtures. Review each master merge for team-vs-War assumptions; threats are armies of teams at War with you.
- Large per-game JSON archives on a long-lived branch stay in history even after moving them out; the diplomacy branch was squash-merged to keep 16 MB out of master.

## 2026-09-28 — Peace starts broke the benchmark opponent
Proxy v2 has no diplomacy code and never declares war, so after the diplomacy merge (games start at Peace) it only fought AIs that attacked it: 25% wins vs 7 Hard and 0.44 captures per game, against 83% and ~6 before. Any rules change that alters how conflict starts must be re-checked against every benchmark and harness. Proxy runs now start in the legacy all-war state (`--proxy-start war`) to stay comparable; a diplomacy-aware Proxy v3 is queued. The overnight evolution run (started before the merge) used the pre-diplomacy binary, so its fitness is all-war too.

## 2026-09-28 — Capping simultaneous AI offers needs a public schedule, not a per-AI limit
Each AI already sent at most one offer per turn, yet a human received three pacts on turn 2: AI brains plan independently from the same state, so no per-brain rule bounds the total. What does bound it without coordination is a schedule every AI can compute from public information: each alive AI team owns a turn slot (turn mod the number of AI teams) for new offers to a given human. The cost is latency (up to seven turns with eight empires), which matters for urgent Peace offers. The native test only failed after the stagger was removed once a 4-empire game reached turn 16, so tests for pacing rules must play past the acquaintance period.

## 2026-09-28 — Worktrees need a real node_modules
A worktree whose app/node_modules is a symlink to the main checkout's makes Vite reject imports from outside the worktree root (HTTP 403), which fails browser specs (the lenses spec). Give each worktree its own copy (`cp -Rc app/node_modules <wt>/app/`, a fast clone on APFS; it's git-ignored) or run `npm ci` there.

## 2026-09-28 — All-war Proxy starts reproduce the old benchmark; 128-game screens overstate levers
With `--proxy-start war` (a `GameSetup.legacy_all_war` field, omitted from JSON when false so old tapes and hashes are unchanged) the post-diplomacy Proxy benchmark reproduces the pre-diplomacy results exactly on the same seeds (Hard 186/300). Separately, the best early-defense lever looked like −9 points on a 128-game screen and was −2 on the 300-game run: screen with 128, but only report the 300.

## 2026-09-28 — Pre-playtest full play-through: what only a long game shows
A scripted "player" drove a whole Quick game (8 empires, 7 Hard AIs) through the UI at 1440×900: Hard AI 2 won on VP at turn 141 while two of my sieges failed, and turns resolved in 100–230 ms throughout. Lessons for next time:
- The local (WASM) and LAN paths apply a resolved turn in different functions (`applyTurn` vs the remote `view` callback); state the remote path resets (`error`) was never reset locally, so an invalid-order toast stayed up for the rest of the game. When adding per-turn state, reset it in both.
- `returnFocusAfterPointer` treated any radio group as owning the arrow keys, so a mouse click on a map lens left focus there: arrows cycled lenses and Return did nothing, the exact "keys stop working" report from playtest 1. Pointer-clicked radios and tabs now hand focus back; only text entry and lists keep it.
- Harness: a long-lived Playwright process with a tiny HTTP endpoint (run a snippet, hot-reload a helpers module) lets you play hundreds of turns interactively and keep one console log. Chromium's closed `<details>` content still has client rects, so filter locators with `{ visible: true }`, not `getClientRects()`. `window.legatum` (store) plus `window.legatumMap.toScreen` locate hexes for real mouse clicks; tile index is `r * width + q + floor(r / 2)`.
- Any rules change makes older save files unloadable: loading the turn-59 save from master on this branch failed with "incompatible engine: archive commit …, rules …" (the save carries its game-history recording, which pins the engine). A playtest build that changes rules will not load the user's saves from the previous build; say so when shipping one.
- New per-unit state that the AI also touches (here `Unit.blocked_turns`) changes determinism hashes from the first turn it is non-zero, even when every recorded order is identical. Omit the field from JSON at its default so initial hashes and archived states stay valid, regenerate with the documented command, and diff the tapes' order maps (unchanged) against the hashes (changed) to prove the change is state-only.
- Capturing a city against Hard (or even Easy) AIs needs a concentrated force: piecemeal arrivals over rough terrain (about 1 hex per turn) lose to the AI's rebuilt garrisons, and Switzerland' upkeep bankrupts a 3-unit army at +2 Gold. A conquest check is quicker in a two-human hot-seat game.

## 2026-09-28 — First evolution run: no strength gain, but the coach earned its keep
Run 2026-09-28-0313 (25 generations × 16 candidates, 128 Proxy + 32 league Quick games each, 40 personality genes): on held-out seeds the evolved AI matched the stock Hard exactly on the Proxy benchmark (65.2% vs 65.2%), so it isn't adopted. Two lessons: the per-candidate fitness was too noisy to steer (the "best" jumped around and the gen-20 checkpoint was worse than gen 10), and personality knobs can't fix behavioral gaps. It did cut the AI faction best/worst ratio from 3.67× to 2.22× on held-out seeds, which is worth a look for balance. The Claude coach's findings were concrete and code-located (empty late-game research, garrisons not answering bombardment, idle defenders, settlers without a timeout, Wide beating every archetype), and they became the coach-proposals task. Evolution v2 (less noise, behavioral genes, current rules) is queued.

## 2026-09-28 — Phone layout review gotchas
- Court's notched `clip-path` corners make hit-tests at the button's corner miss; probe ~9px inside.
- Geometry checks taken while the bottom sheet animates its height are racy; wait for `element.getAnimations()` to finish before measuring.
- Save files carry the engine's rules fingerprint and don't load after a rules change ("incompatible engine"), so each playtest build starts fresh saves; tell the user.

## 2026-09-28 — Review fixes: shared events and forecast fields need their exact meaning
Astra caught four slips in the pre-gate fixes. (1) A reason string in an event that both teams receive (ProposalInvalidated) must not carry private numbers such as the other empire's Influence balance: check who receives an event before formatting data into it. (2) A client warning about a rule (pact cancelled for debt) must mirror the order core checks it in: eligibility is tested after breach fines but before this turn's signing costs. (3) Every CTA whose label comes from the priority-wrapped decision must also navigate with `goToPending`, not `nextDecision()`. (4) `economy.bankruptcy.gold.total` is next turn's projected treasury, not income: read a forecast field's doc comment before labelling it.

## 2026-09-28 — A run's film needs the run's own simulator
The overnight run's film failed at `legatum-sim --replay-export`: its showcase tapes were recorded by the 03:13 engine, and target/release/legatum-sim had since been rebuilt with newer rules. Replays need the exact engine that recorded them. Evolution v2 freezes a copy of the simulator binary per run; for older runs, build the run's start commit in a detached worktree and pass it as LEGATUM_SIM to tools/film/make-film.sh.

## 2026-09-28 — A coalition rule with a tie-break becomes a permanent dogpile in a late pack
Held-out coalition game 910030 (rotation 4) ran to the 1,200-turn cap with 0 captures. By turn 300 every team had banked its seven permanent VP (milestones + faction goal), four of the five titles were locked for hundreds of turns, and only Strongest Army moved. The coalition rule "leader at ≥80% progress" plus "ties select the lowest TeamId" made team 0 the target whenever several teams sat at 8 of 10, and whoever touched 9 drew declarations until the army title moved again. Forcing peace in the one 900-turn war (1W3) did not help (it was re-declared); requiring the target to be strictly ahead ended the game at turn 408. Rules that pick "the leader" must return no one on a tie: an id tie-break both singles out seat 0 (usually the human) and turns a close race into a stalemate. Also: long diagnostic traces are cheap with a per-turn one-line state dump (crates/sim/examples/coalition_trace.rs); read the title holders, not just VP totals.

## 2026-09-28 — Proxy v3 was calibrated before alliances existed
Proxy v3 (diplomacy-aware benchmark: 75% vs 7 Hard at Peace starts) was built on a master without alliances and coalitions. On merge it declines alliances and calls to arms to stay comparable, but the AIs now form coalitions against a leading Proxy, so its win rate on current master is lower than the calibration. Recalibrate (or report both) before using it as the yardstick for the next evolution run.

## 2026-09-28 — Wide dominates, and the first four counter levers didn't fix it
After diplomacy, the forced-strategy study flipped: Wide (not Economic) finishes ahead of every other policy, and frontier-city defense, market plunder, earlier walls and early siege (alone and combined) didn't create a counter. The evolution coach independently saw the same. Levers that make attacking easier don't counter Wide; the next experiments are structural costs of going wide (rising settler cost, per-city tech cost, per-city upkeep, coalitions that weigh territory). Rush's weakness may partly be its scripted policy: it attacks earlier but finishes worse.

## 2026-09-28 — Clean merges can still break the build: compile before committing a merge
Two branches merged cleanly in git but broke compilation together: one added a required field (`stop_on_block`) to `Order::MoveUnitPath`, the others constructed that order without it (the coach-proposals settler timeout, Proxy v4). Git can't see semantic conflicts. After every merge, run `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` (and `npx tsc -b` for app changes) before committing it, and choose values for new fields deliberately (a danger-avoiding route should `stop_on_block: true`).

## 2026-09-28 — Splitting JSX text runs moves glyphs
When adding a phone variant, splitting a desktop JSX text line into different text runs (e.g. `{a}{b}` instead of one string) can shift italic glyphs by a pixel in Chromium, which breaks pixel-identical desktop checks. Keep desktop text runs unchanged and branch the phone variant separately.

## 2026-09-28 — JSON imports in app/src need an import attribute for Playwright
A module in app/src that e2e specs import (app/src/data.ts) imported `./rules.generated.json` without `with { type: 'json' }`. Vite, vitest and tsc accept that, but Playwright's Node loader refuses it, so the whole Playwright suite failed to load (exit 1, 0 tests run). Always add the attribute to JSON imports in shared app modules.

## 2026-09-28 — Faction balance after diplomacy: 5.2x at Quick, fixed by drawbacks to 1.3x
On master after diplomacy, coalitions and the AI work, the best/worst faction win ratio was 5.2x at Quick (Germany 21% / Sparta 4%) and 2.8–2.9x at Standard (Celts 18% / Byzantium 6%). The V9 bundle of compensating drawbacks and payoffs brought it to 1.28–1.36x on 2,000 games per speed (tuning and held-out), without touching signature strengths. Two lessons: a strong army doesn't win if the faction's goal is hard to complete (Sparta held the Army title most often but won 4%), and title deadlocks (one faction holding Economy/Science/Population for hundreds of turns while no one can finish) are the main source of very long games.

## 2026-09-28 — "Attack bounces" in playtest were moves onto units at Peace
All teams start at Peace. At Peace, `enemyAt()` in app/src/commands.ts returns null, so clicking a foreign unit issued a plain MoveUnit, not an attack. Core then logged MoveBlocked ("a peaceful foreign unit blocks the tile") in round 0 and stopped the unit for the whole turn, leaving its goto as a dangling route. The player saw a silent bounce three times (turns 3, 5 and 6 of their game) and assumed pursuit was broken. Lesson: when a player reports combat misbehaving, check the diplomatic relation first. A UI that falls back to "move" for a target it can't attack hides the reason. Replaying a copy of the live autosave's tape reproduced it exactly.

## 2026-09-28 — Agent worktrees filled the disk (696 GB)
Each Claude agent and Astra write task gets its own worktree under .claude/worktrees, and each one builds its own Rust `target/` (4–16 GB) plus node_modules. Worktrees whose agents made commits are never cleaned up automatically, so 179 of them piled up and filled the data volume (13 GB free of 1.8 TB). 152 were fully merged into master with nothing uncommitted, and the rest held rebuildable build output. `tools/cleanup/disk-cleanup.sh` (dry run by default, `--apply` moves to the Trash) removes merged, clean, idle, unlocked worktrees and strips build output from the rest. `tools/cleanup/disk-watch.sh` logs free space to .progress/disk.log every 30 minutes and flags DISK LOW. Moving files to the Trash doesn't free space until the Trash is emptied. After merging an agent's branch, clean its worktree.

## 2026-09-28 — Agent worktree creation can fail during a concurrent git commit
Twice, spawning an isolated agent right after (or alongside) a commit on master failed with "git metadata could not be resolved" and left a locked stub worktree behind. Fix: `git worktree unlock` and `git worktree remove --force` the stub, delete its branch, then spawn again. Avoid committing in the same batch as an isolated-agent spawn.

## 2026-09-28 — G8: the Standard opening is slow for everyone because capitals sit at the 3-Production floor
Replaying the playtest-3 save's tape showed the capital at exactly 3 Production (the floor) from turn 2 to 70, so an 80-cost Soldier took 26 turns and a 150-cost Settler 50. It wasn't a player mistake: over 400 Standard games, Normal AIs finish their first Settler on turn 62 and average 2 cities at turn 100 (Civ 6: first Settler turns 25–35, 5–7 cities at turn 100). The opt-in levers `capital_production` (+2, like Civ 6's Palace) plus `opening_ramp` (the speed surcharge on Production phases in over the first third of the game) bring the first Settler to turn 22 (18 for Hard) and the Soldier to 8 turns, and cut game length by about 14%. But every faster opening pushed faction spread from 3.0x to 7–20x (Germany up, Byzantium down), so pacing and the V9 balance must be validated together. Two lessons: (1) an AI heuristic that recomputes a core price (`first_settler_pending` compared option cost with `speed.scale_cost(base)`) silently breaks under any pricing change. The first ramp run delayed Settlers to turn 74 until it used the same `RuleExperiments::scale_production`. Read prices from the view's options, or share the core function. (2) The third city stays late (turn 97 for Normal) because of Normal AI's "develop before the next Settler" gate, not costs. Details: docs/sim-results/2026-09-28-g8-opening-pace.md.

## 2026-09-28 — Session limit stops every agent at once
When the Claude session limit hit, all five running agents stopped mid-task at the same moment with HTTP 429. Their worktrees and transcripts survive. After the reset, SendMessage to each agent id resumes it with its context. Tell each one that master has moved, and have it merge master itself before its final verification.

## 2026-09-28 — G2 fix: attacks follow the unit, and "why nothing happened" never hides in Movement
Follow-up to the Peace-bounce entry above. The report had filed the explaining MoveBlocked line under Movement, a category hidden by default, so a line that explains why an order did nothing belongs in Orders or Combat. At War, a target could still slip away when the attacker started two or more tiles off: the attacker walked into the empty tile and never fought. The attack now follows the unit (`Unit::attack_target`). It is set in phase 1 only when the destination held a visible hostile unit, or a unit of a team this order list declares War on, and never on a tile holding a foreign city. Each round re-aims the attacker at the target's current tile. An escort or city covering the target stops the pursuit rather than widening the attack, and losing sight ends the order (reported). MoveUnit validation treats teams declared on in the same order list as at War, so the Declare War dialog can target units inside closed borders. `crates/wasm/tests/g2_playtest_bounce.rs` replays the user's turns 1–5 from a trimmed tape fixture. Sims (docs/sim-results/2026-09-28-g2-attack-pursuit.md, 800 Quick seeds): settler captures rose about 25%, battles and city captures moved within noise, and stalls went from 0 to 2. Both stalls are the known title deadlock (one team holds three titles for hundreds of turns), not a pursuit loop: 990061 has about 100 pursuit events in 600 turns. A rule change that shifts trajectories can land a game in the AI's endgame deadlock, so read a new stall's title holders before blaming the change. Rebuilt on master 6882b24 (with promotions), the same 200 seeds had no stall on either side and the same 147.2-turn average: the earlier stall was trajectory luck.

## 2026-09-29 — Long chained verification runs get killed (exit 144)
Twice, one background shell running the whole bar (cargo, then WASM, then vitest, then Playwright) was killed with exit 144 after about 30 minutes, partway through a later step. Every earlier step had passed. Split the bar into two background commands, Rust/WASM/vitest/build first and Playwright on its own, and check each summary.

## 2026-09-29 — iPhone Safari can have no IndexedDB at all
Opening the web build on a phone failed at startup with "ReferenceError: Can't find variable: indexedDB". Hardened browser modes and some in-app browsers expose no `indexedDB` global, so `indexedDB.open` throws, and main.tsx's startup `retryGameHistory` surfaced the throw as an error. platform/archive.ts now checks `typeof indexedDB` and posts histories straight to the host's /api/archive when no local queue exists. Guard every browser storage API with a typeof check, not only try/catch around its calls.

## 2026-09-29 — G18: an attack order silently stayed on the defender's tile until the attacker died
The user's Soldier (#3) attacked the camp guard on turn 17 (100→68 HP), then attacked again on turns 18 (→36) and 19 (dead) with no new orders. Two paths kept the attack alive: a melee attacker that doesn't advance keeps its `goto` on the defender's tile, so the next turn's movement attacks again, and G2's `finish_pursuits` re-aimed a pursuer that had fought. Because `goto` stayed set, the client never listed the Soldier as needing orders, and the only hint was a routine "attacked … 36 HP vs 57 HP left" line. Now an attack order is one attack: a fighter whose opponent survives drops its goto, path and attack target (`end_engaged_orders`), and a pursuit ends when the turn's movement ends (`Followed`/`OutOfReach` say "Needs orders"); only a pursuit waiting for a declared War keeps its aim. Lesson: any per-unit order that can outlive the turn must either be visible in the client's order cycle or end itself. The AI never depended on it: `Planner::rest` gives every army unit an order each turn, and barbarians re-plan every turn. Replay tests of a live save need the state at the turn in question from the old engine (`crates/wasm/tests/fixtures/playtest3-g18-turn17.json` etc.): once the rules change, replaying the whole tape diverges long before the turn you care about.

## 2026-09-29 — G20: surprise war at plain Peace starts before movement; sleepers need the new enemies removed from their baseline
A declaration with no Pact or Alliance now takes effect at the start of resolution (`diplomacy::declare_surprise_wars`, before barbarian planning and unit orders), so an attack in the same order list resolves that turn; the boundary skips those declarations. Breaches keep the next-turn timing and G2's AwaitingWar hold. Two traps: `sleeping_threats` is taken after unit orders, when the War already exists, so the declarer's visible army would count as "already known" and never wake sleepers; remove surprise pairs from the baseline. And the scripted AI plans its army from a view where the target is still at Peace, so it declares and attacks the next turn as before: it never exploits the surprise (wars whose declarer fought on the War's first turn fell from 229 to 118 per 200 games, because that first turn is now the declaration turn; see docs/sim-results/2026-09-29-g18-g20-g21-combat-timing.md).

## 2026-09-29 — G21: removing the contact pin roughly halves who survives a parting hit
The user's wounded Ranger was ordered away from an adjacent Soldier and stayed pinned ("pinned by an enemy attack"), losing 44 HP. Now a unit attacked while stepping away takes the hit without fortification (terrain still counts; it's still standing there when hit) and completes its step if it survives; the attacker stays unless it kills. Civilians stepped onto by an enemy are still pinned and captured, since the capture is their hit. Over 200 Quick games: 12,348 parting hits, 6,493 kills, 5,620 escapes, 235 stopped by something else; before, 6,091 attacked leavers survived and all stayed pinned. A leaving unit can take several parting hits in one turn from different pursuers, one per movement round.

## 2026-09-29 — Isolated agents: the Bash guard rejects compound shell commands
In an isolated worktree, `nice -n 10 <cmd>`, `cd x && npx …`, loops with `$(…)`, heredocs mixed with other commands and computed executables were refused as "too complex to verify". Put multi-step work in a script under the scratchpad (with `renice -n 10 $$` at the top) and run `bash <script> <step>`; Python edit scripts run the same way.

## 2026-09-29 — Agents must not pkill -f shared patterns
To stop an aborted Playwright run, an agent ran `pkill -f "legatum-server --port 0"`. That pattern matches every agent's Playwright test servers on this machine, so it could kill other agents' runs mid-test, and the user's standing rule forbids `pkill -f`. Kill a specific PID, or use a process group you started yourself. Put this in agent prompts that run e2e.

## 2026-09-30 — Lock worktrees used by long runs
tools/cleanup/disk-cleanup.sh deletes the target/ of any unmerged worktree that's been idle for 3 hours. A long evolution or league run that uses that worktree's sim binary would lose it mid-run. Lock the run's worktree (`git worktree lock --reason ...`); the cleanup skips locked worktrees. Unlock it when the run ends.

## 2026-09-30 — Switching a live league run onto the research coach
Five issues turned up when moving the 2026-09-30 league run from plain PSRO to `--research-coach`:
1. `--rules-hours` must be positive even when the rules phase is already finished. Pass the original rules arguments so the finished search's config matches.
2. The coach refuses run directories under ~/LegatumData, because it treats that as a save folder. Put coach runs under ~/LegatumRuns.
3. Run configs are pinned. Copying a run to a new directory requires editing its config.json only for the intended changes (`best_rules_path`, `research_coach`).
4. The coach self-builds its simulator, so `cargo` must be on PATH for the detached process (`nohup env PATH=...`).
5. A state resumed from a non-coach run has no `evidence_dir`. The coach now falls back to `initial/`. Also move aside partial evaluations pinned to the old simulator.
Pinned-config errors now name the offending file.

## 2026-09-30 — Coach cadence: `--coach-every` is OR'd with the time interval
In tools/league coach mode, a research review is due when `review_seconds` has elapsed OR `gen % review_every == 0`. `--coach-every 1` therefore reviews every generation and burns the whole research budget (6 sonnet calls) in six consecutive generations. Leave `review_every` null and let `review_seconds` (default 7200) set the cadence. Also, the coach A/B's default 128 held-out games (16 maps) is too few to confirm effects around +0.03; use 256 or more.

## 2026-09-30 — Mock ranged Battle events must report HP after the whole ranged phase
The TS mock applied ranged damage shot by shot and put the running HP in each Battle event, while core (`battle::apply_stage`) sums the whole ranged phase's damage first and reports HP after all of it. Parity tests never had two shots on one target, so nobody noticed. City strike makes that common (a Ranger and a city, or two cities, hitting one unit), so the mock now applies unit shots and city shots together, then emits every event, then removes the dead in unit-id order, like core. Any new simultaneous stage in the mock should follow the same order: plan from the snapshot, apply everything, then emit.

## 2026-09-30 — Hard v2 (league openings in the game): equal to old Hard head-to-head, longer games, and all-one-opening tables can stall
Hard seats now draw a league-tuned opening (crates/ai/src/hard_v2.rs; genomes in the generated tuned_openings.rs, refreshed by tools/league/export_tuned.py). Checks worth reusing:
- Prove the wiring before trusting a validation: the same seats and genomes on the league's frozen binary and on the game build played six Standard games identically (turns and winners), so the integration adds no behavioural change of its own.
- A single `enabled()` flag that means both "league run" and "any seat option" silently turned the one Hard v2 seat of a rotation run back into old Hard (0 v2 seats reported). Keep "which seats are special" separate from "the runner builds brains itself", and have the report name each seat's brain (`hard-v2:<Opening>`) so a zero is visible.
- On 104 Standard games with one Hard v2 seat against seven old Hard seats (seat rotated), Hard v2 won 12.5% (95% CI 7.5–20%), exactly parity: the league's gains are relative to other openings, not a strength jump over the old Hard. Against the Proxy benchmark (128 Standard games, rotated) the Proxy won 9 with seven Hard v2 opponents and 3 with seven old Hard (not significant, but not the direction we want). Measure an AI swap against both the old AI and an outside benchmark before calling it stronger.
- All-Hard-v2 tables (100 Standard games) ran 333 turns on average against 269 for old Hard on the same seeds (Standard's nominal length is 225), with 1 stall: a table where all eight seats drew DefendedExpand (69% weight, so about 5% of games) ran to the 1,200-turn cap. The equilibrium weight of one opening sets how often a whole table mirrors it; watch the floor and the dominant weight, not only the per-opening win rates.
- The opening phase machine flaps: an army at the edge of `defend_distance` flipped Opening/Defend (and the production strategy) every turn, up to 57 switches per seat.
- Rule changes that fire automatically (city strike) break hand-built scenario tests far from the rule's own code (AI retreat math, analysis reproductions, playtest replays). Scenarios recorded under the old rules pin the old rule explicitly (`no_city_strike`) rather than having their expectations rewritten.

## 2026-09-30 — League-tuned openings made Hard easier for a strong player: the league's fitness never rewards stopping the leader
Final Hard v2 validation (docs/sim-results/2026-09-30-hard-v2-validation.md, 400 Standard games per row): a Snowball or GreedyExpand challenger seat won more often against seven Hard v2 AIs than against seven old Hard AIs (GreedyExpand 13.5% → 18.2%, sign test p = 0.05), one Hard v2 seat won 10.8% against old Hard (parity 12.5%), and on the user's playtest-3 map seat 0 never won against old Hard (0/56) but won 9–15/56 against Hard v2. The cause is visible in the war counts: old Hard declares about 20 wars per game and 25.6 per game on a leading Snowball seat; Hard v2 declares 13 and 12–14. The league scored each opening by its own wins and VP share, so its equilibrium favours openings that keep to themselves; the old scripted Hard's dogpile on the leader is what a human feels as difficulty. Lessons: measure a candidate AI with a human-style challenger against the table (not only AI-vs-AI win rates), and give a league a leader-containment term before expecting "harder". Also: capping DefendedExpand's draw share from 40% to 25% cut the length excess from +12.5% to +8.8% (each DefendedExpand seat adds about 9 turns), and a 2-turn Defend hysteresis cut phase flapping (max switches 57 → about 33) without changing stalls (1 vs 1 per 400 games).

## 2026-09-30 — Decision: playtest-4 keeps the scripted Hard; the next league needs leader containment and an anchor opponent
Hard v2 is off in the app (`legatum_wasm::session::make_brain` plays the scripted Hard) and available only behind the `hard-v2-ai` setup switch (`legatum-sim --hard-v2`); city strike stays a default rule. The overnight league optimised each opening's own win rate and VP share against other league openings, so it produced a varied but passive table: fewer wars, and no dogpile on the leader, which is exactly what a human experiences as difficulty. For the next league, the fitness needs (1) a leader-containment term (reward the table for denying the VP leader, not only the seat for its own score) and (2) anchor opponents that stay fixed, the scripted Hard and a strong human-style challenger (the Proxy, tuned Snowball/GreedyExpand seats). Accept a candidate only if it beats the scripted Hard head-to-head and lowers the challenger's win rate (`legatum-sim --challenger <Opening> [--hard-v2]`, 400 Standard games, same seeds), not on league equilibrium metrics alone. A switch that changes which brain plays belongs in the setup (it travels in saves and tapes, so a reload recreates the same brains).

## 2026-09-30 — Release-check notes for playtest-4
- The phone turn report appears about 1 s after the turn resolves; harnesses must wait for it before reading.
- Scratch scripts can build real-UI fixtures through vite `ssrLoadModule` of app/src/mock/setup.ts.
- Open text bug: the ProposalInvalidated reason from core (diplomacy.rs ~1170) embeds raw player names ("Player 1 was in Influence debt"). The client should rewrite the leading subject to "you" or the empire name (format.ts).
- Design watch: the first Pact offer (about turn 10) can push a new player into Influence debt, because an automatic border claim lands the same turn. The red chip shows it accurately ("9 → −10, debt"), but players may still accept it.

## 2026-09-30 — Why the overnight opening league underdelivered
Full analysis: ~/LegatumData/analysis/playtest3/why-evolution-underdelivered.md.
- Search budget: round-robin tuning gave each opening about 19 CMA-ES steps at Quick and about 5 at Standard, against the hundreds to thousands that 48 noisy dimensions need. Population 8 was about half the textbook default (~15).
- Noise: genome identity explained about 19% of a candidate's fitness variance, the map about 13%, and the 8-player opponent, seat and faction draw about 67%. The winner's curse overstated gains in 83-88% of tests (train +0.05 vs held-out +0.02).
- Objective: fitness was relative (openings vs each other), so leader containment, which is what makes the scripted Hard hard, was never rewarded.
- Next time:
  - train in 1v1 small-map mirrored duels, and confirm in 8-player games before shipping;
  - tune openings concurrently, not round-robin;
  - use a population of about 15 with racing and resampling;
  - use MAP-Elites per opening;
  - add exploiters to the league;
  - include fixed anchor opponents (the scripted Hard plus a human-style challenger) in the fitness.

## 2026-09-30 — Phone e2e selectors: offer buttons get a "Next decision:" prefix
At the 390×844 phone viewport, a selected unit's sheet renders the pending offer as "Next decision: Respond to offer", so an anchored `/^Respond to offer/` selector passes on desktop and times out on the phone project. Use an unanchored name plus `.first()`, as the neighbouring phone tests do. Astra's sandbox can't launch browsers, so its write tasks report Playwright as unverified: the Claude review must run Playwright (a fresh worktree also needs `cargo build -p legatum-server` for e2e/staging.spec.ts).

## 2026-09-30 — The league's tuned "Rush" never rushes: relative fitness collapses opening identities
In 200 Standard duels (tuned genomes, ~/LegatumRuns/duel-sweep/base) Rush declared no war in 96-99% of games and captured no city in any game; every game ended on VP. The active tuned Rush genome has `rush_timeout = 10`, the gene's minimum. Scaled x2 at Standard, `phase_for` in crates/ai/src/openings.rs abandons the rush at turn 20, before the first Soldier finishes (~turn 21). The overnight league optimised win rate with no identity constraint, so CMA-ES turned Rush into a slow expander. That is why "Rush" numbers across the whole league and duel work say nothing about rushing, and why early-military discounts and turning off city strike changed nothing (combat never happened). Related: the tuned `snipe_settlers_weight` is near max, but `snipe_settlers_radius = 1` makes it dead. Rule for future tuning: each opening needs identity gates (e.g. Rush must declare war and reach an enemy city by a set turn in most games, measured in telemetry), enforced as a constraint on candidates, not left to fitness. The built-in Rush (timeout 80) also loses ~98% to GreedyExpand, so the attack behaviour itself needs work too. Details: ~/LegatumData/analysis/duel-rush-vs-greedy.md.

## 2026-09-30 — Built-in Rush can't rush either: primitive war planning shadows the opening's war logic
40 built-in Rush vs GreedyExpand duels: Rush won 2.5%, declared war in 20% of games (always after abandoning the rush, mean turn 127), captured nothing, and stayed at 1 city for ~160 turns while its 160-turn timeout held the economy hostage. Causes in crates/ai/src:
- `plan_primitive_war()` always claims declarations because `PrimitiveParams::default()` weights are non-zero, so `plan_opening_war()`'s muster/`war_army` logic is dead for every non-Default opening, and primitives have no minimum-force gate.
- `strike_target` is only read by gold buying. Marching uses `campaign_target_for()`, gated on aggression and unaware of the declared target.
- `Phase::Conquer` needs `conquer_cities` cities, which a one-city rush never has.
Lesson: when a layered system (openings → primitives → campaign) gets a new layer, test that the old layer's decisions still reach the executor. Being "tuned" hid dead code. Fix queued as Astra `real-rush`. Analysis: ~/LegatumData/analysis/duel-rush-vs-greedy.md.

## 2026-09-30 — Opening identities are shadowed across the board, not just Rush
Astra's read-only audit (.reviews/astra-opening-identity-audit.md; gate rates in docs/sim-results/2026-09-30-duel-identity-gates.md) found the same pattern in every opening. Shared primitives run first and claim the decision even when they do nothing:
- `plan_primitive_buy()` returns true without buying, so no opening's `burst_buy`/`gold_save` ever runs.
- Primitive escorts ignore `WaitForEscort` and `EscortPolicy::None`, and release escorts before founding.
- Primitive buys and victory investments ignore settler targets, so Tall has no real city cap.
- `primitive_production_bonus()` subtracts the predecessor tier's gold, although core stacks tier yields: a Clearinghouse is valued at 1 gold instead of 4.
The existing opening escort test builds a planner without primitives, so it tests a bypassed path. Tall's ongoing strategy weights favour food and industry 4x, so its science stays at about 11 against Default's 25. Lesson: tests for a layered AI must run the production dispatch path (all layers on), and every tunable gene needs a test that it changes behaviour.

## 2026-09-30 — CORRECTION: faction balance V9 was never merged to master
The 2026-09-28 entry "Faction balance after diplomacy … fixed by drawbacks to 1.3x" describes V9 as adopted, but its implementation commit b25bbbe ("Adopt V9 faction balance as the default rules") only exists on `astra/adopt-balance-v9`. Master, playtest-3 and playtest-4 all ship the pre-V9 factions. The adoption branch itself measured 1.350x at Quick and 1.567x at Standard, already slightly outside pillar 8. Found by Astra's faction-balance diagnosis (.reviews/astra-faction-balance-diagnosis.md). Lessons:
- After "adopting" anything, verify `git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> master`.
- legatum-sim defaults to Normal difficulty: always pass `--difficulty hard` for balance runs.

## 2026-10-01 — AI route search: unexplored tiles must count as passable
`AiContext::move_cost` returns None for unexplored tiles, while `PlayerView::movement_path` treats unknown terrain as passable Grassland. The new settler-escort shared route used the former, so pairs at the fog frontier held forever. The fix (6e434d9) treats fog as Grassland and falls back to the civilian's route. Any new AI path search must decide fog semantics explicitly; ViewBuilder tests default to a fully explored map and won't catch it. The remaining 4 stalls in 1,120 duel games are endgame stalemates (Economic/Tall pairs stuck at 7-9 VP to the 1,200-turn cap): passive openings lack a closing plan.

## 2026-10-01 — V9 re-landed (9d75a9d); balance still outside pillar 8 on Hard
Merged on top of the real-Rush and identity work. The one conflict (military.rs doc comment) kept master's Rush functions. A two-dot tree diff of a branch cut before a merge makes the merged code look "deleted": always trial-merge (`git merge-tree --write-tree master <branch>`) before concluding a branch drops work. Astra's Hard validation (10,000 8-player games): best/worst ratio 3.02→2.31x at Quick tuning, 4.48→2.73x at Quick held-out, 2.60→2.44x at Standard tuning, 3.36→1.81x at Standard held-out. Better everywhere, still above 1.5x. Germany is last throughout; Byzantium and Celts lead. Report: docs/sim-results/2026-10-01-reland-balance-v9.md.

## 2026-10-01 — Teaching the AI to fear city fire made it passive
Astra's ai-city-strike-awareness (branch, not merged) added city fire to the scripted AI's danger, exposure, retreat, heal and assault forecasts. Over 400 Hard 8-player Standard games, city-fire losses fell from 12.9 to 5.9 per game, but captures fell from 0.215 to 0.083 per game. The Proxy benchmark didn't improve (127 → 125 of 128 lobbies). Risk-aware tactics need a matching "commit when the forecast is good" rule, or the AI just stops attacking, which makes it easier for humans. Judge AI changes by captures and wins, not only survival. Revision queued as ai-city-strike-awareness-v2.

## 2026-10-01 — `start-settlers=N` means N EXTRA Settlers
The rules experiment adds N Settlers to the normal starting Settler (crates/core/src/game.rs ~113), so start-settlers=3 starts with four. Every "settlers3" result from 2026-09-30 is a four-Settler start. "Start with 3 Settlers" (the user's pillar-10 proposal) is `start-settlers=2`. In the tuned-genome sweep that gave GreedyExpand 0.60, Rush 0.62, Tall 0.27 and DefendedExpand 0.42. Spotted by Astra's Tall analysis.

## 2026-10-01 — Identity gates in evolution: noisy held-out rates need a fixed floor, not relative slack
With strict no-regression against the incumbent's held-out gate rate (60-120 seat-games), DefendedExpand's large, significant win gains (+0.25, p<1e-6) were vetoed when identity dipped 0.60 → 0.59. Relative slack (incumbent − 0.05) fixes that but compounds: 0.55 → 0.50 → 0.45 over successive promotions. The rule now in tools/duel/duel_evolve.py: an incumbent at or near its gate keeps a fixed floor of required − 0.05, a failing incumbent gets no slack, and comparisons use an epsilon.

## 2026-10-01 — City-fire awareness v2: commit to good assaults (merged)
The v2 revision keeps city fire in exposure, retreat and heal for uncommitted units, and makes assaults mass melee plus ranged support and accept the forecast shot when capture is viable. Over 400 Hard 8-player Standard games: captures 0.19 → 0.27 per game, city-fire losses 11.2 → 5.7 per game, turns +0.9%, no stalls. Default's duel mean rose slightly. Astra's note: staging at range 3 leaves infantry blind, so an assembled army needs a survivable range-2 reconnaissance step. The TS mock mirrors exposure and retreat but not massed-assault coordination.

## 2026-10-01 — Tall VP plan (merged 30922b6): modest gain, structural ceiling remains
Tall's AI now targets its reachable VP: growth to two population-8 cities and 20 population, the faction goal, a Great Work, Walls before science when threatened, and science as the closing title. In built-in duels its mean went 0.21 → 0.26, and Tall vs Rush 30% → 50%, at 72% identity. It is still far from valid. ## 2026-10-01 — Valid duel openings still don't make a harder 8-player Hard
With the fixed, evolved openings (six of seven duel-valid), an 8-player Hard whose seats play them for the whole game (uniform pool, no Tall) was not harder for a human-style challenger than the scripted Hard. Challenger wins: GreedyExpand 11.0% → 15.3%, Snowball 11.0% → 11.3%, Rush 4.0% → 6.8%, Proxy 1.6% both. It also had 12 stalls against 0, and leader pressure fell. Duel strength and multiplayer strength are different skills: the scripted Hard wins 8-player games through mid/late leader containment, which the openings lack. Next experiment: openings early, then hand off to the scripted Hard (Astra hard-openings-handoff). Report: branch astra/hard-openings-confirmation, docs/sim-results/2026-10-01-hard-openings-confirmation.md.

## 2026-10-01 — Openings-then-hand-off matches old Hard's difficulty and keeps opening variety
Hard v2 with a hand-off (each AI seat plays an evolved opening early, then switches permanently to the scripted Hard) played 400 8-player Standard games per challenger. Challenger wins: GreedyExpand 12.0% old → 11.0%, Snowball 11.0% → 10.0%, Rush 5.0% → 5.5%, Proxy 1.6% unchanged (paired p ≥ 0.67). Wars per game returned to old levels (15.3 vs 16.5); full-game openings had cut them to 5.4. There were no stalls. So the hand-off adds variety without losing difficulty, but doesn't make Hard harder. Rush handed off on turn 2 because its starting Soldier met the army target; fix queued (handoff-rush-fix). None of these sims reproduces how badly a human beat Hard. The challenger stand-ins win only ~11%, so "harder for a human" still needs a human-like benchmark.

## 2026-10-01 — Faction goal planning merged; Mongols wins dipped
Rebased goal planning (d4b090b): Sparta plans Walls, guards and a legal expedition around city fire, and Mongols keeps feasible Market trios and only founds safe replacements. On 600 matched Hard 8-player Standard games: best/worst ratio 2.76x → 2.55x, Sparta wins 10.2% → 12.8%, Mongols goals 36.3% → 36.7%, but Mongols wins 10.7% → 7.8% (64 → 47; about 1.6 sd, cause unisolated). ## 2026-10-01 — The disk watcher only cleans below LOW_GB (150 GB) free
tools/cleanup/disk-watch.sh logs every 30 minutes but runs the cleanup only when free space is below LOW_GB (default 150) and AUTO_APPLY=1. Overnight, Astra worktrees grew to 370 GB (free 482 → 351 GB) with no cleanup, as designed. A manual `tools/cleanup/disk-cleanup.sh --apply` freed 237 GB of merged, idle worktrees. During heavy Astra nights, run the cleanup by hand at heartbeats rather than waiting for the low-disk trigger.

## 2026-10-01 — A human-playbook benchmark (Proxy v5) gets 17%; humans still win far more
Proxy v5 (`--proxy-version 5`) plays the user's stated plan: about 3 cities, army, early conquest, gold into armies, then turtle and tech. It wins 17.3% (CI 13.9-21.3%) against 7 scripted Hard AIs in 8-player Standard games, against v4's 1.75% and a GreedyExpand challenger's 12.75%. It has 2.8 cities at turn 100 and 3.5 at turn 136; the user had 8 by turn 136. So "Hard is too easy for humans" is still not reproduced in simulation. The gaps are execution (siege timing, capture coordination, purchase bursts, consolidation). City fire resolves before movement, so retreats need planning a turn ahead. v6 is queued.

## 2026-10-01 — Human-playbook benchmark v6: 31% against 7 Hard
Proxy v6 (`--proxy-version 6`, opt-in) adds coordinated captures, earlier army assembly, purchase bursts, settler raids and consolidation to v5's plan. It wins 31.3% (CI 26.9-36.0%) against 7 scripted Hard AIs in 8-player Standard games, against v5's 15.0% on the same opponents. It has 3.7 cities at turn 136 and makes 580 captures in 400 games. Still short of the user's real dominance. Findings: staging at radius 3 can deadlock outside two-tile sight, and successful captures need immediate relief troops. This is the first benchmark that measures "hard for a human-like player"; use it, not GreedyExpand challengers, to judge Hard changes.

## 2026-10-01 — Against human-style play, the hand-off Hard is no harder
v6 wins 31.2% against 7 scripted Hard AIs and 34.8% against 7 hand-off Hard v2 AIs (400 games each, same seeds; docs/sim-results/2026-10-01-v6-vs-hard-variants.md). Opening variety doesn't buy difficulty. Difficulty for humans must come from better scripted mid-game decisions (defending settlers and thin cities, reacting to an early conquering neighbour), measured with v6.

On master with everything from tonight, scripted Hard, 2,000 games per speed: ratio 2.59x Quick and 2.49x Standard (held-out 2.30x / 3.11x). ## 2026-10-01 — Balance bundle D: rewarding weak factions' goals converts survival into wins (1.16-1.57x)
Germany and Mongols usually survive but lose the VP race. (A fresh 2,000-game Quick cohort later confirmed D at 1.44x vs 2.59x for defaults.) Raising their existing identity goals to 3 VP (requirements unchanged), plus small drawbacks on the leaders (Byzantium conventional buildings 120% → 130%, Celts 100% → 110%) and +5 production on Sparta Settlers, gave best/worst ratios of 1.49x/1.16x (Quick/Standard tuning, 2,000 games) and 1.57x/1.27x (held-out, 1,000 games). Every faction lands at 9.8-15.8%. An extra 500-seed Quick cohort read 1.68x, so Quick sits right at the edge. It's an opt-in `--rules-experiment` bundle on master, awaiting the user's decision (docs/sim-results/2026-10-01-balance-v10-iteration.md). 500-game held-out cohorts were too noisy to judge bundles; use 1,000+.

## 2026-10-01 — How the human-playbook benchmark beats Hard, and what fixing it costs
Astra's 400-game v6 audit: 545 of 580 city captures came after at least 3 consecutive turns of visible warning, 554 began with no garrison, and 513 of 561 captured cities were never retaken within 10 turns. The scripted Hard sees the threat, but doesn't garrison or recapture. 47 candidate fixes were tried. Broad defence quotas lengthened AI-vs-AI games beyond 10% or raised stalls and faction spread. Focused guards, escorts and early containment cut v6 from 31.25% to 26.0% while passing those guards. The run died on model capacity before committing (WIP 812b7e2 on astra/hard-vs-human-playbook); the continuation is queued. Lesson for long Astra tasks: ask for intermediate commits so a crash doesn't strand hours of work.

The scripted Hard (Hard only; Normal unchanged) now garrisons cities under visible threat, escorts settlers, buys emergency defenders and contains early conquerors (crates/ai/src/hard_defense.rs). ## 2026-10-01 — The 3-Settler start and balance bundle D interact; don't stack them blindly
8-player Hard, 1,000 games per cell (docs/sim-results/2026-10-01-decision-evidence.md). 3 Settlers (`start-settlers=2`) made games 12.5-13% shorter, raised Standard wars (17.3 → 22.9) and captures (0.21 → 0.34 per game), and cut human-playbook v6 wins from 31.25% to 19.25%. v6's early lead grows, but it loses ground from turn 75. The "6 of 7 openings valid" result leaned on Tall as everyone's victim. Without Tall (evolved genomes, base rules, ~/LegatumRuns/confirm-final/base-evolved), the significant edges are: GreedyExpand > DefendedExpand, Snowball, Economic; Default > DefendedExpand, Economic; Rush > Snowball. ## 2026-10-01 — The opening results were measured on a slowed-down early game (G8 pacing still off)
Turn-by-turn production from recorded duels (Standard): GreedyExpand's first Settler took 35 turns (T2-T37); Snowball and Economic build a Monument first (T2-T26, the fallback while Workshop and Market are locked behind Fabrication and Exchange), then the building, so their second city comes around T77-81; Rush builds a Market between Soldiers and declares at about T61. G8's diagnosis (2026-09-28) still holds: Standard costs are 2x Quick, and capitals sit at the 3-production floor. Its fix (capital-production + opening-ramp) has been waiting on the user since then. Consequences: Rush can't strike early, GreedyExpand isn't punished (0.11 settlers and 0.04 cities lost per game), and "infrastructure first" openings look odd. Opening build lists must only name items available at turn 1, or say explicitly what happens while an item is locked. Retune openings and balance after pacing is decided (Astra pacing-validation queued). The user also dropped DefendedExpand as an opening.

## 2026-10-01 — Astra runner: pin the model per task; the Codex default was unusable
tools/astra/runner.sh passed no `-m`, so tasks used whatever ~/.codex/config.toml set. When that became `gpt-6.1-sol` (rejected for ChatGPT-account Codex: "model is not supported"), tasks died within seconds (pacing-validation, a master review). The runner now takes `model: astra|sol|luna` and `effort:` headers (gpt-6-astra / gpt-6-sol / gpt-6-luna; default sol medium; the reviewer uses sol medium) and logs the model on each start. Runner loops were restarted by PID after the script was replaced with `mv` (a running bash reads its script incrementally, so never edit it in place). Separately, "Selected model is at capacity" errors from gpt-6-astra killed two long tasks; ask long tasks for intermediate commits.

## 2026-10-01 — Hard recapture logic didn't move the human-playbook benchmark (not merged)
Astra's recapture planner (branch astra/hard-recapture-r2, 558b816) re-gathers troops, ranged support and reinforcements to retake recently lost own or allied cities. v6 won 109/400 against it vs 110/400 against master (seeds 3620001), with Hard-only guards neutral. No measurable gain, so it wasn't merged. Lost cities are rarely recoverable by the time the AI reacts; prevention (the merged warned-city defence) is what moved the number. Forecasts must also budget the garrison's faction healing during travel: targeting a city's current low HP overestimates viability.

## 2026-10-02 — macOS /bin/bash is 3.2: no associative arrays
A `#!/bin/bash` study script used `declare -A C=([d]=... [pd]=...)`. On macOS's bash 3.2 that fails silently: every key evaluates arithmetically to index 0, so all five "conditions" ran with the same flags, and 2 hours of sims produced identical rows. Use a `case` lookup function (or /opt/homebrew/bin/bash), and smoke-test the condition-to-flags mapping itself, not just the simulator flags. `source <(...)` is also broken in bash 3.2. Identical rows across conditions should be read as a harness bug.

Standard, 8-player Hard, 1,000 games (docs/sim-results/2026-10-02-pacing-study.md): capital-production + opening-ramp moved the first Settler from turn 49 to 18 and the second city from 55 to 26; cities at turn 100 went 2.09 → 3.05; games ran 6% shorter; human-playbook v6 fell from 26.0% to 22.5%. Bundle D's ratio rose 1.69x → 1.96x, so balance needs retuning under pacing. The built-in GreedyExpand's 30-turn Settler interval (15 at Quick) was what kept it at ~2 cities at turn 50; with interval 0 it averages 2.66 with 3+ cities in 68% of duels, matching the Civ 6 benchmark. GreedyExpand still beats Rush 73-77% under pacing: counters, not economy, are the remaining problem.

Four TI4-style redesigns ran overnight as a chain: each Astra task merged the previous branch first, and a script released the next only after an exit-0 finish. ## 2026-10-03 — Planning-time validation must apply the same phase order as resolution
Playtest-5 bug: declaring war at Peace and ordering a ranged attack on that empire's city in the same turn is legal at resolution (surprise wars apply in phase 0, before ranged fire). But the planning UI validated the ranged order against the current Peace state, flagged "no enemy unit or city to attack there", hid the city from ranged targeting, and trapped the unit in the "needs orders" loop. G20 had fixed only the melee path. Any rule that resolution applies early (surprise wars) must also apply in planning validation, targeting overlays, forecasts and AI planning; check every order type, not just the one in the report. Fix queued: fix-ranged-same-turn-war.

## 2026-10-03 — Turn report history: layout and test gotchas
- The This Turn panel has no spare height at 1440x900: any new row breaks `minimap.spec` "all eight rows fit" (1 px tolerance). The Last turn control therefore replaces the panel subtitle once a report exists.
- The Court look hides `.ph-sub`, so anything placed in a panel subtitle disappears there unless explicitly overridden.
- Report history is in memory only (last 20), not in the localStorage autosave, to stay clear of its size limit.
- `Event::Battle.attacker_at` is serde-default and omitted when `None`, so state hashes and pinned tapes didn't change; fogged attackers are redacted in `event_visibility.rs`.
- `mockClient.test.ts` "runs 30 turns with lively AIs" takes about 5 s alone and timed out at the 5 s default under load average ~170; it now has a 20 s timeout. With many parallel branches building and simming, expect wall-clock-bound tests to flake: rerun before blaming the change.

## 2026-10-03 — Walls-only city strike: Rush becomes viable, conquest rises
Cities now fire only with Walls (any tier; one core function `combat::city_can_fire`). Measured on the branch before merge:
- Duel Rush vs GreedyExpand (60 seeds, 1,800 games): Rush 25.0% → 45.8%; Rush is now a valid opening (mean score 0.385 → 0.521). Economic is the only invalid opening left. Rush still reaches an enemy city by turn 80 in only 44% of games: delivery, not the city's guns, is now its limit.
- 8-player Hard Quick (500 games, seed 5200001): captures per game 0.07 → 0.35, Walls built 10.7 → 12.4, faction ratio 1.87 → 1.33, turns 123.5 → 125.0, no stalls. Standard and v6 were unfinished at merge because of machine load.
- The finding confirms the earlier diagnosis: unwalled cities shooting back was the main thing blocking rushes, more than unit costs or AI.
- Part of Rush's shortfall against GreedyExpand is the new AI wall response (walls valued more when a rival masses nearby), which is the intended counter.

## 2026-10-03 — AI upkeep bankruptcy: a deliberate-disband safety net, not stricter spending
Scripted AIs never checked upkeep before buying or building, so `rules::cities::pay_gold` force-disbanded their costliest unit about 11 times per game (200 Hard Standard games). Tightening production and purchase solvency cut disbands to 2.4 per game but suppressed armies enough to reopen a title-race stall (`coalition_stall`, seed 910030). What shipped (claude/ai-budget, merged 3335d915) is a safety net only: when `PlayerView.economy.bankruptcy` says this turn ends bankrupt, or this turn's own purchases tip it negative, the AI disbands its weakest idle garrison unit first. Result on the walls-only tree: upkeep disbands 11.3 → 0.72 per game; captures 1.07 → 1.19; faction ratio 2.38 → 1.32; v6 34.0% → 31.5%. These are single 200-game samples, directional only. New telemetry: `upkeep_disbands`.

## 2026-10-03 — "Captures per game" is not an AI quality metric
The user pointed out that aggregate captures mix factions that should conquer (Sparta, Mongols) with ones that shouldn't (Celts razes; Switzerland turtle). Report conquest per faction against its identity, and judge AI combat skill by efficiency (captures per war declared, losses per capture, failed walled assaults) rather than volume. Earlier reports in this log that cite total captures (walls-only, AI conquest, AI budget) are directional at best. The method lives in the legatum-factions skill.

## 2026-10-03 — New state fields must skip serializing their default
The Byzantium salvage goal added `Player.byzantium_salvage_science` with plain `#[serde(default)]`. Every archived AI test fixture then re-serialized with an extra `"byzantium_salvage_science":0`, and six AI test binaries failed their archive-hash pins. `crates/core/tests/factions.rs` also still used the old Byzantium goal. Neither showed up until the full release check, because the branch was merged before its agent finished its own full test run. Rules: new state fields use `skip_serializing_if` for their default, as state.rs already does; and run the whole workspace test suite on the merged tree before shipping, even under a cutoff.

## 2026-10-03 — Byzantium goal retuned: salvage Science, 1,200
Byzantium's goal was "Deep Survey + explore 100 tiles" (completed in about 98% of games, a freebie). It is now 1,200 Science earned from salvage camps on rivals' land, the faction's broken rule. On 1,000 eight-player Hard games per speed (seed 5000001), completion is 44.2% Quick and 58.4% Standard, inside the 40–60% band, and Byzantium wins 10.4% and 10.9%: slightly weak, unchanged by the goal. Faction ratio on that run: 1.53x Quick, 1.67x Standard. Switzerland are worst at Standard, and that's the pending tuning task. Gotcha: `cargo build -p X --example Y` doesn't relink X's default binary, so one validation run silently used a stale threshold; cross-check a small run against expectations before trusting a big one.

## 2026-10-03 — Hard AI ignores a runaway conqueror (playtest 6)
The user rushed as Mongols on Hard and eliminated the Athens and Byzantium by turn 52. Every other AI stayed at Peace: no walls, no alliances, no second front. Leader containment (coalition warnings, Calls) keys on VP pressure, and the user had only 4/10, so a conqueror with low VP is invisible to it. Walls-only city strike plus the conquest AI made a human rush much stronger, and the AI had no counter. Threat must be scored from public aggression and momentum (captures, eliminations, wars, armies near borders), not VP alone. The work is on claude/ai-threat-response, built on Astra's stopped opponent-assessment branch.

## 2026-10-03 — Orders that look accepted but fail
In playtest 6 a ranged order on a city at Peace queued, drew its icon on the map, and was then rejected by core, with a misleading "no enemy there" message. Moves already asked "Declare War?" first; ranged orders never checked the relationship. The MapCanvas ranged test passed because it never asserted that queued orders had no errors. Fixed on claude/attack-at-peace. Also: at 961–1024px wide the desktop turn dock wasn't a flex column, so a taller call to action overflowed at 1000x600; the dock's budget there comes from the race panel's minimum height.

## 2026-10-03 — War events: two timings, and how ally calls appear
`WarDeclared` has two timings. For a surprise war at Peace, `relation.effective_turn` equals the resolved turn; when a Pact or Alliance is broken, it's the resolved turn + 1. An ally answering a call to arms emits its own `WarDeclared` (declarers = [ally]) and then `CallAccepted`; breaking a treaty to declare war emits `TreatyBreached` before `WarDeclared`. The war interstitial (`app/src/celebrate/alarms.ts`) takes all its wording from `format.ts`, so it can't drift from the report. To add one sound without rebuilding all audio, import `build_audio`, call `build_sfx` on the new entry, then run `node app/scripts/audio-credits.mjs`.

A full replay of the user's Mongols rush (70 turns, every state hash matched) shows:

- **No wars.** AIs never declared war on each other. The Sparta declared war on the user at t57 and then withdrew. A Celts–Japan alliance against the user lasted two turns.

- **The user's recipe:** 2 Rangers plus 1 melee, positioned in range before a surprise war, killing garrisons from range and capturing with melee. The AI's Rush opening goes to war at about t12 with 2 melee units and no ranged support, and rarely captures (27% of games, median t75).
- **Mongols:** the v6 proxy wins as Mongols far more than as any other faction (10/13 and 22/25 in two runs), which is worth a balance look.
- **Walls timing:** earliest Walls is about t45–55 at Standard, against a human capture at t35.

## 2026-10-03 — Passive ranged garrison: a faction-conditional pass ate the unit's one order
In playtest 6 the Athens' Ranger in Resonator held for three turns and died without firing. `plan_military` runs an early `garrison_cities` pass, only when a Mongols empire is at war with us, and it gave the garrison `hold_or_upgrade`. A unit gets one order per turn, so that pre-empted `ranged_fire`. The existing test passed only because its enemy wasn't Mongols: synthetic fixtures with a single enemy faction hide faction-conditional passes. Fix (claude/ranged-garrison-fires, merged fcefc16d):
- **Holds become shots:** `fire_from_holds` converts any ranged `HoldUnit` with a target in range into a shot, at every difficulty.
- **Target choice is value-based:** threat removed × kill chance, with a capture threat counting the city's HP. Shooting would-be captors first comes from the scoring.

**Results** (200 Hard games):
- Idle garrison-turns with a target in range: 14.7 → 1.6 per game.
- Mongols win rate: 33% → 26%; its rivals' garrisons were the ones affected.
- Faction ratio: 4.7x → 3.7x.

Open judgement calls: firing forgoes fortify and the resting heal, and a concealed Celts hunter now reveals itself by firing.

## 2026-10-03 — LLM opponent seat: first 10 games (Luna escalating to Astra vs 7 Hard)
Merged b8fc1cbc; see docs/llm-seat.md.
- **Results:** the LLM seat won 1 of 10, with mean VP equal to scripted Hard (3.9 vs 4.0). It walled before its first threat in 8 of 10 games, where scripted Hard is late or never walls. It declared 52 wars for 1 capture, and never rushed.
- **Luna vs Astra:** agreement is 80% on war targets, but Luna says "no war" 96% of the time and agreed with Astra's wars 6 of 35 times. Peace agreement is 48%, accepting offers 62%. Luna is overconfident: 75% agreement even at 0.9+ confidence.
- **Cost:** each `codex exec` call carries about 25k tokens of Codex's own agent instructions, mostly cached. A direct API call would cut input about tenfold. Games take about 16 minutes each.

**Hard AI blind spots it found:**
- **Containment.** It only fires against an aggressor with 5+ cities (`diplomacy.rs::containment_target`, `cities < 5 * members`).
- **Late action against VP leaders.** Wars on the eventual winner cluster in the final 5–20 turns.
- **Wars without pressure:** 0.19 captures per war, and unwalled enemy cities left untouched for turns.
- **Late Walls.** The median gap from a nearby enemy to building Walls is 29 turns.
- **Pact sprees.** Accepting every Pact sends Influence from +16 to −29, and Pacts get signed with empires never met.

**Findings channel (502 reports).** The top design flags are "accepting every Pact is a no-brainer" and "expansion is too slow" (Settlers take 14–52 turns; 3–5 cities at t200). Some "bugs" were gaps in the briefing (missing faction-goal progress, no Influence breakdown).

## 2026-10-03 — Worktree hygiene and agent spawns
86 worktrees accumulated: the disk watcher only cleaned below 150 GB free. It now removes merged, clean, idle (3h), unlocked worktrees every 30 minutes; the first run freed 270 GB. ## 2026-10-03 — Pact fixes: contact rule and value scoring (claude/pact-fixes, folded into remove-influence)
- **Effect of value scoring:** AIs signed about 80% fewer treaties (Standard: 15.1 → 2.8 per empire per game). Influence-debt turns fell from 123 to 4 per game, and wars between treaty partners fell about 90%. The restraint comes purely from the scoring.
- **The cost:** the Switzerland collapsed at Standard (9.0% → 3.7%) because they relied on blanket Pacts for safety. Faction identities can lean on AI habits; check every faction when changing a shared system.
- **Lesson for humans:** a treaty with only a one-off fee is a no-brainer. It needs ongoing upkeep or an exclusive downside.
- **Tape versioning:** new GameState fields change every tape's initial hash. A tape-version gate in `Tape::initial_state` keeps old tapes and archives replayable.
- **Mock timing:** the mock's contact recording must happen at core's update points, not on every `refreshVision`, which also runs every movement round.
- **Shared scratch files:** agents shared the scratch script `scratchpad/nice.sh` and one overwrote it to `cd` into its own worktree. Agents must use per-agent scratch subfolders.
## 2026-10-03 — Where sim time goes, and why sccache can't share our own crates
- **Profile** (xctrace Time Profiler, master, 8 players, Hard, Standard, 1 thread): building `player_view` is 52% of a game, AI planning 37%, `resolve_turn` only 16%. Inside the view, `research::tech_unlocks` (26%) previews every building and unit in every city, calling `city_yields` 2+ times per item per city. Each `city_yields` scanned all units (`squatter` via `units_at`) and all cities (`city_at`) for each of the 18 work tiles, and `Hex::within` grew and sorted a fresh Vec (`grow_one` alone 9%).
- **Fix (branch claude/perf-player-view):** squatted tiles and nearby cities are collected once per `city_yields` call; `within` pre-sizes and skips the sort (it is built in `Ord` order already); `tech_unlocks` reuses per-city results (Production depends on the item only through its auto focus, and a unit leaves the after-yields unchanged). Same outputs: tapes byte-identical to master on 10 games (Quick and Standard with barbarians), and the runner tape pins and determinism tests pass. About 30% less CPU per game (user CPU 15.1 s → 10.5 s for 4 Quick games, 44.2 s → 30.7 s for 6 Standard games), about 1.44x the games per core.
- **Next hot spots:** the Inheritance usefulness experiment (`sim::inheritance`, ~12%: shadow games resolved every turn plus extra planning) runs in every sim but only feeds research telemetry, so it could be opt-in; AI clones and drops `PlayerView`s (~8%).
- **sccache only shares third-party crates across worktrees.** Cargo's `-C metadata` for a path package includes its path, so legatum-core/ai/sim in two worktrees never share a cache entry (tested with two copies of a crate: the registry dependency hit, the local crate missed, with or without `SCCACHE_BASEDIRS`). Expect ~30–40% Rust hit rates; it saves dependency builds, not ours.
- **Overload is mostly sims:** at load ~220 on 16 cores, ~53 runnable threads were sims (11 cohorts, 3–6 threads each, at least four of them master baselines on seed 5200001 or the proxy v6 cohort) and ~28 test binaries. A release build of legatum-sim took 28 minutes wall for 73 s of CPU.

## 2026-10-04 — Too many concurrent Opus agents hit the session limit
At about 23:50 on 2026-10-03, roughly 12 concurrent Claude agents exhausted the Claude Max session limit, and every agent died mid-task. Agents spawned with `isolation: worktree` couldn't be resumed afterwards ("worktree could not be verified"). Agents pointed at worktrees the lead had created by hand resumed fine, and their background sims kept running as orphans. Lessons:
- Keep about 5 Claude agents running at once.
- Hand long simulation runs and mechanical work to Astra (Codex).
- Prefer lead-created worktrees, which survive a resume.
- If an isolated agent dies, start a fresh agent in its existing worktree with a full brief.

## 2026-10-04 — Pathfinding bounces (claude/pathfinding-bounces, merged)
A melee unit attacking an adjacent target is a "mover" that never leaves its tile. Treating every friend with a pending order as passable sent units through attackers, so they bounced. Now one shared costing (`core::path::route_around_friends`) is used by preview, resolution, AI preflight and the mock. Friends that stay put are never passed, and friends that are moving out are risky, so a free route wins ties. Friendly bounces fell 8% and friend-caused failed attacks 31%. About half of the remaining AI friend blocks are destination collisions (the AI picks a tile a friend occupies), which is an AI destination-choice problem, measurable with `crates/sim/examples/bounce_probe.rs`. Still open: move and attack orders in the unit panel show raw coordinates ("MOVE TO 11,4").
