## 2026-10-04 — Thread-cap pool starved small requests
The first slot.sh had no queue order: 6-thread sims kept grabbing freed tokens, so a 2-thread probe waited more than 40 minutes. A mutex directory left empty by a killed process (it died before recording its pid) also deadlocked every caller. Fixed with a first-come-first-served ticket queue, and by breaking owner-less mutexes older than a minute. When replacing a script that's in use, `mv` the new file over it: running bash instances keep the old inode.

## 2026-10-04 — Budgets and restarts: what the supervisor must watch
- **Correction (same day):** the Fable weekly line read as unused while the all-models weekly line was well along. I took that to mean Fable had a separate, spare budget. The user says it doesn't: Fable burns the weekly budget faster. Never use Fable; offload to Codex Sol or Luna instead.
- **The restart fixed BTLEServer** (stuck at 100% CPU for 13 days, even with Bluetooth off).
- **Locks survive restarts.** Worktree locks naming a long-dead agent PID survive a reboot and silently stop cleanup from reclaiming about 53 GB. Unlocking them was blocked by auto-mode for agents, so it needs the user's OK.
- **The Astra runner resumes on re-queue.** It reuses an existing `astra/<name>` worktree (its `worktree add` fails, then it merges master into the existing one), so re-queued tasks continue from their saved commits.
- **The supervisor role.** The perf watcher became the ops supervisor (.claude/agents/legatum-ops-supervisor.md), with a self-maintained playbook (.claude/skills/legatum-ops) covering budget projection, postmortems, throughput and the machine.
- **Stale locks are now cleared automatically** (user-approved). `tools/cleanup/unlock-stale-locks.sh` unlocks worktree locks naming a dead PID; the disk watcher runs it each cycle before cleanup. PID-less locks (release builds, shared baselines) are untouched. The earlier dead-PID locks had already been released by the stopped agents.
- **A reboot orphans Codex tasks.** Their files stay in `.progress/astra-queue/running/` with no `codex exec` behind them, so the queue never restarts them. Four sat there after this morning's restart (sparta, salvage limiter, terrain resync, Switzerland/Japan); moved back to pending. The supervisor now checks for this.
- **Budget policy:** pace Claude usage to the weekly reset, keep extra usage off, and near a limit switch to token-free CPU/GPU work (sims, builds, Laya training) and Codex.
- **Codex couldn't write ~/LegatumRuns.** The runner's sandbox writable roots were ~/.cargo, /tmp, .git and .progress only, so `cached-baseline.sh` and every ~/LegatumRuns run folder failed inside Codex tasks ("mkdir: ... Operation not permitted"). Tasks silently fell back to private dirs and re-measured master. Added ~/LegatumRuns and ~/.cache/huggingface (for Laya) and restarted the runners. Gotcha: in zsh, `kill $pids` with a newline-separated list doesn't split; pass PIDs explicitly.
- **The Vite font 403s were caused by the worktree setup.** Adding the Scenarios fs.allow (`['.', '../scenarios']`) replaced Vite's default allow list. In worktrees, app/node_modules is a symlink to the main checkout, so fonts resolved outside the list, 403'd, and broke the console-clean Playwright checks (lenses ×3). It may also shift layout metrics. Fix: also allow `realpathSync('node_modules')`. The staging spec also needs `cargo build -p legatum-server` (debug), which the release script didn't build.
- **Race panel at 1440x900.** Since the whole-rows race panel (UI-review fix), on the turn after a title change one row scrolls behind "+1 more" (minimap.spec.ts:127 fails by 15px). Shipped in 6.3 as known; the fix goes on master.
- **Sims are cheap now.** An 8-player Hard Standard game takes about 5 CPU-seconds (10.4 s user for 2 games on master's baseline binary, 19 MB RSS, measured under load ~130). A 400-game cohort is about 35 core-minutes. The machine's overload comes mostly from parallel Rust builds and test suites across many worktrees (each builds the whole workspace; sccache can't share our crates), plus Playwright.
- **Lanes replace one worktree per task** (user's idea). Every Codex task used to get a fresh worktree, so every task paid a cold build of the whole workspace in 3 profiles (clippy, release tests and sim, WASM), with ~26 GB of target each; there were 62 worktrees. Each queue worker now owns a persistent locked lane (`runner.sh queue <k>`) and switches branches in it. Several agents in one worktree at once was rejected: cargo's build lock serializes them, and mixed edits break builds and confound sim results.
- **The supervisor runs every 30 minutes on Claude Opus** (lead cron; user, 2026-10-04). A brief Codex-shift variant was dropped: Codex capacity is limited too. The lead writes usage to `.progress/supervisor/usage.json` first; the supervisor keeps runs lean via `tools/ops/snapshot.sh`. Each run names the top constraint on progress and acts on it. The constraints named today, biggest first:
  1. the Claude budget;
  2. lead-only UI verification: Codex can't run a browser, so the Playwright bridge is queued;
  3. hotspot merge conflicts on tape pins and fixtures: the one-command repin tool is queued;
  4. CPU oversubscription from builds: lanes are done and the build-slot cap is queued;
  5. long-lived branches.
- **Correction: Codex/ChatGPT capacity is not abundant** (user, 2026-10-04). Both the Claude and Codex budgets are limited and fixed. CLAUDE.md and the ops playbook said "abundant ChatGPT credits"; both are corrected. Pace both budgets, and keep Codex to about 4 lanes.
- **Heartbeat** (user request): `tools/ops/heartbeat.py` prints phone-width progress bars for every outstanding Codex task. The stages are queued 0%, running (elapsed against the typical run time for its effort, capped at 80%), awaiting review 85%, and merged 100%. It runs on request only (user, 2026-10-04). A cron prompt can only run on this session's model, so the script does all the work and the turn is one tool call. A separate Haiku session running the same script would be cheaper still. Hide superseded tasks by listing them in `.progress/heartbeat-retired.txt`.
- **An Xcode auto-update breaks git and linking machine-wide.** At 10:27 Xcode updated from 26.6 to 27.0, and until `sudo xcodebuild -license accept` is run, every `/usr/bin/git`, `cc` and `ld` fails with "You have not agreed to the Xcode license". A lane runner then failed all 8 queued tasks in 6 seconds. Workaround for one-off commands: `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`. The supervisor added runner guards: pause while git fails; tasks that fail within 2 minutes go to hold/. Also, inside the Codex sandbox, `kill -0` on outside processes returns "Operation not permitted", so slot.sh run by Codex took live holders for dead ones and broke the thread cap. The fix is folded into the build-slot task.
- **Workaround while the Xcode license is pending:** `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools` gives a working git and linker (tested: rustc link, git, clang 21). runner.sh now falls back to it automatically, so the queue no longer needs the user at the Mac. Codex tasks already running keep the broken environment until they're re-queued.
- **Resolved:** the user accepted the Xcode 27 license and turned off App Store auto-updates (`com.apple.commerce AutoUpdate = 0`). The runner's Command Line Tools fallback only triggers on the license error, so it now stays dormant.
- **RAM is not a constraint.** The workload is CPU-bound: a sim game uses about 19 MB, builds a few GB, and almost all of the machine's memory is free. The headroom matters for the GPU, which shares unified memory: Laya training, or a local open-weights LLM as a token-free cheap tier (proposed experiment: measure agreement with Luna before use).
- **Glass at the Gate: the AI attacker's "give up" was bankruptcy.** In the user's run, Mongols started at T20 with 9 Gold, one city and five military units (army strength 90). It spent T21–23 shooting from range, then on T24 disbanded three units to avoid bankruptcy (`production.rs::disband_weakest_unit`), and the rest drifted off. No part of the AI weighed "my money runs out in 3 turns" against "taking the city is worth VP", so the bankruptcy handler quietly overrode the war plan. This is the user's broader point: the AI is a stack of local rules with no common currency (VP or win odds) and no persistent campaign commitment.
- **Per-change sims cut back** (user): full balance cohorts per branch measured rulesets that would never ship and slowed landings (39+ min per gate under load). Now per change it's correctness plus a 50-game smoke check plus a targeted probe; full balance runs once per integration (7a, 7b), then the balance pass.
- **Terrain LOS landed (dfd3f2e6).** Playwright runs fine on the host even though Codex's sandbox can't launch Chromium, so UI branches from Codex must get their browser checks at landing. Under load around 165, three vitest tests timed out but passed in isolation; purchases.wasm.test.ts (a 300-turn synchronous mock) now has a 90 s timeout because terrain LOS adds per-turn mock cost. For information only: the Standard faction ratio is 3.08x after terrain LOS, against master's 4.06x.
- **The batch landing (Sparta, Switzerland/Japan, perf, build label) hit content conflicts beyond the pins:** the factions skill, game-rules.md, app data.ts, GuideContent and the mock state. Under the combined rules, promotion.json's archived orders no longer produced a promotion; it was regenerated with the promotion_tape example. Expect fixed-order archive tapes to break whenever combat or XP rules combine, and regenerate them; don't patch the expectations.

## 2026-10-04 — WebKit's null relatedTarget broke the game menu's outside-focus close (playtest 6.3)
"Exit to title" (and in principle every other item) in the in-game menu did nothing in the Mac app, but a quick Chromium check passed, which hid the bug for a while. Root cause: `GameMenu.tsx`'s `onBlur` handler closed the menu whenever `!e.currentTarget.contains(e.relatedTarget)`. Chromium populates `relatedTarget` with the element about to receive focus; WebKit (the Mac app's WKWebView) fires `blur` with `relatedTarget: null` when a mousedown moves focus from the already-focused first menu item ("Save to file…", auto-focused on open) to another button in the same menu, *before* the new element takes focus. The handler read `null` as "focus left the menu" and closed it mid-click, so `mouseup` landed on whatever the menu had covered (confirmed with instrumented pointerdown/mousedown/mouseup/click listeners: mousedown target was "Exit to title", mouseup target was a "Peace" button underneath) and no `click` ever fired. Fix: never trust `relatedTarget` for this; defer to `requestAnimationFrame` and check `document.activeElement` once focus has settled. Any other `onBlur`-based "did focus leave this container" check in this codebase should use the same pattern, not `relatedTarget`. Diagnosis needed the real engine: `LEGATUM_E2E_BROWSER=webkit npx playwright test` reproduced it in under a minute; Chromium (Playwright's default) never does, since it gives a real `relatedTarget`. Worth a standing check: run the game-menu/exit spec under webkit when its surrounding code changes, not just Chromium.
- **Headless Playwright browsers play audio through the speakers.** The user heard Legatum music while landing tests ran. The app now skips audio when `navigator.webdriver` is set, which works in every browser engine. Vitest's environment also sets webdriver, so the check is limited with `import.meta.env.MODE !== 'test'`; without that, 12 sound tests fail (branch claude/exit-and-growth-label, 76075229). Landing this branch, I'd initially merged the branch tip before it was amended to add that guard; the stale commit broke the same 12 tests, so always re-check a branch's current tip just before merging, not just when the lead names it.
- **Agents leave hidden built-in browser tabs open.** The exit-fix agent left a tab on localhost:5799 (its own legatum-server) in the Claude app's browser pane; with the pane hidden, the game's music kept playing. Agents that use the browser pane must close their tabs and stop their servers when done.
- **A stale dev app bundle can shadow the installed playtest.** The main checkout's `app/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/Legatum.app` (built Oct 2, no Scenarios menu) was registered with LaunchServices, and the user's launcher opened it instead of /Applications/Legatum.app (6.3). Fix: trash the stale bundle and `lsregister -f /Applications/Legatum.app`. Release builds now trash the source bundle after installing it.
- **WebKit surfaces the browser's own ResizeObserver backpressure notice as an uncaught `weberror`; Chromium doesn't.** Running `screen-tour.spec.ts` under WebKit for the first time, the scenario-completion test failed "No browser console errors" with a message that printed as empty (`e2e/fixtures.ts` built it with `stack ?? message`, and WebKit gives an empty-string stack, which `??` doesn't fall through on). Logging the raw error showed the real text: "ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications." — a benign browser diagnostic, not an app fault. Fixed both: the fixture now allowlists that exact message and uses `stack || message` so a future empty-stack error isn't hidden again. Expect more such WebKit-only diagnostics once `tools/release/check.sh`'s new `playwright-webkit` step runs regularly; log the raw error object before assuming it's a real regression.
- **The threat-response branch didn't survive integration with the faction batch:** 5 AI behaviour tests failed (garrison retreat vs walls, the Celts unique unit, the Swiss war at T51, a Pact threshold, elimination tracking). It was stopped mid re-merge loop, so it never re-verified. Lesson: branches that rework shared AI decision logic should land before, or together with, faction AI changes, not race them. Moved into ai-campaigns for 7b.
- **7a baseline (faecae92; 8-player Hard, 400 games per speed):** Standard ratio 15.4x (Mongols 30.8% vs Sparta 2.0%); Quick 9.6x (Byzantium and Mongols 19.2% vs Sparta 2.0%); v6 21.0%. The redesigned Sparta is the outlier at 2% at both speeds. The diagnosis task asks whether it's the rules or the AI not playing the identity. Informational, not a gate.
- **Playtest 7a shipped (tag playtest-7a; master ad7fe254 after merging the release).** The UI review found two 1000x600 blockers. (1) The growth label was clipped mid-word: ellipsis can't cross the nested tooltip span inside the inline-flex .pbar-label; fixed with flex-wrap. (2) The forecast card's city-fire math sat below its overflow-hidden box; it now scrolls on short windows. That second fix needed `.forecast.forecast`, because the base `.forecast { overflow: hidden }` rule comes later in styles.css and would otherwise win over the media query.
- **The user's 7a game, Sparta (Hard) at T53:** one city (first Settler queued at T52); declared war on the human at T43 but sent 2 of 4 units; the wounded attackers then held position (no field healing), never pressing to a capture. Restlessness probably drove the war, and a 'phony war' dodges desertion cheaply (design flag for the user). Fed into the sparta-diagnosis task.
- **The re-pin tool landed (eca157ed).** Tape pins now live in crates/sim/tests/pins.json, and tools/sim/repin.sh regenerates the fixtures and pins in one go. On master, repin.sh reproduced the prior hard-coded hashes exactly (zero drift), confirming it's a faithful replacement. A merge conflict in these files is now settled by taking either side and running repin.sh.
- **The Playwright bridge landed (2b44c95e) and its daemon is running.** Codex tasks can now run Playwright through tools/ui/pw-request.sh, with results and screenshots in .progress/pw-bridge/results/<id>/. Codex UI work no longer has to wait for the lead to run browser checks. The daemon must be started each session; it's in the lead's memory notes.
- **ResizeObserver self-observation loops are WebKit-visible only.** VpTrack's row-fit effect observed the element its own callback resizes. Chromium stayed quiet; WebKit raised page errors (4 celebrate.spec failures). Never observe the element a ResizeObserver callback resizes. Found at landing because the Codex sandbox has no browser (fixed in 6724d8c2). Also from the user's Sparta playthrough: the early military edge, conquest as economy and the overall identity all landed. Healing at 2 HP/turn was the main pain ('one attack and they're out of commission'). An edgier option, no healing at all with healing by capture or kills, is proposed and awaiting the user's decision.
- **Kill-healing must come after deaths.** Under snapshot resolution, any per-kill reward (Sparta's +100 HP) must be granted after the stage's damage is applied and dead units are removed. Otherwise a unit killed in a mutual exchange could be 'healed back' by the kill it scored (the user caught this). The same rule applies to any future on-kill effect.
- **Codex 'Selected model is at capacity' kills tasks mid-edit** (sparta-blood-healing, 2026-10-04 17:55; seen before in several logs). The runner now re-queues a task that dies with a capacity error (up to 3 tries, 10-minute back-off), instead of filing it as a failure. The branch and worktree keep the partial work.

## 2026-10-04 — `WorldBackdrop`'s decorative `PlayerView` has no `players` array; `TerrainCache` code must guard for it
Building the Japan root-veins/spire art (`app/src/map/hive.ts`, baked into `terrain.ts`'s `drawTowns`), `TerrainCache.update()` reading `view.players` unconditionally (`new Set(view.players.filter(...))`, to find which owners play Japan) broke every screen-tour test that starts at the title or lobby screen: `WorldBackdrop.tsx` builds its fixed decorative map with `world = { width, height, tiles, cities, units: [], me: 0 } as unknown as PlayerView` — no `players` field at all, cast through `unknown` to dodge the type check — and feeds it straight into `new TerrainCache(view, ...)`. The crash ("Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')") only ever surfaced as every title/lobby/new-game test failing `watchErrors`' "no uncaught exceptions" check, not as a Japan-specific failure, because the backdrop mounts behind the title and setup screens generally, not just when Japan is picked. Fixed with `(view.players ?? [])`. The existing Switzerland-bastion lookup at the same call site (`view.players.find(...)`) has the identical latent hole, just never hit because the backdrop's cities are never walled. Lesson: any new `terrain.ts` code touching `view.players` must tolerate it being absent, since the title-screen backdrop is a real (if minimal) `PlayerView` consumer, not a toy; run the full `screen-tour.spec.ts`, not just the scenario you're adding, before trusting a terrain-layer change.
- **Campaign AI step 1: mixed.** Over 100 matched Standard games, abandoned sieges went 121→107 and favourable peace offers 78→39, but engine bankruptcy disbands went 13→209. Campaigns kept armies the treasury couldn't pay for. Commitment without funding just moves the failure. A campaign-funding fix (reserve ledger: Gold runway, then fund, assault or make peace before the engine disbands) is queued ahead of landing.
- **layout.spec.ts never tested the 1000x600 hard constraint.** Its sizes start at 1100x700, and the screen tour only screenshots 1000x600 without checking for overflow. The faction-sheet agent added a real 1000x600 overflow test, which caught Sparta's sheet overflowing by 73 px. Other 'fits the window' claims probably have the same gap; add 1000x600 to layout assertions when touching them.
- **The attack-path detour was a client preview bug** (app/src/path.ts), from the user's turn 38. previewRoute blocked every tile any pending friend would step on, but core only lets a lower-id friend's step this round take a tile first (movement.rs round declare). And re-issuing an order reused the unit's own stale path whenever the destination matched (commands.ts moveSelected). Lessons: the client preview must reserve tiles exactly as core declares them, and order creation must leave out the unit's own old order. To reproduce a live-game bug, replay the tape and test order *sequences*, not just the final orders. Fixed in 18a7bc85.
- **Production banking landed (fdcb3b27).** Two branches had written their own productionStallText; banking's 'drops to population X' was wrong, because available population is counted after growth. The landing kept the accurate wording plus banking's 'stays banked' clause. The opening-race baseline on the merged tree matched the branch (median 340, 25/50 wins).
- **Split counterattack and overflow are implemented (dce745d6).** The counterattack is computed once, against the strongest melee attacker (the lowest retaliation value; a judgement call), and split with the remainder going to the strongest. "Already fought back this turn" is read from the turn's shared event log, so any new caller that passes a fresh events vector mid-turn would allow a second counterattack. Overflow uses the snapshot's garrison defense, so city damage is applied first. A garrison stepping out of the city that round is exempt, matching the existing rule. Rush probe: rush-offense captured in 50/50 runs vs 44/50, about a turn faster; rush-defense held 50/50 both ways. No scenario yet tests a rush against walls. Also: cached-baseline.sh passes --label and --out-dir, which `legatum-sim scenario` rejects, so call the cached master binary directly for scenario A/B runs.
- **Sparta blood healing done (2980585b).** Probe on 200 games: win rate 1.5% → 3.5%, median first capture T107 → T93.5, captures 0.74 → 0.92 per game, worst-faction ratio 20.3 → 8.7 (Mongols 30.5% unchanged). The hidden cause of the passivity: AI-wide 60 HP "recover first" thresholds permanently benched wounded units for a faction that can't rest-heal. Every Settler paying +50% moves the Sparta first Settler from about T15 to about T23. Two general fixes came with it. Chromium sends no hover events to disabled buttons, so their tooltips never opened; a styles.css rule now passes the pointer through. And a shared sccache server started inside a Codex sandbox couldn't write worktree target/ dirs ("error writing dependencies … Operation not permitted"); restart sccache outside the sandbox, or use RUSTC_WRAPPER= as a fallback.
- **Campaign funding fixed the bankruptcy regression (2e4a96f1).** Root cause: settle_insolvency let the engine choose whenever covering a deficit took several units, and a structural deficit repeats, so the engine disbanded the costliest unit every turn (978 engine disbands at any distance, against 68 on master). The fix is a reserve ledger: Gold runway with a floor of 4 turns at Standard, checked before diplomacy; production switches toward Gold; unfunded purchases are vetoed; cheap units far from the front are trimmed deliberately; a campaign continues only if capture lands inside the runway. 100 matched games: bankruptcy near cities 13→6, front disbands at war 428→178, favourable peace 78→37, abandoned sieges 121→118 (noise; most now follow unit deaths, not money). Replay of the user's Glass at the Gate: the attacker captures Hymnal at T24 and stays solvent. Lesson: compare AI cuts against what the engine does *repeatedly*, not once.
- **Influence removal landed (4578d4ad), with 11 conflicted files.** Lesson: when a merge deletes a whole UI subsystem, trace the call sites of anything kept from the other side (BorderDelay lived only inside the deleted Influence/Pact UI). And never take 'ours' mechanically for fixtures or scenario files: two still held pre-removal orders (Pact proposals) with stale hashes, which rehash_fixtures caught. One-line treaty definitions matter at 1000x600: a 3-clause Alliance definition pushed Accept and Decline below the fold. A WebKit menu-close-mid-click bug remains on 'Reset hints' (same class as Exit to title), filed as a separate task.
- **`e2e/layout.spec.ts`'s `SIZES` (1100x700, 1280x800, 1440x900) never actually exercise the user's laptop (1000x600).** Building the TI4-style faction picker (claude/faction-sheets), every size in that array passed while the real 1000x600 overflowed the Sparta sheet by 73px internally (`scrollHeight - clientHeight`) — 1100x700 alone gives a fixed-height dialog 100px more room than 600 does. `screen-tour.spec.ts` does take 1000x600 screenshots, but `shot()` only records layout-audit findings for the reviewer; it never asserts on them. Added a dedicated `1000x600` test to layout.spec.ts that checks every faction's sheet for zero internal scroll, since that's the one size this project's "fits the window" tests were silently skipping. Any future "fits the window" assertion should include the literal 1000x600 case, not just sizes larger than it.
- **Expansion landed (52f797e2) under the functional-only gate.** It had failed only the old balance limits (Switzerland 0/50, Mongols 25/50). A blocked git reset in the landing worktree turned out not to matter: under the new policy the 'abandoned' merge was exactly the commit to land, so nothing had to be discarded. Before destroying work to retry, check whether a policy decision makes the existing work landable.
- **The user's Byzantium game, 132 turns, 7a-era build.** Human Byzantium techs by turn: 4 at T50, 9 at T100, 13 at T131 (Science 46/turn, top). The AI Byzantium led tech from ONE city (10 techs at T75, 12 at T100) until it was eliminated by T125. AI expansion is still the glaring gap: Mongols 1 city all game, most AIs 1–3 cities at T130, the human 9–10. Coalitions formed against the human leader as designed. War micromanagement fatigue started around T130.
- **Settler risk is a judgement, not a rule** (user, 2026-10-04): the human sent unescorted Settlers only toward areas with no other players' units, and captured exposed AI Settlers opportunistically. The playtest-8 AI spec now prices trip risk from visible threats and adds opportunistic Settler captures.
- **Landing split-counterattack-and-overflow (dce745d6, into c113b388/23d1a8a7): a test's independent tape replay must mirror production's event-attribution logic, not just its event *counts*.** `sim_metrics.rs`'s `instrumented_metrics_match_replayed_tapes` replays each tape itself and compares the result to the live report, to catch instrumentation drift. It tracked `PlayerEliminated` as bare `{player, turn}`, while `runner.rs::observe_events` also back-scans the turn's earlier events for a `CityCaptured`/`CityRazed` naming who did it, and stamps that onto `Elimination.by` (an existing field, from before this branch, `skip_serializing_if` empty so it rarely showed up). This branch's new split/overflow damage was the first thing in this fixture's history to put a capture event immediately before an elimination in the same turn, so `by` populated for the first time and the test's hand-rolled version silently fell behind. Fixed by giving the test's replay loop the identical backward scan. Lesson: when a test reimplements production logic to get an independent check, a passing test for years doesn't mean the two stayed in sync — it can mean the divergent code path never fired yet.
- **Campaign funding landed (73b509fd); the hardest merge of the day.** The branch predated banking, the Influence removal and expansion. New files can't show merge conflicts, so `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` was essential: it caught new modules built against removed Pact, Influence and trust APIs. Archived Pact *relations* were mapped to Peace, not Alliance, so empires weren't falsely pre-allied. The Glass at the Gate replay on the merged tree still captures Hymnal at T24, solvent throughout. Lesson: after merging a long-lived branch across an API removal, always run a full all-targets check, not just the tests.
- **Goal-driven AI step 2 (claude/p8-goalai): fewer, better wars.** Hard now picks one plan (Economy/Peace, Campaign, Contain, Snipe) by its change in a fitted chance-to-win estimate. On 100 held-out Standard games against master: abandoned sieges 134→67, favourable peace 53→20, wartime disbands near cities 174→57, wars declared 2,514→753, captures 806→400 (captures per war doubled), cities per seat at T100 2.70→2.79, zero plan switches without a reason. Details: docs/sim-results/2026-10-04-goal-driven-ai-step2.md.
- **The siege forecast overstates new wars; calibrate it on observed captures.** New wars priced at 61%+ took the city only 38% of the time, 41–60% only 11%, and marches judged by army strength alone almost never (13 of 592). Fix: marches use the same siege rollout from their assault tiles, and odds are corrected to (raw − 30) × 1.2; on held-out seeds 41–60% then took 52% and ≤40% took 21%. A first correction overshot (captures halved) — check the correction on a cohort it wasn't fitted on.
- **In the fitted win estimate, Gold barely matters.** The economy title share dominates (8 logits per full share) and the runway shortfall weighs −0.08. So the estimate can't stop a plan from draining the treasury; the plan needs explicit gates (no campaign on a runway under the floor unless its capture comes first). A campaign plan that committed a wider force than the local ring also blocked the siege clock's pre-emptive cut and led to an engine bankruptcy disband in the Glass at the Gate replay: reverted.
- **"Avoid every tile a rival could reach" strands Settlers next to rivals.** Hard marks rival reach as Settler danger; a Settler caught inside it found no safe route and held, turn after turn, beside the army that could take it (183 of 188 surprise snipes in one cohort). Holding is the worst choice there: head for the nearest city.
- **Rubber-banding wars need a reachable enemy.** Pricing a containment war by "VP denied to the leader" made every seat declare on whoever led (5,396 wars, 2,627 reversed) until denial required armies within 15 hexes of the target and the current containment target stayed on offer while the war lasted. The 2%-of-target denial per horizon is still an assumption, not a measurement.
- **`Tip.tsx`'s `placeBubble` only keeps a bubble clear of the top bar for the `bottom` placement.** `Bubble`'s `viewport.top` (the minimum `top` a bubble may use) is set to the top bar's bottom edge only when the trigger sits *outside* the top bar; for a trigger that lives inside it (e.g. the Science stat), `viewport.top` is just the 8px gap, so a `left`/`right` fallback can float the bubble up over the top bar itself. Found adding the Science hover's multi-line source list (G-science-hover): marking the unit panel `data-tip-avoid` (so a tall hover wouldn't cover the selected unit's name/HP at 1000x600) pushed `placeBubble` to pick `right` instead of `bottom`, which then clipped into the top bar's own Turn counter — a worse overlap than the one being fixed. Reverted rather than fix the general case; a top-bar trigger's tall hover is left to overlap whatever panel sits below it at narrow widths. A real fix would clamp `top` to the top bar's bottom edge for every placement when the trigger is inside it, not just `bottom`.
- **Restarting Claude with agents mid-flight** (21:45): background agents die but their worktrees persist on disk, uncommitted files included, so a mid-merge state survives. Before restarting, have each agent commit WIP and report its exact next steps, save those in resume files (.progress/*RESUME.md and the handoff doc), then respawn fresh agents in the same worktrees. Services started with nohup (pw-bridge, reaper, disk-watch, sccache) survive; session crons don't.
- **Sparta kill-heal missed overflow kills.** Participants were collected only from Battle events with a unit defender. Garrison damage from combined-assault overflow is recorded as a hit on the city, so a garrison killed through the walls healed nobody (unless a capture's full heal covered it). Decision: overflow garrison kills count, shared by everyone who hit the city tile that stage. Lesson: when one rule changes how damage is attributed (overflow), audit every rule that reads those events (kill-heal, kill Gold, XP).
- **Laya teacher data without Codex:** gen-data.sh hard-wired the Codex deciders. LAYA_LLM_CMD and LAYA_ESCALATE_CMD now override them, so Claude (claude-decider.sh with Sonnet 5.5, escalating to Opus 5.5) can teach while Codex is out of budget. The first Sonnet-taught batch (4 games) and an MPS fine-tune started overnight on 2026-10-04 (~/LegatumRuns/laya/overnight.log).

## 2026-10-05 — Reuse a sibling branch's conflict resolution when landing
Landing blood-healing on top of split-counterattack conflicted in 17 files. The reinforce branch had already merged the same two sides (2b01d4e9), and our side matched its pre-merge side in every file, so the landing took reinforce's resolution file by file (`git checkout 2b01d4e9 -- <file>`) instead of re-resolving. Before resolving a big conflict by hand, check whether another in-flight branch has merged the same pair. Diff each side against that branch's parents first; reuse is only safe where they're identical. Separately, the screen-tour spec matched report text case-sensitively and broke when a captured-city report began "Its counterattack…". Match report prose case-insensitively.

## 2026-10-04 — Reinforcing your own city goes first (claude/reinforce-priority)

- **Built as a pre-fight step inside `movement_round`, not a new phase.** After declare and classify (and the Mongols claim and swap passes), `reinforcements()` picks, per city tile, the lowest-id non-ranged military unit of the city's owner that makes a plain move into it, when no military unit holds the tile and an enemy melee attack (`Attack(City)`) targets it. That unit is moved at once (pos, step cost, `UnitMoved` then the new `CityReinforced` event), `occ` is updated, and enemy `Attack(City)` intents at 0 HP are rewritten to `Attack(Unit(garrison))`. Everything after (contested ruins, overflow, the capture rules) then sees an ordinary garrison, so no other rule needed a special case. Limiting it to threatened cities means a peaceful move into your own city is untouched, which kept the determinism tapes and every pinned hash unchanged.
- **Three older tests encoded the rule being replaced** (`movement_contention_tests.rs`: f12 incoming defender, mutual kill plus two own survivors, teammates' HP after a contested ruin). They asserted a meeting engagement between an incoming defender and the attacker; now it is a melee against the garrison. If a future change makes a test like these fail, check whether it was written for the old "both claim the ruin" behaviour before treating it as a regression.
- **A unit an enemy attacks where it stands this round gets no priority** (it takes the parting hit and completes its step as before). Moving it first would have made the enemy's planned fight at its old tile hit nothing, and handling that cleanly needs a second fight-planning pass. Revisit only if players hit it.
- **The turn-107 save cannot be replayed on current code.** It comes from engine faecae92 (Pacts, Influence), so neither its tape (`unknown variant Pact`) nor its state (`missing field protected_until` after mapping Pact to Peace) loads. The test `the_turn_107_shape_...` rebuilds its geometry (wounded Trooper into a 0 HP city, two Soldiers from the other side) instead. Archive replay of a save only works for saves from the same schema; for older ones, rebuild the shape.
- **Garrison killed by overflow is an Sparta kill** (lead decision): `heal_sparta_killers` now also counts damaging Battle events against the victim's own city tile (`Defender::City` with owner and `at` matching), from any stage this turn. Before, only `Defender::Unit` events counted, so a garrison that died to overflow healed nobody, even though the iron-price gold already counted city-target fights.
- **A pre-7b save fails with a raw serde error, so `loadErrorMessage` now covers it.** Loading the user's 7a autosave on current code throws `invalid saved game: unknown variant Pact` (the title screen showed "Could not load the save: Error: invalid saved game…"). `app/src/saveErrors.ts` now treats "invalid saved game" and "unsupported save version" like "incompatible engine": plain words, and the save file is kept. `app/e2e/old-save.spec.ts` injects a state with a removed treaty kind and checks the title screen. Making 7a saves actually load needs a JSON migration, not just a serde default: Pact to Peace in relations and cooldowns, drop Pact proposals, reshape the alliance `security` record (`minimum_end` becomes `protected_until`), and drop or re-hash the archive. With those patches the 7a autosave loads in the engine (checked offline).

## 2026-10-05 — Removing a rule variant breaks every older save
Removing Pact and Influence made 7a saves fail to load: unknown variant `Pact`, missing `protected_until`, and a reshaped alliance `security` record. The archive can't be replayed either, because its engine commit and rules fingerprint differ. Until the reinforce branch, the title screen showed the raw serde error. `app/src/saveErrors.ts` now shows a plain "made with an older version" message. Loading a 7a save would need a JSON migration in `crates/wasm/src/json.rs::parse_state`: map Pact to Peace, drop Pact proposals, and map `minimum_end` to `protected_until`. That's about half a day, and the game would continue under the new rules. Before removing an enum variant or a serialized field, decide whether user saves matter for that release, and say so in the release notes. The LAN server's own save-load path still shows the raw error.

## 2026-10-05 — Rule text changes can break the faction-sheet fit
Blood-healing lengthened Sparta's sheet card to three lines, and the sheet overflowed 1000x600 by 9 px. `layout.spec.ts` catches this, but landing 1 ran only the screen tour, so it reached master; landing 2 shortened the text (c591d386). Landing gates now include `layout.spec.ts`.

## 2026-10-05 — macOS bash 3.2 treats an empty array as unbound under `set -u`
The overnight Laya run made 0 teacher decisions. `gen-data.sh` passed `"${options[@]}"` with an empty array, and macOS's /bin/bash 3.2 aborts on that with "unbound variable". The script died in its first second, and the fine-tune then failed with no logs. Expand optional arrays as `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}`. Overnight scripts should check each stage's output (the decision count is 0) and stop with a clear message, not carry on.

## 2026-10-05 — WebKit Playwright aborts under heavy load
During the 7b release check, 41 WebKit tests failed with `browserType.launch … exitCode=134` and click timeouts while the load average was 74 (other landings running). The same build passed 58/58 once re-run at lower load, and Chromium was unaffected. A WebKit failure at a load average above about 40 is load until proven otherwise: re-run that step when the machine is quieter before debugging. Also, a contrast audit must wait for entrance fades: the faction picker measured 1.2:1 mid-fade.

## 2026-10-05 — Goal-driven AI step 2 against the human-playbook benchmark (Proxy v6): not easier, not harder
Landing p8-goalai on top of reinforce-priority and the 7b UI work (200 Standard games, seeds 3600001+, Proxy v6 against 7 Hard AIs, same seeds both sides). Master: the proxy wins 51/200 (25.5%, CI 20.0-32.0%, median winning turn 180), makes 343 captures and loses 457 cities. Merged: 45/200 (22.5%, CI 17.3-28.8%, median 161), 347 captures, 411 cities lost. Both win rates are inside each other's CI, so the plan layer didn't make Hard easier for a human-like player, even though wars fall from 20.9 to 6.7 per game and total city captures from 1,978 to 1,307. The proxy's captures are unchanged (343 vs 347); why isn't established. The AI now takes about 11% fewer cities from the proxy. The sim doesn't record "AI recaptures" separately; cities lost by the proxy is the nearest measure.

## 2026-10-05 — The overnight supervisor never ran: session crons need an idle, living lead
Overnight 2026-10-04→05 the ops supervisor ran 0 times: its last run was 13:08 EDT, and only 1 of about 30 scheduled ticks reached the lead after 13:30. A CronCreate job fires only when the lead session is idle, and the lead was busy with agent hand-backs almost continuously. The Claude app then died at about 23:18 and stayed down until 07:50, so no tick could fire and no agent could resume. Meanwhile the Laya run I launched at 21:49 died in its first second, and I never checked its first output. Fixes: a token-free shell watchdog (`tools/ops/watchdog.sh`) tracks jobs registered via `tools/ops/bgjob.sh` and sends macOS notifications. It doesn't alert when the app is down, because nothing else runs then (user). And the lead checks every background job's first unit of progress within minutes of launching it.

## 2026-10-05 — A title-screen message must live in the menu's flow, and Playwright's scrollIntoViewIfNeeded scrolls the app root
The older-save message was absolutely placed under the menu and overprinted the footer at 1000x600; the menu already had only about 35 px of slack, so it now sits above the buttons, hides the tagline and trims button padding at short heights, and makes Single Player primary while it shows. Separately, `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` on a turn-report line also scrolled the whole app, shifting the screenshot: the tour now scrolls `.report-body` itself (`scrollWithinReport`). A forecast card has `pointer-events: none` and a height cap, so it cannot scroll; the tour now asserts the last line's text box ends inside the card (`expectWhole`).

## 2026-10-05 — Laya with a Claude teacher: hardcoded Codex tier names, and a 73% escalation rate
Once the bash fix was in, the first Sonnet-teacher game recorded 33 decisions. But `gen-data.sh` still accepted only answers labelled `luna`/`sol`, so it rejected the Claude answers and stopped. Training then refused to run, because it needs teacher answers from at least two games for a by-game holdout. The check now accepts any teacher tier, and games already recorded are skipped instead of paid for again. Cost: Sonnet escalated 24 of 33 decisions to Opus, and a Quick game took about 1,100 s, nearly all of it LLM time. Before scaling Laya data, check whether Sonnet-only answers are good enough targets, or tighten the escalation threshold.

## 2026-10-05 — Laya fine-tune "below chance" was the untrained head plus too little training, not a label bug
The first Laya fine-tune scored 12% on the first 100 held-out questions (chance 28%). Round-trip tests (`tools/llm-seat/test_laya_train.py`) show the label mapping is right for choice, score and noul, and the training logits match `system_one`'s. The cause was that the untrained head is anti-correlated with this teacher (23% on all 440 held-out questions, 8% on threat scores), and 300 steps at batch 1 and lr 2e-5 barely moved it: the old checkpoint scores identically to the base on all 440. Reporting only the first 100 questions (all early turns) also hid that: the baselines there are 67% and on the whole game 50% and 54%. With 6+ epochs at batch 8 and lr 1e-4 it reaches about 50%, level with the "most common answer per question family" baseline and below the scripted default (54%); longer training overfits (79% train, 46% held out). Gotchas:
- Evaluate on every held-out question and print chance, per-family majority and scripted baselines every time; a number without them says nothing.
- Calling `agent.model.train()` also turns on dropout in the frozen encoder (the first version did): keep a frozen encoder in `eval()`.
- A frozen encoder's output never changes, so cache it once (the default with a frozen encoder; `--no-cache` turns it off) instead of re-running 400M parameters every epoch. On a busy GPU the one-off cache took 10 minutes; three concurrent MPS jobs make every step several times slower.
- `scripted` on a research or focus question is a tech or city name, while the menu also has a literal `scripted` option meaning "let the scripted AI choose"; both count as agreeing with the scripted AI.
- In zsh, `$VAR` holding several file paths (or a glob) is not split or expanded when passed to a command; use a wrapper script or an array. It cost two failed 10-minute waits here.
- `grep` in a pipeline buffers when its output is a file, so a background run looked stuck for 20 minutes. Use `python -u` and log directly.

## 2026-10-05 — Playwright WebKit crashed macOS WindowServer twice and logged the user out
The two "computer crashes" (2026-10-04 23:17 and 2026-10-05 08:15) were WindowServer aborts. Each one logged the user out and killed every app, the Claude app and all agents included, and about 20 hours of agent time were lost. The 08:15 report shows the request came from a process named "Playwright" (`voucherInfos`), in `_XWindowListCreateImage → CreateCaptureSurface → iosurface_create_common → WSIOSurfaceDebugTallyAndAbort`. WindowServer was holding 46,099 IOSurfaces (55.1 GB) and had been running only since the previous crash. Playwright's WebKit on macOS takes screenshots through WindowServer window capture, even headless. With several agents each running screen tours (about 90 shots per size) in WebKit, the capture surfaces piled up until WindowServer hit its limit. Chromium headless renders off-screen and is unaffected. Fix: `app/playwright.config.ts` refuses WebKit on the macOS host unless `LEGATUM_ALLOW_HOST_WEBKIT=1`. Only `tools/release/check.sh` sets it, with 1 worker. Agent and landing gates use Chromium only.

## 2026-10-05 — Icon pass: a test stops family-icon reuse coming back
The art audit found tiers reusing a family icon (Reactor was the Workshop, Embassy the Monument) and `■` falling back for War Shrine, because `icons.ts` aliased tiers to their family. The alias map is gone and `unitIconName`/`buildingIconName` (in `data.ts`) resolve a faction piece by its own name (`building-customsbastion`), so a new unit, building or faction replacement with no SVG fails `src/icons.test.ts` instead of silently showing a neighbour. The set is solid silhouettes with knocked-out detail (the README said monoline, which only one file was). Drawing gotchas: a shape plus its holes must be one `evenodd` path (overlapping solids in one path cancel), touching parts need a 0.2 overlap or a seam shows when scaled. Two first drafts read as the wrong thing (the Legionary shield with a bolt looked like a battery, the Oathbearer great helm like a tombstone), so check every new icon at 16 px before keeping it. Replacing the text glyphs changed `textContent` that tests asserted (`'▼1 bad'`, `'✓ Ready'`), so those now assert the icon element instead.

## 2026-10-05 — IOSurface leak follow-up: one clean WebKit run doesn't leak
Measured with `ioclasscount IOSurface` (baseline about 400–650, with ±200 noise from other apps). 40 WebKit screenshots then a clean close: no growth. 40 screenshots then SIGKILL of the browser: no clear growth at this scale either. So a single run, clean or killed, isn't the leak. The 46k build-up came from something about the night's volume: many parallel agents' tours, and WebKit processes aborting under load (`exitCode=134` at load 74). It wasn't reproduced. The watchdog now logs the IOSurface count every 5 minutes (`.progress/jobs/iosurface.log`) and alerts at 10k. That gives evidence for when it climbs, and a warning long before WindowServer's limit.

## 2026-10-05 — A forecast-feasible campaign can still never begin, so a seat-declared war can sit on paper
The plan layer's `campaign_forecast` (a siege rollout over the units in reach) and the campaign's own start gate (`campaign_can_take`, over units within 4 hexes, plus "no new campaign while the army holds a captured city") disagree. Forcing a seat-chosen war into the plan on a bare forecast gave 3 paper wars in 6, all at 12% capture odds or less; the plan dropped them within 2 to 23 turns and the war ended in peace. The seat's war options now require capture odds of at least 15%, no held captured city, and (for a force already in reach) the campaign's own gate (`Planner::campaign_against`). Forced wars usually price negative in the plan's own terms (value -30 to -180): the seat may choose a bad war, but never a war that cannot start.

## 2026-10-05 — The PlayerView has no events: infer own losses, finished items and peace from turn-to-turn diffs
The LLM seat sees only the PlayerView, which carries no event log, so the verification's advice to "show losses from the events" cannot be followed literally. `SeatMemory::observe_changes` diffs consecutive views instead (own units gone, `producing` Some to None, research current to None, War to Peace) and names the cause heuristically. A city with `producing: None` at turn start has just finished an item or was just founded; the scripted AI queues the next one in the same turn's orders, so the briefing must say that rather than "builds nothing".

## 2026-10-05 — `laya_plan_trace` needs a single-game decisions file
The multi-game warlike run writes all games' decisions into one JSONL, and the tool keys directives by turn, so games overwrite each other (78 order differences). Filter the file to one `game_id` first; then the replay matches the tape exactly (0 differences in 148 turns).

## 2026-10-05 — An LLM teacher's "bug reports" mostly describe its briefing, not the game
Of the Laya teacher's top bug claims, only one was a real behaviour bug: paper wars. Under the Hard plan layer a campaign starts only from the plan (`campaign.rs:285`), so wars the LLM seat declared were never fought. The rest came from the seat's text briefing:
- turn-start "builds nothing" and "Research: none" on the turn after a completion;
- no barbarians in "seen near us";
- the Sparta desertion drawback missing from the faction text;
- `SeatMemory` recording declarations but never peace;
- the army line dropping Settlers and Scouts.

The teacher only sees a snapshot every 5 turns, so one-turn states read as long idle spells. Lesson: before filing an LLM's finding as a game bug, replay the game from its recorded answers (`tools/llm-seat/replay-decider.py`) and check the events. Fix briefing gaps before generating training data, or the student learns from mislabelled states. Report: `.reviews/laya-findings-verify-2026-10-05.md`.
## 2026-10-05 — The tech unlock card: four gotchas
Building the unlock card (branch `claude/p8-tech-unlock`) turned up four things worth keeping. (1) `celebrate/moments.ts` is imported by Playwright specs, which run in plain Node and can't load SVG or other asset imports, so everything it imports must stay asset-free: `unlockCard.ts` reaches `ui/techCardUnlocks.ts`, which took `YIELD_KEYS` from `bits.tsx` (SVG imports) and broke every spec until those moved to `ui/yieldKeys.ts`. (2) The e2e specs serve `app/dist`, so a screenshot taken without `npx vite build` shows the previous CSS: a z-index fix looked like it had failed until the rebuild. (3) A `position: fixed` card inside the moment lane is still painted in the lane's stacking context (z-index 4), under the right and bottom docks; the lane itself needs the higher z-index (`:has(.moment-card.unlock)`). (4) `itemDescription` drops a Byzantium Archive's "+2 border growth" (the Byzantium gets no Archive Science, so the gains list is empty and the text starts with ". No Science"); the card's sentence rebuilds it from `BUILDING_STATS`, but the tooltip text still has the bug. Also: a research finishes at most once per empire per turn, so there is at most one unlock card per turn and no card queue is needed; and the tech sting is now `sting.major` because the card is tier major.

## 2026-10-05 — Unlock card review: held cards, hidden panels still "in view"
Following the UI review, the unlock card is now held until its own controls, Esc or Return close it (`interrupt` is a no-op while it is up, because the map, the unit panel and the report all call it on gestures), and it waits out any open `<dialog>` instead of hiding behind it: a modal dialog makes everything outside it inert, so a top-layer card could not be clicked, hence deferral through a MutationObserver on `dialog[open]`. Two traps: an IntersectionObserver still reports a city card as "in view" when a modal research panel covers it, so unseen marks keep clearing behind the panel (a tour test that re-set the set while the city panel was mounted raced with that; deselect first), and a sticky city head means an auto-scroll must align the list to the head's bottom edge, not use `scrollIntoView`, which put "Choose what X builds" half under the head. Pinned cards in the Just unlocked group already carry the same text as normal cards (same `renderOption`, tested): building descriptions are one short line, only units add upkeep.

## 2026-10-05 — Reward emblems: the engraving mask eats later shapes, and the lost-city card never shows
Art pass 2 gave each reward kind its own emblem (`app/src/assets/rewards/`, generator `rewards/src/build-rewards.mjs`, kit shared with the seals in `heraldry/src/kit.mjs`). Two gotchas. (1) In the `Seal` canvas an engraved `cut`/`cutFill` removes everything drawn before AND after it unless the later shape has a `halo`; a cornerstone star and a half-tone face both vanished until given `halo: 1`. (2) A lost city never shows its lane card: the alarm screen announces it first and the story filters it, so only the report line exists; fixtures for it time out waiting for `.moment-card`. Also: the standard fixture's two players are on one team, so a "captured" or "lost" fixture needs a third empire (player 2) as the other side. The camp card's gain list is now data on the moment (`Moment.gains`, icon names only, so `moments.ts` stays asset-free for the Node-side Playwright specs); at 1000x600 the explanatory detail lines are hidden to fit, gains stay.


## 2026-10-05 — Population is territory (claude/p8-territory): the rules, the retune and what broke
- **Rules as built.** A city works every owned tile within 3 hexes; each population above 1 claims one tile, nearest ring first and the best by focus within a ring (user: "nearest first, prioritizing quality"; also beyond 3, where tiles are claimed but unworked and hatched on the map). Losing population releases the worst unworked tile, else the latest. Buying is limited to tiles within 3 hexes, any order, priced `base × 100/125/150%` by ring (`tile_price`; the base is 20 + 10 per tile gained, speed-scaled). The former border-growth sources became Food (accepted).
- **The opening got far faster, and the spread wider.** Working all of ring one at population 1 took a 48-game Hard Standard probe (seed 9100, 60 turns) to a median first Settler at T11 and second city at T17 (target T18/T25). Levers, in probes: capital +0 Production and 65% first Settler T12/T19; capital +0 and 100% T16/T23 (30 Food first growth) or T18/T24 (45); capital +2, 100%, T17/T23 at 60 Food, T19/T25 at 75. Shipped: capital +2 kept, first Settler full price, first growth 65 Food: Standard T18/T24, Quick T16/T23. Dropping the capital's +2 looked tidy but left grassland-only capitals at 3 Production (a Settler in 25 turns at Quick). Start Production now spans 5 to 14 by terrain (it was 5 to 6), because the whole ring is worked: expect bad-start complaints, and consider a Production floor that scales or a start-fairness rule in mapgen.
- **Forecasts hold territory fixed.** The growth and tall-empire forecasts don't add the tile a growth will claim, so they undershoot growth slightly. Tests that compare a forecast to real resolution must box the city in (own every other tile), or the real city grows faster than forecast.
- **Fixtures whose premise was the old rules.** (1) Archived states: `border_progress` is gone and `grown_tiles` is new, so their re-serialized hashes changed; the pins in campaign_memory, defense_retreat, scout_threats, settler_threats and ranged_garrison moved, with a note in each. (2) Archived PlayerViews carry old city-detail fields: `escort-t168-t170.json.gz` was migrated (border fields dropped, new ones empty). (3) Scenario files embed a state with a checked hash: `cargo run --release -p legatum-sim --example rehash_scenarios -- scenarios/*.json` re-encodes them (baselines untouched). (4) A hazard fixture's geometry moved on its own: a rival city that grows now claims ring 2 toward the settler and puts a foreign border in its sight, so `settler_threats` keeps its rival city in resistance (resisting cities neither grow nor claim). (5) Counterfactual replays diverge sooner now (a unit built earlier, a treasury shortfall): the replays drop what no longer applies and say why.
- **AI site scoring.** `site_potential` and `site_strategic` scan the 37-tile work radius, ring 3 at half weight (each yield halved, rounded down), foreign tiles still -8 each, so scores run about 1.5x higher than before and `settler_min_site_score` (60, an evolved gene) is now a looser bar. Not re-tuned: no balance sims while the AI is weak. Pinned in the proxy v2 test (36 plains x 7 - 8).
- **Mock parity is mostly free if the mock ports whole functions.** `settle_territory`, `next_claim`, `next_release`, `tile_price` and the buy gate were ported one-to-one and the WASM parity tests (diplomacy, purchases, resources, ruins) passed after assertion updates; the cost was in fixtures that hard-coded `borderProgress`.

## 2026-10-06 — The Monument and Assembly are cut; what the old border sources became (claude/p8-territory)
- **The user rejected "everything becomes Food"** (an Archive giving Food didn't fit); the lead decided the rest: the Japan keeps Food (Brood Hall +2, resonance +1); the **Archive** is +3 Science; **Civic Networks** is "bought tiles cost 25% less" (a percent in `tile_price`, shown in the price breakdown); **Public Administration** makes a new city claim its best ring-2 tile (by the growth order, not counted in `grown_tiles`, so never released, and no `tiles_claimed`); **Soil Reclamation** is +1 Food in every city and the **Granary** needs no tech (buildable turn 1). Monument and Assembly are gone everywhere. Public Administration is a prerequisite (Closed Habitats, Federated Markets), so it was never a dead end.
- **Brood Hall as its own variant.** `BuildingKind::BroodHall` replaces `Monument` (`#[serde(alias = "Monument")]` so old states, orders and fixtures still load); `available_to_faction` makes it Japan-only. Anything that used the Monument as "the cheap neutral building" (tests, the AI's pre-Settler filler, the Switzerland' recommended opening) now uses the Granary. The AI filler order is now Scout (only if none), Granary / Brood Hall, and a Soldier only as the last resort (the Soldier at 40 would otherwise beat a 50-Production Granary and cost Switzerland 3 Gold a turn).
- **Dropping the Monument shrank the Germany's goal to five ordinary buildings** (`ORIGINAL_BUILDING_FAMILIES`: Granary, Workshop, Market, Laboratory, Walls). Faction text says "all five".
- **An effect that is only Science is "does nothing" for the Byzantium**: the Archive (+3 Science only) briefly became faction-unavailable for them (it had been available through its +1 Food), which would have locked them out of the Relay Uplink (it needs an Archive). The lead's call: no building that does nothing, so the Archive stays unavailable to the Byzantium and `data::great_work_requirement_for(faction, building)` drops the Archive requirement from the Byzantium's Relay Uplink (core `building_blocker`, the AI's `investment.rs` plan and the mock all use it; `great_work_requirement` stays the faction-blind base). Note `building_blocker`'s Great Work checks (one per empire, already done) must not hang off the requirement: a `None` requirement used to skip them.
- **Opening pace did not move** (48 Hard games, seed 9100, 60 turns): first Settler T18 and second city T24 at Standard (T16/T23 Quick), the same as before the cut, so the first-growth cost stayed at 65 Food. The Granary is buildable at once but the AI rarely benefits early.
- **Fixture fallout.** The serialized name changed (`Monument` to `BroodHall`), so every archived-state hash pin moved again (campaign_memory, defense_retreat, scout_threats, settler_threats, ranged_garrison, attack_opportunism; the stored hashes in settler-cleared-goto, settler-detour-loop and rush-defense-t21-t29-orders were rewritten). `Assembly` can't load at all, so it was stripped from the two AI view fixtures (listing/unlock entries and building lists); a serde alias can't map a removed building to a different one. Scenario states re-encoded with `rehash_scenarios`. Bare sims need `tools/sim/repin.sh` for the tapes.
- **The AI fixture builder lists items by tech only**, so it offered the Brood Hall to every faction (the Switzerland picked it); `ViewBuilder::detail` now filters it with `available_to_faction`. Similar silent assumptions will bite the next faction-only item.

The watchdog's IOSurface log showed 248 (23:52), 1,474 (23:57), 25,484 (00:02) and 32,262 (00:06), then flat. Over that window the release check ran its single-worker WebKit step (23:52–23:56) and the Tauri bundle (23:56–00:03), and the ChatGPT app started its computer-use node servers at 00:00 (screen capture also goes through `_XWindowListCreateImage`). ## 2026-10-06 — City-built improvements (branch claude/p8-improvements): what was not obvious
- **A new `ProductionItem` variant compiles but is silently wrong where code matches `Unit | Building` by hand.** `City::holds_progress`, `switch_production` and the BuyItem "carry the bank" branch listed the two old kinds explicitly, so an Improvement's progress counted as unassigned Production and switching away lost its bank. Rust's exhaustiveness check can't see `matches!` lists; the banking and purchase tests in `crates/core/src/improvements/tests.rs` caught it. Search for `ProductionItem::Building {` in `matches!`/`if let` before trusting a clean build.
- **`#[serde(tag = "kind")]` forbids a variant field called `kind`**: the item is `Improvement { improvement, tile }`, mirrored as `{ kind: 'Improvement'; improvement; tile }` in TypeScript. The tile rides in the item (so queue, bank, order and event all name it) and the kind is redundant but validated against the tile's resource.
- **Capture keeps improvements** (lead, 2026-10-06; the first build cleared them): Civ-familiar and conquest is the core loop. Razing, release and founding on the tile still clear them.
- **Strategic stockpile income deliberately ignores improvement.** Requiring a Mine would orphan deposits beyond the 3-hex work radius (they can never be improved), so owning a known deposit is still enough and the Mine only adds the tile's yield. Revisit if Mines should gate Trooper and Siege Engine supply.
- **Claim and release scoring keep valuing a resource at its improved worth** (`owner_tile_potential`); only the worked yields, the claim preview and the yields lens show what the tile gives now. Otherwise claims stop leaning toward resources the moment improvement is required.
- **Mock/WASM parity fixtures need three teams.** A two-empire fixture whose players share a team ends the game on turn 2 by elimination victory ("The game is over") even though both engines agree; use a third empire on its own team (`improvements.wasm.test.ts`). A release test that needs population to stay put sets `resistance` (no growth), because a full ring-3 city grows every turn.
- **Opening pace** (48 Hard Standard games, seed 9100, 60 turns, `OPENING_TURNS=60 opening_pacing`): first Settler T19, second city T26, against T18/T24 before. 160 of 384 empires had an improvement among their first six builds (median turn 23: Farm 86, Pasture 41, Quarry 33, no Mines), so the AI builds them after its first Settler, as intended. 50-game Standard Hard smoke: 0 panics, 0 stalls, all finished, 24 of 400 empires never founded a second city (6%). Not balanced; the pace shift is the cost of paying 30 Production before a Wheat tile's Food counts.
- **Art lessons.** The first sprite pass read as a technical diagram (thin single strokes, rectangles); what made it read as engraving was hatching on the shadow side of every cut (furrows, quarry walls, hillside), irregular outlines instead of ruled ones, and a tonal wash under the line, all at the hill pen weight. Check the art at high zoom first (a throwaway Playwright spec at camera zoom 3), then at the real tiers. The mine's base must sit well inside the hex (the clip cut the adit off at first). A tooltip on the picker row covered the very tile the hover was lighting, so improvement rows carry none.

## 2026-10-06 — Art pass 3 (map): what the shots taught
- **A stale `app/src/wasm-pkg` makes 183 vitest tests fail** (`BUILDING_STATS[...]` undefined in every `*.wasm.test`) and looks like a regression. Run `LEGATUM_WASM_NO_OPT=1 scripts/build-wasm.sh` (35 s) in a worktree before trusting vitest; `cargo build --release -p legatum-server` and `npm run build` before the e2e gate.
- **Translucent strokes drawn per piece double up where pieces overlap**, which is exactly what made the Japan roots look like beads and barbs. Fill every piece of one object as a single path (nonzero rule) and set the alpha once.
- **Label de-collision must not depend on which labels are on screen**, or names pop in and out while panning. It depends on zoom only; offscreen labels still take part in the greedy pass.
- **Seat colour as a tint**: the UI's seat colours mixed 30% with umber keep their hue and all eight stay at least 38 RGB units apart (`seatColors.test.ts`); a parchment plate with a seat-colour rim reads at a glance, the old solid fills did not sit in the atlas palette.
- **`e2e/art-map.spec.ts` + `src/test/mapArtFixture.ts`** give a busy, deterministic map (eight empires, camps, ruins, resources, a Settler) for before/after shots at normal and far zoom; the fixture's `free()` must read the live state, not the pre-found-city one, or units stack on one hex.
