## 2026-10-19: a quick type check in a worktree without node_modules
- **A box verify's local log folder can hold the previous run's logs** (`.progress/verify-remote/<branch>/steps/` still showed yesterday's PASS files while the summary said `app-tsc FAIL`), so read the summary, not the folder. To find a TypeScript error in seconds: symlink the main checkout's `app/node_modules` into the worktree's `app/`, run `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p .` with Node 22, ignore the `wasm-pkg` "Cannot find module" lines (the WASM package isn't built there), then remove the symlink. Here it was an unused import left by a merge.

## 2026-10-20: the slot-queue test failed only on the box
- **`tools/cloud/box/tests/test-slot-queue.sh` exited 1 on the 64-core box (and passed on the Mac) because it waited for two ticket files.** The second waiter deletes a killed waiter's ticket as soon as it runs, which on a fast machine happens before the 50 ms poll sees two files, so the count never reached 2. The test now waits for `next-ticket` to reach 3. The same slow-versus-fast timing difference makes a count-based wait unreliable whenever the code under test cleans up after itself; poll a monotonic counter instead.

- **The Engineer's cover prop spilled half a hex because the gear was placed beside the covered unit, and the unit is already pushed to the hex's right by the stack spread** (`render.ts`: a stack of two spreads +-1.16 token half-widths; the hex is only about 4.4 half-widths wide). Drawing the prop behind the figure fixed the spill but made it vanish: every miniature stands in a soft vellum pool (`MINI.halo`) that washes out anything behind it. It now stands in front of the pair's feet, right-aligned inside the hex (`siegeProps.ts::siegePropRect`, a unit test over seven zoom levels).
- **The same release had a cause that looked like a rule:** see the 8.9.6 T155 entry above. A second card-fitting lesson: at 1000x600 the whole-fight forecast card needed four rounds of shedding lines before the walled, garrisoned, two-attacker case fit; the test that matters is the worst case, not the screen-tour's single-attack one.
- **A "Coming soon" slot outlived its feature twice:** the Scenario Lab's "Waiting for the Military Engineer" card stayed after the Engineer and then the real scenario (`swiss-walls-athens`, "The Walls of Athens") shipped. The slot is deleted; `SOON_SLOTS` is empty and the Lab e2e asserts the real card.
## 2026-10-20: allied cities are transit-only (`astra/allied-city-transit`, landed)
- **Rule:** a unit may pass through an allied city but cannot end its move there (core `movement.rs`/`units.rs`, the TS mock, path preview and reach map, every AI proxy, `game-rules.md` section 1 and 5). Measured on current master plus allied wars: human-seat benchmark (Hard, all seats, 256 salts per map, `LEGATUM_HVH_RESEED_DICE=1`) 42.1% (95% 40.5 to 43.8) against a control of 39.0% (37.3 to 41.0) taken before the allies branch landed, so the difference mixes both rules and shows no loss; war suite check `war-golden-horde-thin` 95% of 64 (floor 30%).

## 2026-10-20: strategic supply replaces the stockpile (increment 1, `claude/strategic-supply`)
- **The AI barely builds the buildings supply gates.** `crates/sim/examples/supply_census.rs` (64 eight-player Standard Hard games): Hard empires have a median 4-5 cities and 0.3 Forges at T150 (0.7 at T250, Factories 0.3, Pikemen about 1). So a deposit's economic value to the AI is small in this increment, and resource wars will matter more once Hard grows wider or the Copper/Silver lines land.
- **Deposits already change hands in AI wars.** 7.3 strategic deposits per game passed with a captured city before the AI valued them, and 8.4 with the valuation (62 of 64 games had at least one; same seeds, though the second run also carried a master merge). Shortages (an idle user) hit 53 empires in 36 of 64 games.
- **The map is already scarce enough:** 11 Iron and 10 Coal deposits per 48x32 map, 1.4 Iron and 1.25 Coal nearest each start. Empires of 8-12 cities hold a median 4-6 Iron supply, so 2-3 of 66-80 such empires could put a Forge in every city. Placement needed no change.
- **Old archives keep the stockpile in their provenance hash.** Tests that check an archived state against its recorded FNV hash (`threat_response`, `attack_opportunism`, `ranged_garrison`) failed once the stockpile fields were dropped. The fix is to splice the old field back into the hashed JSON (`with_stockpile`), not to change the recorded hash, so the fixture still proves it is the user's game. Scenario states are different: they carry their own hash, and `rehash_scenarios` re-encodes them (19 of 26 changed).
- **Builds in progress have to hold supply.** Without that, two cities could each start a Forge with one spare Iron, and one would finish idle. Validation runs city orders in list order, so the second start is refused with its reason. The AI's `supply::within_budget` mirrors this so its orders never fail.
- **Byzantium's levy cap (2) blocks a third Pikeman.** Supply tests that need several Pikemen use another faction.

- **Merge with the Military Engineer (landed first, c86feb376).** The Engineer retired the siege units and added `city_defense_covered` and `city_defense_vs`; the era branch had `era` in every city line. The stale-intel gene had been taken off master (`2d5cff754`), so the branch's copy of it was dropped, not merged. Era duels: one era ahead the melee line wins in three attacks with 51 to 56 HP left until the Renaissance and in two with 81 to 90 from then on; two eras ahead is one blow from the Modern era. War suite check (`war-golden-horde-thin`, 128 runs): 67% against 100% on the 30% curve (floor 30%), so the early Mongol attack is worse on a curve whose first steps are smaller. Only the V7 proxy knew the rule. `ScriptedBrain::orders` now drops a `MoveUnit` that ends in an ally's city.

- **Box habits that cost time.** `cargo test` on the box is nextest in the debug profile, and `runner::tests::opening_league_twenty_standard_games...` takes 18+ minutes there: use `cargo nextest run --workspace --cargo-profile release-checked` (4 minutes). Two AWS spot batches launched in the same minute made the second fail with exit 254; launch one at a time. `verify-remote.sh` run from a worktree writes its logs into that worktree's `.progress/`, and a branch whose `chart.png` or `ledger.jsonl` diverges from master fails the verify merge: take master's chart.

## 2026-10-20: the Mongols raise Walls and train Engineers from the Medieval era (user decision 2026-10-19)
- **How it is built.** Walls are an Ancient technology (Masonry), so the gate is the player's era, not a technology: `data::available_to_player(faction, engineers_absorbed, era, item)` and `faction_excluded_building_at(.., era)` (era 2, `MONGOL_WALLS_ERA`). `available_to_faction` now says yes to the Mongols for the whole line and the Engineer, so a research card lists Walls for them only once their era allows it (the Masonry card, researched in the Ancient era, no longer lists it for them, but `tech_has_benefit` is true for every faction and technology now: Masonry stopped being a stepping stone). The TS mock mirrors it with an `era` argument that defaults to the Medieval era, so a caller that forgets it sees the late-game rule.
- **AI.** The capture bonus for a Workshop city (`mongol_engineer_capture_bonus`, +500) now applies only before the Medieval era, because after it the Engineers can be trained anyway. The Mongol build lists need no code change: the AI builds from the city's option list, which core now fills with the Walls line in the Medieval era.
## 2026-10-20: the Scenario Lab has no "win the game" objective
- **To let the user test "can a human Japan win from T100", the closest objective is `score` over a long window** (`--objective score --turns 150`); `core::scenario::Condition` only has holding cities, city and unit counts, owning a city and a rival's city cap. A normal VP victory still ends the game, so a win shows, but the result card scores VP, not the win. A `WinGame` condition would be the clean fix if more "can you win from here" scenarios come up. The state for an 8.9.6 save played on today's engine came from `extract-state.sh` (replayed on the save's own engine) and `cut.sh --state`, so the scenario runs under the new rules.

## 2026-10-20: armour rules open ground, Tanks get 5 moves (user decision 2026-10-19)
- **Rule as built.** From the Modern era (`combat::ARMOUR_ERA_TIER` 5) the melee line's +18 against mounted applies only while the melee unit stands in a city or on Forest or Hills, attacking or defending; its own tile counts. The era is the melee unit's (Infantry, Humanoid Robot), not the mounted unit's: a Rifleman still has the bonus everywhere. The decision named Jungle, which the game does not have. A meeting engagement has no cover. Where the bonus is lost the breakdown carries a line of 0 ("Open ground: no bonus against armour", added to `Breakdown.parts` directly because `add` drops zeros), so the forecast does not hide it. The unit era chip on the map counts the class bonus but not terrain, so it does not see the rule.
- **Era duels in the open (mean rolls):** Tank against Infantry in the same era now wins in 3 attacks with 51 HP left, and an Infantry attacking a Tank dies after dealing back 29 HP; before, the Tank died. Tank has 5 moves (`data::TANK_MOVES`); the Autonomous Armour keeps 4, which is a step down from its predecessor and worth the user's eye.
- **Benchmark.** Human-seat benchmark (Hard, all seats, 256 salts, reseeded dice): 31.3% on the accelerating curve against 32.0% with this rule (+0.7 pp, CI -0.8 to +2.1): no change.
- **Cover is read, not stored.** `PlayerView::has_cover` (forecast, AI) and `rules::battle::unit_has_cover` (resolution) both read terrain and cities; the AI's `fight_bonuses` takes the view and both positions.

- `data::BOMBER_RANGE` 8 (was 5) and `FIGHTER_STRIKE_RANGE` 5 (was 3); the Fighter's guard radius stays 4, so it now strikes farther than it guards. Card text, ring labels, the Air wing headline and the Guide read the rules export, so only tests held the old numbers. The AI's "are Bombers likely near this city" reach is `BOMBER_RANGE + FIGHTER_RANGE`, now 12 hexes, so a Flight-era rival 11 away now keeps a Fighter at home on guard.

## 2026-10-20: the open-ground rule is gated by the armour, not the melee unit (coordinator correction)
- The first build judged the rule by the melee unit's era, so a Rifleman kept the +18 against a Tank in the open, the case the user complained about. It is now the mounted unit's era (`unit_era_tier(other) >= ARMOUR_ERA_TIER`): against the Tank and the Autonomous Armour every melee unit needs a city, Forest or Hills; against the Cavalry and older it never does. The Autonomous Armour has 6 moves (the Tank 5), not the Tank's predecessor-beating 4 the first build left it with.
## 2026-10-20: era VP is scored by accident today
- **The AI's pursuit of era objectives has no measurable effect** (2 × 256 Hard games, 8 empires, same seeds; `docs/design/research/era-objectives-tradeoffs-2026-10-20.md`): with objective-seeking turned down as far as the knobs go, empires scored 5,670 objectives against 5,673, and each objective's met-share was within a few points whether it was drawn, not drawn or not pursued. 26 of 50 pool objectives are met by more than 15% of empires that never aimed at them; Fight objectives are 72% of all era scores ("destroy N units" alone 28%); 33% of era scores land on a turn when the same empire scores another era; seven objectives are dead (4% or less). This matches the user's complaint that he could "get all the points by accident". There is no knob that fully turns objective-seeking off (`objective_bonus_percent=0` still leaks through `weight.max(1)` in `objective_capture_value`); a real `objective_seek` gene is part of the redesign.

## 2026-10-20: five idle orders became two (Sleep and Skip)

- `HoldUnit`, `HealUnit` and `WakeUnit` are gone from core, AI, mock and app; `SleepUnit` is the one standing order for every unit and `SkipUnit` the one-turn order. Resting (heal, +3 fortify a turn) never needed an order: `heal_and_fortify` already rested every unit that had not acted, so Hold and Heal only differed in what they did to `standing_order` and `needs_orders`. That is why the AI could switch every Hold to Skip with identical play (it re-issues orders every turn and ignores `standing_order`), and why a Sleep issued by an AI unit would only have cost time: `sleeping_threats` builds a visibility map per team with sleepers every movement round.
- Old data still loads through serde aliases: orders `HoldUnit` and `HealUnit` read as `SleepUnit`, `WakeUnit` as `SkipUnit`, and the saved standing orders `Fortify` and `Heal` as `Sleep`. `StandingOrder` kept its place in the view as a one-variant enum. A tape that holds an old Hold now replays as Sleep, so its states hash differently and wake events appear (run `tools/sim/repin.sh`).
- Behaviour that changed for players: a Sleeping garrison wakes when a new enemy comes into sight within its movement range (old Fortify never did), and a sleeper stays asleep at full HP (old Heal woke it with a "healed" notice; `UnitHealed` is removed).
- Core never auto-fires a unit: ranged units shoot only on an explicit `RangedAttack`, so "Sleep holds fire" costs nothing. Only the AI converts its stay-put order into a shot (`fire_from_holds`, now over `SkipUnit`).
## 2026-10-21: the unit triangle ends at the Modern era (user decision 2026-10-20)
- **Replaces the open-ground rule** (cities, Forest, Hills) of 2026-10-19: `combat::triangle_applies` is true only when both units are from before the Modern era (`TRIANGLE_END_ERA_TIER` 5), and it gates `class_bonus`, `fight_class_bonus` and `add_fight_class_bonus` (core), `triangleApplies` (TS mock) and the unit card matchup line. The cover plumbing (`own_cover`, `PlayerView::has_cover`, `unit_has_cover`, `OPEN_GROUND_LABEL`, the AI's position arguments) is gone. Tank 5 and Autonomous Armour 6 moves stay.
- **What it does to the numbers.** An Infantry or a Tank gets no +18 from any class, and nobody gets one against them; a Cavalry (Industrial) still gets it against a pre-Modern ranged unit and a Rifleman against a Cavalry. With the era steps already +28 and +45 at the end, the Modern and Future fights are decided by strength, cost and moves alone. The duel table changes only where a Modern or later unit meets a counter-class unit.
- **The era chip on a unit** used the class bonus and now follows the gate through `addFightClassBonus`.

- **The box (c8g.16xlarge, spot) relaunched at 04:42 UTC and every job died with exit 143** ("connection dropped, reconnecting", then "Terminated"), including the 8.9.7 release check 17 minutes in. `box.sh status` shows the relaunch time on its first line. ## 2026-10-21: 8.9.7 UI review fixes, and what broke around them
- **A tech card listed Walls for the Mongols with a price they could not pay.** Core now sends `TechUnlock.locked_note` ("Walls for the Mongols from the Medieval era") for any listed unlock the faction cannot build yet; the research card, hovercard, unlock moment and tech detail show it in place of the build line and prices. The mock mirrors it (`mock/view.ts` `lockedNote`).
- **The new `a [AEIOU]` copy rule caught a real bug at once**: "Becomes a Irrigated Farm" in the improvement description. Run new copy rules against the rendered corpus before assuming the list is clean.
- **Found City now advances past whatever stands on the new city's tile** instead of clearing the selection for good: the first fix (selection stays empty) broke the touch flow, and selecting a stacked escort made the next click on the city a move.

- **A spec that changes the viewport must restore it**: the Scenario Lab "N more below" check left 1000x600 on, and the Technology-discovered card then covered "See result".
- **A spec that selects a unit right after Continue races the game's own first selection**; wait for the first selection, then choose.
- **Two primaries since the idle-orders merge were Sleep (unit card) plus the dock's call to action**, not End Turn. `ui/turnLead.ts` now decides who leads: a selected unit's card holds the primary and the dock steps back (`.cta.stepped`), unless the call to action is urgent (siege, offer, treasury, broken order) or nothing is pending, when the card's choice steps back. Also fixed: the Sparta tour tests Sleep's tooltip (Heal is gone), the turn-one tour drops the tile-price step (tile buying is gone), and a hovered danger button on the unit card is deeper red for AA contrast.

## 2026-10-21: landing the Codex removal batch (tile buying, Aid Station and Power Plant, Embassy and Academy)
- **Benchmark deltas against the master control (human-seat, Hard, 64 salts per map, reseeded dice, all-seat; rule removals cannot be split seat-only and opponents-only because every seat gets the rule):** tile buying 37.3 to 36.5 (-0.8 pp), Aid Station and Power Plant 39.8 to 39.1 (-0.7 pp), Embassy and Academy 39.1 to 37.9 (-1.2 pp), crown upkeep 39.1 to 36.7 (-2.4 pp). All inside the 95% interval (about +/-3.5 pp). Single maps move up to 14 points on 64 salts, so read only the overall.
- **Luna's removal branches were never run through the app gates.** `remove-dead-rule-switches` left stray `);` lines that broke four test files, `remove-aid-station-power-plant` left an unused import and a Playwright test that used the Factory (which needs a Forge first), and `remove-embassy-academy` left a spec asserting "Needs an Academy first". The fast profile does not run the new specs they add, so run the affected e2e specs by name on the box (`remote.sh . --npm -- bash -c 'scripts/build-wasm.sh; (cd app && npm run build); cargo build --release -p legatum-server; cd app && npx playwright test --project=game <specs>'`).
- **Two retired-building migrations now coexist.** `core::save_migration::drop_retired_buildings` (Aid Station, Power Plant, Embassy, Academy) and the older `wasm::json::migrate_removed_buildings` with its load notice (Embassy, Academy). Fold the second into the first when the next building is retired.
- **`remove-dead-rule-switches` is blocked by the TypeScript mock.** `app/src/mock/setup.ts` sets `legacy_vp: true` so mock and WASM agree on the five legacy titles; with the switch gone the WASM emits VP v2 `TitleChanged` events the mock never does, so about 60 mock/WASM parity tests in 10 files fail. It lands after the mock is retired (or after the parity helpers ignore VP v2 events).
- **`remove-crown-upkeep` stalled a Hard duel through a Celts AI bug that crown upkeep had been hiding (fixed on the branch).** `hold_metrics` seed 6 (Athens against Celts) hit the 1200-turn cap with 5 and 11 VP and 98 broken holds. No crown moved after turn 126: the Celts held all three crowns and the target (10) only with its live goal (Raise the Warbands, 2 VP), and lost the goal every one or two turns, so every hold broke at turn 1. Cause: the Celts AI keeps one camp per city and clears the doubles, but it counted camps by the nearest city while the goal counts the city whose territory holds the camp (`goals::wild_camp_cities`); where they differ it cleared a city's only camp, lost the goal, called the Wild again (11 camps) and repeated (123 completions, 122 losses, 1,475 own camps cleared). Crown upkeep neither caused nor cured it: master with upkeep zeroed (`overreach-gold-x10=0`) has 0 stalls in the same 192 duels, because the removal also drops the AI's crown valuation and the games diverge early; seed 6 is the game where the Celts ends on 9 permanent VP plus the goal against a 10 target. `Planner::territory_city` now reads `CityDetail.territory`; seed 6 ends by a hold win at turn 418, and 192 Hard duels (seeds 1 to 192) have 0 stalls (before the fix on this branch 1; master with upkeep 0). A game stalls whenever one team's target depends on a live goal and the owner's own orders break it: look at who breaks the hold before suspecting a rule. Benchmark (human-seat, Hard, 64 salts per map, reseeded dice, all seats, 2026-10-21): master 37.9% [34.4, 41.4] against this branch with the removal and the fix 36.5% [33.0, 40.0] (-1.4 pp, inside the interval; the removal alone read -2.4 pp earlier on another master); the Celts map moved 6.2% to 9.4%.
- **Spot restarts kill every box job at once (exit 143, "box is stopping").** A verify that died then proves nothing; rerun it.

## 2026-10-22: the AI values supply (`claude/ai-supply-value`)
- **The Forge was not unvalued, it was outbid.** In 64 census games a Forge-ready city offered a Forge scored about 290 and lost to the due-turn ladder (Granary 1,100, Laboratory 1,400, College 800, Market 900) and to Settlers and troops (2,000 and more). A flat `industry_priority` of 300 per Production (a Forge 900, a Factory 1,500) doubles Forges (0.73 to 1.26 at T250) and Factories (0.30 to 0.55); 600 gives 1.55 and 0.64. After that the binding limit is supply: median Iron supplied is 3 and used 1 to 2 with 3 to 4 Forge-ready cities, so the next lever is deposits (Mines, expansion, capture), not valuation.
- **The priority must yield to a stalled-growth city** (`faction_tests::industry_payback_does_not_delay_stalled_growth_at_either_speed`, the Hydroponics test): the same food test gates the boost.
- **A Forge started is often abandoned: 46% of Forge builds at priority 600, 42% at 300 (34% at baseline).** The city's build is replaced by military production (Military Engineers, Drones, Artillery, Soldiers). Progress is banked, so it is not all lost, but the Forge's timing is at the mercy of war production. Not changed.
- **The public economy share can't make a deposit city a target.** `price_campaign` feeds a deposit's Production into `TeamFacts.economy`, worth 1 to 3 points of win chance against capture terms of 1,000 to 5,000. Raising `supply_value_percent` from 0 to 300 left captures with a deposit unchanged (8.4 / 8.2 / 8.0 a game). A dedicated `supply` term (`supply_term` 400, tripled when short) is in, but its effect on deposit captures is also under noise at any weight up to 2,000: about half of all cities hold a deposit, so the base rate is 40 to 50%. Deposit transfers rise (7.4 to 8.3 a game) only through the demand the Forges create (`unmet`). A real test needs the choice among reachable targets, not the capture count.
- **Pikeman against Forge for the same Iron:** a Pikeman's strength premium over a Phalangite (23% for 55 Production) is worth about 0.4 Production per turn over 30 turns; a Forge gives 3. So at peace a contested Iron goes to the Forge and Pikemen fall (0.64 to 0.45 per empire at T150); at war the premium counts 8 times and the Pikeman wins. `supply_war_percent` 0 restores the old behaviour.
- **Gate (1,024 games per arm, reseeded dice):** seat-only -1.9 pp [-4.7, +0.9], opponents-only -0.5 pp [-3.5, +2.5]. The seat leans worse: a Forge is 160 Production for +3, so a human-quality seat does better with the ladder; it is inside noise but not clearly harmless. `industry_priority` 150 is the fallback (Forges 0.34 / 1.06 at T150 / T250 in the 64-game census).
- **Idle buildings no longer count toward "N Forges" objectives** (`Objective::progress`); the AI's `lacking` count is unchanged, so it can still think a city with an idle Forge is done. The unsupplied 25% now applies in `crates/ai/src/{tactics,analysis,dual,threat,opponents}.rs` (`supply::attack_total`, `ranged_total`, `defense_total`, `power`); the frozen proxy brains and the app's `aftermath.ts`, `siege.ts`, `unitEra.ts` don't.
- **A stale background script clobbers edits.** A regex rewrite of three AI files that backtracked catastrophically finished minutes later and overwrote an edit made in between; check `git diff` after a long-running codemod, and parse call arguments instead of using a dotall regex.
- **The box was saturated (12 slots, 11 queued)** during the gate: 256 games took 42 minutes there, 1,024 took about an hour on this 16-core Mac at nice 15, then two hours at load 30. The local `target` in the scratchpad (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`) built `hard_vs_human` for local arms files.
## 2026-10-21: the game-speed layer is gone, the tables hold the real prices (increment 1)
- **What went.** `GameSpeed`, `GameSetup.speed`, `PlayerView.speed`, `speed.scale_cost(x)` (always `x * 2`), `expected_length`, `science_history_turns`, `RuleExperiments.production_half_speed`/`scale_production`, `GoalSpec.speed_scaled`, the "Game pace" breakdown line, the sim's `RunOpts`/`RunMeta` speed, the app's `scaleCost`/`GameSpeed`/`RULES.speeds` and the TS mock's pace maths. Every old "base tuning" number was doubled in place (units, buildings, techs, improvements, START_GOLD 60, growth 30 + 16/pop, capture resistance 6, XP [16,46,90,150,226], barbarian turns and Gold, Alliance 60/120, wonder rewards, the idle cap 60). New constants: `data::EXPECTED_GAME_TURNS` 300, `FIRST_THIRD_TURNS` 100, `rules::SPARTA_DESERTION_INTERVAL` 5, `economy::ramp_price(turn, listed)`. Old saves, tapes and lobby configs that carry `"speed"` (even `"Quick"`) still load: serde ignores the key, and the archive `Metadata` keeps a write-never `speed` field so `deny_unknown_fields` does not reject old archives.
- **How "the default game did not change" was proved.** The state hash is FNV over the whole JSON, so dropping the `setup.speed` key moves every hash; "pins unchanged" cannot be literal. Instead: master with a hash that strips `"speed":"Standard",` (baseline) against the branch (plus a verification-only patch that restores two roundings, below) over 570 games (8-player Hard, Hard v2 with tuned openings, primitives, Rush, Normal, Easy, mixed brains, 1v1; seeds 92-99xxxxx, full length): every per-turn hash of every game identical. Replaying baseline tapes through the new engine (`--tape-in`) isolates engine from AI: that is how the unscaled consumers below showed up. The harness lives in the session notes of this change; rebuild it with `legatum-sim --tape-out` on both trees and compare `games[].hashes`.
- **Two roundings do move, by design.** Tech diffusion is now `floor(real * (100 - pct) / 100)` (it was floor on the half price, then doubled: up to 1 Science apart) and the Sparta premium is exactly 3/2 of the real price (the Settler was `(3f + 1) / 2` on an odd half price: 113 became 112.5 -> 225 instead of 226). So the repinned tapes differ from master's by the removed key AND these two; the verification patch that re-adds the old rounding gives identical games, which is the proof that nothing else moved.
- **The traps (all caught by the harness, none by the tests).** Code that read an UNSCALED table value and now sees double: tribute prices (`tribute::PERCENT` 10 -> 5 so the price is the same), the AI's keep values / loss ratios / military budgets / engineer cover cost (all in half Production points: `legatum_ai::tuned(cost) = cost / 2`; a future AI pass may rescale them), the strategy classifier's Rush threshold (`early_military_cost >= 60` -> 120), and `o.cost += SETTLER_COST_STEP` in an AI test that added the half-unit step to an already-real option cost (kept as +20). Genes and tuned genomes that went through `scale_cost` were doubled with their bounds (`settle_patience`, `reserve_deficit_turns`, `surplus_upkeep_turns`, `objective_horizon`, `campaign_march_patience`, `troop_runway`, the opening genes `settler_start`/`settler_interval`/`gold_save`/`war_deadline`/`rush_timeout`/`recovery_turns`, the primitive genes `escort_civilians_wait`/`scout_upkeep_until`/`scout_upkeep_intel_age`/`market_first_economy_horizon`; `tools/league/tuned-five-openings.json`, `tuned_openings.rs`, `tools/evolve/genome.py`). Old ledger genomes (`docs/sim-results/ai-quality/...best.json`) are in the old unit: double those genes before reusing them.
- **Ops.** `tools/ops/agent-worktree.sh acquire` fails with "master is already used" when a pool directory it wants does not exist yet (it runs `git worktree add <pool> master`): create the pool with `git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/pool-N <branch>` first. `cargo test` on the box is nextest: it takes no `-q`. A `timeout` around `remote.sh` kills the box job.

## 2026-10-22: the opening ramp is gone; the early prices were retuned instead (increment 2)
- **What changed.** `economy::ramp_price` (half the listed price on turn 0, the full price from turn 100) and the "Early-game discount" breakdown line are deleted, with the no-op flags `opening-ramp`/`capital-production` and the `early-military-discount` experiment (its only quote line was the ramp line, so deleting that line broke the `buy_cost_for` debug assertion for the experiment; delete a lever together with its breakdown line). Settler 70, +50 per trained Settler; Granary and Brood Hall 50, Workshop and Market 60, Library 80, Walls 60 (Swiss 80, Athens Library 70), Farm/Pasture/Quarry 30, Mine 40; units, later buildings and techs are untouched. Numbers and method: `docs/sim-results/2026-10-22-opening-ramp-removal.md` (400 games: first Settler T18 and second city T25 before and after; games ~8% shorter; first Soldier T30 to T32).
- **Plain prices were enough, units were not retuned.** Cheaper units (50-70% of listed) did not help the opening and would have made every later war cheaper, because the ramp's discount was temporary and a table price is forever. The price of the ramp's removal is that a Spearman is 80 from turn 1 (it was 40) and the early buildings stay cheap all game (the ramp made them full price from turn 100).
- **AI valuations that read table prices moved with the retune.** `city_keep_value` read the Settler's price as a city's worth; it now has its own constant (`CITY_KEEP_BASE` 75) so a 70-Production Settler does not make cities cheap to lose. Four AI-decision tests picked a Settler where they expected a Soldier because a Settler (70) is now cheaper than a Soldier (80), where the ramp kept it at about twice (78 against 41 on turns 4 and 8); their scenarios now set the Settler's price at the empire's third (170). `macro_economy`'s upgrade test saw the AI buy a 40-Production Mine (80 Gold) instead of upgrading a garrison.
- **A recorded-orders fixture is price-sensitive.** `threat_response.rs` replays a user's orders from a turn-35 save; orders address units by global id, so units that complete 3-4 turns later (full price instead of the ramped one) shift every later id and the recorded conquest never finishes. Both tests are `#[ignore]`d until the orders are re-recorded (`docs/status/next-tasks.md`). A topped-up stored Production does not help.
- **The mock found a latent crash.** The new trajectory put barbarian units (owner 255) in view around turn 31 and `diplomacyAi.team(255)` dereferenced an undefined player; `team()` now returns -1 for them like core's `TeamId::BARBARIAN`.

- **Bisect of `war-golden-horde-thin` (64 Hard runs per commit):** 89% through 10-22 01:21, 67% after move-through, era objectives step 1, supply AI and the ramp removal, then 0% from the free-Alliances merge (`72fc33073` alone on its old base: 89% → 54%). Likely a design consequence of free Alliances plus "allies fight together", not a bug; the balanced-game bloc census decides it.

The AI was joining Alliances without pricing the wars it inherits (fix in progress, `claude/alliance-inherited-wars`).

Both sides of the Alliance value have to move.

When allies already share an enemy (a coalition against the leader), an Alliance inherits no new war and the shared-enemy and coalition terms make every Alliance positive; the signing fee and upkeep were the only restraint. Testing an AI bloc-size cost; if that fails, the rule needs a cost (the user's call: one Alliance at a time is the lead's pick).

- **Appending to a pending Codex task file is a race.** I appended the Heir-name instructions to `rename-legacy-factions.md` with `cat >>` after the runner had already moved it to `running/`. That created a new pending file holding only the appended text, with no header. The runner ran it as a nameless review task on **gpt-6-sol** (the default model), which breaks the Luna-only policy, and it did nothing. ## 2026-10-23: the climb daemon waited 12 hours on a finished spot run
- **`os.kill(pid, 0)` finds a zombie.** The climb daemon starts each spot batch with `Popen`. To tell whether a run is still going, it checked `os.kill(pid, 0)`, but it never reaped the child, so a finished run stayed a zombie (`<defunct>`) and counted as alive. The Celts' gen-14 batch finished on its server at 13:00, and the daemon then waited until 01:15 the next day. That was the last climb running, so round 1 sat stalled while its status line kept saying "in flight on spot (586 min)". Restarting had always fixed it, because a new daemon isn't the zombie's parent. Fix: `climb_program.py::pid_alive` reaps with `os.waitpid(pid, WNOHANG)` first. Rule: a supervisor that polls its own children must reap them. When an "in flight" age is far past the batch's `max-hours`, treat it as stuck.

- At 8 Hard empires the WASM End Turn already averages 54 ms late game (p95 63, max 87); the cost is spread across every seat's decision view. Native `perf` (frame pointers on, `tools/perf/native-perf.sh`) puts `resources::deposits` (a full 1,536-tile scan allocating a `Vec<Deposit>` per call) at 21% and `eras::current_era` at 6%, both reached through `shortage_after` for each production option of each city in `view::city_detail`. Numbers and tools: `docs/sim-results/perf/turn-latency.md`.

None was landed until the morning. The lead only wakes on its own background jobs and agent hand-backs. ## 2026-10-24: payoff moments on the map (moments-fx)
- **Towns and borders are baked into terrain chunks, so an animation has to hold them back, not paint over them.** `TerrainCache.setHold` takes what a moment is still animating (towns and walls the overlay draws, a town's old population or era, a tile's owner before its claim) with a signature; only chunks near a tile whose hold changed repaint, at the few instants it changes, never per frame. Painting a "before" state over a chunk that already shows the "after" cannot work (a new town or a new border line shows through). Live layers (roads, improvements) instead draw twice: the view from before outside the revealed area, the current view inside it (`drawRevealed`).
- **A one-off engraving of a painted sprite reads as pen and ink** (Sobel on the luminance over vellum, the silhouette outlined, hatching only in the deepest shadow, sepia at about 85% alpha) when it sits on a pale vellum ground; without the ground and with hatching in the midtones it read as a dark blob. Capped at 256 px so the first use costs no visible hitch.
- **Several moments land on one capital in a busy turn** (a wonder, five era objectives, a crown, a war and a peace on 8.9.6 T151): VP seals merge per empire per turn, and seals take slots beside a rising building or another seal instead of stacking on it.
- **Frame-stepped captures freeze `performance.now()`**, so the perf counters read 0 in them: measure frame cost on the real clock (`perf63` in `moments-fx.media.ts`).
- **A media test with no action timeout hangs for its whole hour** when an alarm (a war declared at turn start) covers the turn dock: the harness closes alarms, takeovers and unlock cards before ending a turn, and sets a 45 s default timeout.
- **`.moment-lane.reduced *` (specificity 0,2,0) loses to a card rule like `.moment-card.unlock .unlock-seal` (0,3,0)**: a new card animation needs its own reduced-motion override, and `::after` is not covered by the lane's rule at all.

- `tools/astra/runner.sh` defines `model_slug` when each lane loop starts, so changing the mapping (here `astra` → gpt-6-astra) only affects lanes started afterwards. Running lanes keep mapping `astra` to Sol until they're restarted. ## 2026-10-24: landing batches of Codex branches
- **Split refactors go stale fast.** `astra/review-split-lobby` passed its own checks, but merged with master it no longer compiled: master's LobbyScreen had changed underneath it (missing `playerIds`, `playerColor`, unexported `SeatsTable`). Release file-split refactors only when no feature work touches those files, and land them soon after they finish.
- **A pipe hides a failed fast-forward.** `git merge --ff-only ... | tail -2 || fallback` never runs the fallback, because the pipe's exit status is `tail`'s. Don't pipe git merges in a landing script, or set `pipefail`.
- **Rivals' Great Works can't be landmarks yet:** a city's buildings are only in `CityView.detail`, which the view carries for your own cities, so `landmarks.ts` shows only yours. Showing a rival's needs a public "great works" field on the city view from the core (the Great Work milestone itself is public).
- **The WebKit screen tour fails 14 specs on master as of 2026-10-24 (company, factions, heir, post-game, research-unlocks, turn-one; box job 20261024T170446Z-684d83).** A branch's WebKit failures are only its own if they are not in a same-day master run: compare before chasing them.
- **Construction animation took two rejected rounds (2026-10-24), and both failed for the same reason: they were effects laid over finished art, not the building being built.** Scaffolds that don't follow the structure, and a clip reveal of the finished painting, both read as cheap. Real construction needs art made for it (staged paintings of the same building) and a researched design approved first; until then it is switched off behind one flag, with the plan, holds, landmark placement and staged-art loader left in place.

## 2026-10-24: real games rarely have big battles from the player's seat
- **The designer's own empires field only 1 to 6 units,** so his saves can't show a complex battle from his seat. To film or stress-test combat, copy a late-game save, move the human seat to the empire with the biggest army in contact (strip the turn archive so the copy is consistent), and never write the original. The busiest real turn found across four games had 13 movers and 5 clashes, playing in 3.8 s. Busier turns need a synthetic fixture (30 shots and 20 clashes is about 6 s), and that's what the pacing test covers.

## 2026-10-24: the AI gate for seven Codex branches (`docs/sim-results/ai-quality/gate-1024/`)
- **Gate method that worked: one binary, gene groups as arms, effect = on minus off.** Where a branch ships its genes on, set the benchmark binary's defaults to 0 for a bench build (so "baseline" rivals play the old way) and give arms the on values; or keep defaults on and use arms that turn one group off (effect is minus the delta, and the opponents arm flips the same way). One cloud batch of 9 to 15 arms, 4 servers, took about 45 minutes. At 1,024 games per arm the interval is +-3 pp, so the -1 pp / +1 pp landing rule cannot separate a real 1 pp effect: re-run a borderline arm on fresh salts (`--seed 1001`) and pool before deciding. The settler-capture gene read opponents +0.9 then +2.6 pp and was left off.
- **A branch that deletes a gene's code leaves an inert arm.** The revive branch removed the `siege_exempt` and `plan_persist_skip` checks, so its "restore the old exemption" arm was identical to the control in every game (identical games across arms mean the arm does nothing, as before). Check that an arm's gene is still read (`grep` the code) before trusting a flat result. The dedicated arm after rewiring showed the removal cost Sparta's 8.4 seat 64 to 48 wins of 128, as the old code comment said, so Sparta keeps its exemption.
- **Merging two supply fixes made one double-charge.** master and the ruins branch had both fixed Siege-upgrade Iron budgeting in `supply.rs::within_budget`; git merged them cleanly into a first loop that reserved Siege and a second that reserved it again. A clean merge of two fixes to one function needs a read of the result.
- **Changing a gene's default breaks tests that assumed it.** Four AI tests failed once `peace_settler_capture` defaulted to 0 and `vp_peace` priced Peace in the pre-hold test; tests of a gene's behaviour should set the gene.
- **VP race effect on holds:** in 2,000 all-AI eight-player games the five `vp_*` genes left holds broken at 49.4% to 49.8% and first-hold wins at 65.5% to 67.9%; the branch probe's 49% to 60% (32 seeds) was noise. The measured gain is in the human-seat benchmark, not in all-AI hold statistics.

Replaying his recorded orders for the window (`scenarios/war/scripts`, `crates/sim/examples/war_script`, recorded from the tape by `extract-war-states.sh`) reproduces his result to the damage roll (the same 102, 87, 124, 89 on Cologne): Germany's AI loses three cities by T218 in 64 of 64 runs and is eliminated on T221, 0% on both goals. In those 128 runs it ordered no Fighter and bought none; its `air_rebase` default saves its Bomber and a second Bomber is built, but it strikes ground targets. Orders name hexes, so replay survives a changed position; use it only where the AI cannot play the attacker's side (untested past 8 turns, where the two worlds may diverge). Also: (1) the Japan T142 fixture's "hold all ten" read 0% because Kyoto (20 HP, 1 citizen, no Walls) falls on turn 3 in every run and the failed `keep` ends the run, so a goal that must let the window finish uses `win` only; (2) with Sparta played by an AI the exchange is about even (Japan loses 7.5 combat units a run, Sparta 7.9 and Athens 1.3), nothing like his 30 for none, and Sparta and Japan sign Peace in 45 of 64 runs where he refused every Japanese offer for 150 turns; (3) all three first predictions missed by 30 to 70 points, because the AI as attacker is much weaker than the designer and a weak city decides a hold-all goal. Details in `docs/sim-results/hard-vs-human/war-scenarios/README.md`.
- **2026-10-27: A replayed-orders script fits for about 12 turns, not 17.** `war-german-air-early` from the Japan bomber game: the same recorded orders from T205 gave Germany 100% on "keep 4 of 6" (predicted 5%) because from T207 his strikes and Armour routes name hexes where the real game's units stood (`WAR_TRACE_FAILED=1 war_trace` shows each skipped order); from T207, T208 and T209 also 100%, from T210 4%, as in his game. Check a script's fidelity by starting it at several turns and keeping the earliest start at which it still reproduces the recorded result.
- **2026-10-27: Raising the AWS cap is two steps, and the lead can't do either.** A higher `monthly_budget_usd` doesn't lift the launch ban already tripped: the `legatum-sims-deny-launch` policy stays attached to the launcher until it is detached (`infra/cloud-sims/README.md`). The permission system denies the lead `terraform apply` and `aws iam detach-user-policy` even after the user picks an amount, so prepare the edit and the preview (`terraform plan`, one in-place change), then hand the user both commands.
- **2026-10-27: An oh-my-zsh update prompt can eat the first character of a pasted command.** The user's paste of `cd ~/code/legatum/infra/cloud-sims && terraform apply` ran as `d ...`, so `terraform apply` ran in the repo root ("No configuration files") and nothing changed. When handing the user commands, give the `cd` as its own block, and check the outcome (`read_terminal`, or `terraform state show` for the budget) rather than assuming it ran.

- **2026-10-27: A stranded unit used a foreign city as its stepping stone out of closed land (war-suite flag "unit 66 (Ranger) stands in the foreign city Hiroshima", `war-japan-chur-ring` run 41, T155).** Real rules bug, not a detector false positive: Peace made on T154 left a Swiss Ranger in Japanese land, and the Swiss AI (its trapped-unit mover, `ai/src/diplomacy.rs`, single adjacent MoveUnit) ordered it onto the adjacent Japanese city because `path::exit_distances` counted the city centre as passable and the shortest egress ran through it; the engine accepted the step (the Mongols-only `neutral_city` block in `rules/movement.rs` never applied) and it ended the turn inside the empty city. Fix: `path::exit_distances_around` treats city centres on closed land as walls; `rules/movement.rs::exits_from` (resolution), `PlayerView::exit_distances` (validation, settlers, AI) and `app/src/diplomacy.ts:borderSteps` use it. Regression tests in `rules/movement_contention_tests.rs` (they fail without the fix). Goal results on the ring scenario are unchanged (0%, 64 runs, same losses). Not touched: the frozen AI proxies (`proxy_v4`..`v8`) keep the old egress; a Courier Hall holder's cities are open at Peace by `passage_allowed`, so a non-Mongols unit might still walk into one (unchecked).
- **2026-10-27: The W1 operation record (gene `operation_planner`, off) turns the bombed-but-never-entered Swiss T220 into a capture every time, and breaks a melee-only storm.** One record per front owns roster, aircraft, rendezvous and home guard, takes its units' orders before every other army pass, and every two turns rolls commit / gather / withdraw forward from its own view (`crates/ai/src/operation.rs`, `search::evaluate_operation`). War suite, 64 runs, paired with the W0.2 baseline (gene off reproduces it run for run, 1,344 of 1,344): `war-swiss-tepid-t220` 23% to 100% (bombers and the walk-in now belong to one order set; T220-fresh 51 to 100), Golden Horde 100 to 93 (60/64), thin 90 to 89, `war-walls-rise` 81 to 92, German air T210/T214 4 to 31 and 0 to 60 (the German operation retakes the city the replayed Japanese script captured; the script never defends it, so read this as an upper bound), Swiss T180 and the Chur ring still 0, German stand 93 to 89 and Japan T142 78 to 75 (intervals cross zero), and **Sparta's First Blood 100 to 4**: its five Spearmen have no shooter, and the commit executor only sends melee in once the city is at 0 HP or a volley drops it, so a melee storm never starts; the existing assault coordinator (which stormed on its forecast) no longer sees those units. Withdraw-on-tie plus a per-city cooldown also bounced the objective between Anvil and First Foundry. Suite mean 43 to 49, parity 8 to 10 of 21. Also: (1) `LEGATUM_ROLLOUT_THREADS=1` makes every war_suite thread queue on one shared rollout thread (the suite ran at 120% CPU and took 440 s instead of about 110 s even with the gene off, because some opponents are Hard + Search); use 4 for suite runs and 1 only to time one decision. (2) Native cost per decision on one thread: about 10 ms at T30 with 4 empires, 40 to 70 ms in the 8-empire Golden Horde, 75 to 110 ms at T143 to T187, and about 390 ms for a seat's first decision of a game (generating its sampled map, as Hard + Search also pays); a rollout turn with three seats at war costs about 9 ms, so the 12-turn cap is the budget lever. (3) Over 4 to 6 turns the win-chance score separates alternatives only when a capture or a game end happens inside the horizon (T220: 3,853 against 1,619); elsewhere it differs by tenths of a percent, so a tie rule decides.
- **2026-10-27: W1 round 1: the operation's commit must start with the existing assault coordinator, ties must not withdraw, and a withdrawal must close the whole front.** First Blood (five Spearmen, no shooter) went 100% to 4% in the first version because commit only sent melee in after a volley; running `coordinate_city_assaults_at` on the roster first and letting the melee wing storm a city without Walls brings it back to 100% (run 0 takes Anvil on T32 and First Foundry on T36, as plain Hard). Hysteresis (a new operation stands on commit and changes only for +100 of 10,000 win chance) and a front-wide cooldown after a withdrawal stopped the objective bouncing between the two German cities. Round 1, 64 runs paired with W0.2: suite mean +10.0 points (43 to 53%), T220 23 to 95%, T220-fresh 51 to 95%, walls-rise 81 to 100%, German air T210/T214 4 to 18% / 0 to 76%, German stand 93 to 92% and Japan T142 78 to 76% (both inside noise), Golden Horde 100 to 89% (57/64; -10.9, interval -18.8 to -4.7), T180 and Chur still 0. The four "stands in the foreign city" flags in Japan T142 are other seats' units (e.g. P3's Assault Trooper, unit 79, run 60, T155) stranded in Sparta's land after a Peace and stepping into the city as egress, the pattern `claude/fix-stranded-egress` fixes; `WAR_TRACE_FLAGS=1 war_trace` prints each flag with the unit's owner and move.
- **2026-10-27: W1 rounds 2 to 4: the operation's own losses came from home defence, Peace vetoes and short horizons, not from committing; and the Swiss T180 and Chur cases do not move with a better score or a purchase (stop rule).** (1) *Golden Horde 57/64 in round 1 was a lost home city, not an early commit:* the roster emptied a Mongol city a neighbour at Peace stood beside, and it declared and took it (run 10, T141). Keeping a city's garrison while any foreign army is within 6 hexes brought it to 61/64, then 64/64. A static allocation mirroring `defend_cities` (nearest units until the threat is covered) crushed it to 26%; reverted. (2) *Japan T142 (the defender) fell to 70% because the operation vetoed every Peace:* the Hard defender survives by signing Peace (45 of 64 runs at baseline). Vetoing only while the last decision found fighting on better than withdrawing by the margin restored it to 79 to 82%. (3) *A plan that drops the war mid-assault* (T210, a Phalangite lost, plan to Contain another team) used to end the operation and let Peace through; now a committed operation decides at once instead. (4) *Adding a third alternative shrank the horizon from 6 to 4 under the 12-turn cap,* and T220-fresh fell from 89% to 34%: the hold victory at the end of T223 dropped out of the rollouts. The cap is now 18 turns with the enemy seats re-planning every other turn; that saved little, because a rollout turn is about 9 ms of whole-world resolution in an 8-empire late game, not planning. (5) *Zero-sum material term and buy-then-attack, two rounds, no change on T180 or Chur:* in both the defender converts its Gold (3,152 and 6,481) into garrisons the turn the army shows up, the attacker's army is one to two eras older, and the attacker is broke (219 and 43 Gold), so a reinforce choice is offered rarely (chosen in 2 of 48 traced runs, both T180; 2 purchases ordered, 0 dropped by the supply budget). Final round (r4), 64 runs paired with W0.2: mean +7.9 points, T220 23 to 92%, Golden Horde 100%, thin 90 to 98%, First Blood 100%, German stand 93 to 92%, Japan T142 78 to 82%, T210 100 to 92% (-7.8, single-sample rollout noise flips commit and withdraw by about 120 points), T180 and Chur 0%. Gene off still reproduces W0.2 run for run.
- **2026-10-27: W1 round 5: a new operation must stand on the ordinary passes, not on commit, and near-tie resampling alone does not remove noise; the planner still bleeds about 1.5 more units a run where attacking cannot win.** (1) Rolling the alternatives again on a second fresh sample when the best two were within 300 points (gene `operation_tie`) left T210 at 89% and T220-fresh at 56%, and roughly doubled the cost of those decisions (Chur up to 280 ms). (2) The bleeding came from hysteresis standing on commit: a new operation committed unless the rollouts clearly showed otherwise, so in Swiss T180 it lost 12.7 units a run (plain Hard 8.1). A new operation now stands on withdraw (plain Hard) and takes the army only when committing beats it by the margin; T210 is back to 98% and Golden Horde, First Blood and both defences hold or improve (German stand 95%, Japan T142 84%). (3) A reinforce chosen on noise on the last turn of T220-fresh pulled the walk-in away from a city already at 0 HP; reinforcing is now offered, like gathering, only while the army is short of its force (T220-fresh 32% to 62%). (4) Hopeless cases, off vs on (round 7, 64 runs, combat units lost per run, ours / theirs): T180 8.14 / 2.98 vs 9.54 / 2.95; Chur 8.90 / 5.78 vs 10.54 / 5.50, cities lost 0.98 vs 1.00; T180 against the designer's recorded orders (new `war-swiss-tepid-t180-replay`) 6.70 / 2.00 vs 8.48 / 2.29, 0% either way, predicted 15% and 45%. The likely cause is the information limit, not the executor: determinized rival treasuries scale ours by the public economy title, so a poor Swiss seat models Athens as poor and its rollouts do not see the Infantry Athens buys. (5) Rebuilding `war_extract` on an old engine to record a seat's orders: copy the current `tools/scenarios/war_extract.rs` into the engine tree's `crates/wasm/examples/` and build there; the binaries left from W0.2 predate the `seat:first-last` argument and silently write no `orders-<seat>.json`.
- **2026-10-27: The T180 replay is the key finding of W1: even against his real, nearly undefended Athens, Spearmen and Archers can't open a walled 200-HP city, so the Swiss stall was mostly army quality, not operations.** Against the designer's recorded orders (`war-swiss-tepid-t180-replay`: one unit walks in on T185, nothing bought for Athens) the Swiss AI takes nothing in 64 of 64 runs with the gene off or on. The operation planner fixes coordination (Swiss T220: bombers plus a walk-in), not an army one to two eras behind its target.
- **2026-10-27: W1 last round: bleeding is fixed by a stricter start and a loss stop; a treasury floor from visible enemy troops changed nothing; seat stagger and short horizons cost T220.** (1) A start margin (`operation_start_margin` 300: committing must beat the ordinary passes by 300 of 10,000 before the operation takes the army; Chur run 27 committed on a +120 edge and lost seven units in two turns) plus a loss stop (withdraw when roster deaths exceed the decision's rollout forecast, pro rata, by 2 units; then 10 turns before a new operation) bring the hopeless cases to plain Hard's losses: T180 8.20 vs 8.14, T180 replay 6.71 vs 6.70, Chur 9.73 vs 8.90 (still +0.8). (2) Flooring the enemy's sampled treasury at the purchase price of the troops seen appearing at its cities since we watched gave identical results with or without it (64-run subsets), so it was removed: without event history the view cannot tell a bought unit from a trained one, and the rollouts' Hard defenders buy anyway. (3) Swiss T220 fell from 85% (r7) to 51 to 65%: staggering later decisions by seat moved the Swiss decision off the turn it mattered (65% without, 51% with; the gene is now off), and the start margin skips some near-even commits (run 1: +242). Two samples per decision (cap 24) did not restore it (57%), so it is not plain sampling noise. (4) The German air gains of r1 to r7 (up to 57% and 76%) disappear once the operation stands on the ordinary passes: they came from committing counter-attacks into cities the replayed Japanese script never defends, an artifact of the script.

- **2026-10-27: W0.4 ranked the AI candidates on one frozen-control gate (`docs/sim-results/ai-war/baseline.md`); three things in it are not obvious.**
  - **The human-seat gate's rivals never bomb.** Its opponents are Hard+Search, and Search drops air strikes unless `search_air_orders=1`. Turning that on costs the seat 22 pp: those rivals now bomb as the app's plain Hard already does. Until the gate's control has it on, every air gene is measured against rivals that never strike. That's why air defense r2 reads −4.7 pp in the seat (Fighters bought against nobody), and why its opponents-only −24 pp mostly comes from `air_capture_bundle` turning on the same Search air pass. Re-freeze the control with `search_air_orders=1` before judging air work.
  - **8.9.13's Germany-map drop is the valuation gene.** With `modernization_value=0` on every seat, Germany 8.6 goes from 144 back to 186 of 256 (+16 pp; 8.9.13 lost about 15), while Switzerland 8.3 falls from 87 to 52. A noninferior overall result can hide one gene's map-specific cost. None of the seven candidate arms recovered it.
  - **Gene arms that can't act cost a full arm of games.** `search_air_orders` only acts in Search and opening wrappers, and the benchmark seat plays plain `ScriptedBrain`, so its seat-only arm would replay the control. A combined arm whose extra gene is inert in one role likewise replays the single arm there. Check where a gene is read (`grep`) before paying for an arm.
  - **Comparing two binaries' games:** a bench that adds telemetry fields (the strategy-lab `hard_vs_human`) changes every game-record hash even when the games are identical. Compare on the fields both binaries record (`air`, for one, grew new subfields). The bench reproduced master on 128 of 128 games that way.
  - **Box tests run under nextest:** grepping `cargo test` output for `test result` on the box shows only the doc-test lines. The real summary is nextest's `Summary [...] N tests run`.

- **2026-10-28: 8.9.14 UI review fixes: four layout traps worth knowing.** (1) The unlock card scrolled as a whole (`overflow-y: auto` on the card), so its primary button scrolled out of view at 1000x600; the body (`.unlock-body`) scrolls and the footer is `flex: none`, and the tour now measures `getBoundingClientRect().bottom <= innerHeight` for the longest cards. (2) A `float: right` count inside a `<summary>` wraps across the divider and the next row in the 196 px rail; stack it as a block there. (3) Elements inside a closed `<details>` still return client rects, so "is it on screen" checks use `checkVisibility()` (the "+N more empires" counter counted hidden rows until it did). (4) The rail's own `.sidebar-scroll { height: 88px }` rule in `sidebar.css` is dead: `:root .game .right-sidebar .seatbar > .sidebar-scroll` outranks it, so the rail scrolls the whole column. Left as is, since the rail looks right with it.
- **2026-10-27: Checking the build label needs a count, not the first match.** The bundled JS also holds older "Playtest 8.9.x" strings (release notes), so `grep … | sort -u | head` showed 8.9.10 and 8.9.11 for the 8.9.14 build. Use `grep -rao "Playtest 8\.9\.[0-9]*" app/dist | sort | uniq -c` and look for the new label (it appears once).

- **2026-10-28: the human-seat benchmark's rivals are plain Hard now; the old control was 36%, the real one is 16%.** (1) The eight benchmark maps carry `search: true` on every AI seat (the lobby's experimental Hard+Search level), and Search skips air strikes, so the gate's rivals never bombed while the app's default Hard does. `hard_vs_human` now plays rivals as plain `ScriptedBrain`; `--rival-search` or an arm's `"rival_search": true` restores Search rivals. Same binary, 2,048 games, 8.9.14: control 331 (16.2%) against 745 (36.4%) with Search rivals (+20.2 pp [+17.9, +22.5]); Germany 35 against 121 of 256. Ledger rows and W0.4 numbers were all measured against non-bombing rivals; only compare new numbers with new numbers (`docs/sim-results/ai-war/baseline.md`, W2.0). (2) Against bombing rivals the verdicts flip or sharpen: `air_defense=100` seat-only +3.2 pp [+1.6, +4.8] (it read -4.7), modernization off costs the seat 3.7 pp [-5.5, -1.8] (8.9.14's gain holds), and modernization off for the rivals helps the seat 3.4 pp. Re-test any air gene measured before today. (3) The `zero_offset_reproduces_the_archived_game_output` test in `hard_vs_human.rs` had been failing on master: `cargo nextest` doesn't build example tests, so nobody saw it. Run `cargo test -p legatum-sim --example hard_vs_human` when touching that file (on the box: `tools/cloud/offload.sh`). (4) An arms file naming a gene the binary doesn't have panics every server in seconds (`unknown field`), costing a launch and a few cents; check the gene exists on the branch you build before launching. (5) The 5-arm, 2,048-game batch took 11 minutes and 0.74 server-hours (about $0.48); the Search rivals were the expensive part of the old gate (14 arms, 7.78 server-hours).

- **2026-10-27: war fixtures from the 8.9.13 Athens and Sparta games (`docs/sim-results/hard-vs-human/war-scenarios/README.md`, "Fixtures from the designer's two 10-27 games"); five things that are not obvious.**
  - **A recorded-orders replay reproduces his game in run 0 and only partly in other seeds.** Run 0 keeps the game's own seed, and on the 8.9.13 build it reproduces every capture on the same turn (6 of 6 cases; the AI memory carried by `extract-war-states.sh` with `memory,0:101-177` makes the brains replay the real game). Seeds 1 and up change the dice and the brains' tie-breaks, and his orders (exact paths and hexes) stop fitting as soon as a unit dies or stands elsewhere. The Sparta-game defences therefore read 95 to 100% for the AI (Germany's Berlin hangs on one roll: a Hoplite left at 6 HP in run 0 is killed in run 1), against his total loss. Scan start turns before trusting a verbatim script; where nothing reproduces (Germany), ship it as a regression guard and say so.
  - **A goal that does not name its victim or its cities measures something else.** An any-city capture goal read 14% on `war-sparta-next-door-t101` (the Spartan army took a Mongol city in 9 of 64 runs; Athenian cities: 0). A `MinCities` defence goal read 71% on `war-japan-hoplites-t43` (28 of 64 runs lost all three cities and founded a new one: 28% is the real figure). `Condition::CapturedFrom` and `Condition::MinStartingCities` exist for this; use them for any capture or hold goal.
  - **The start state can break the script.** At T42 (the declaration turn) one Hoplite stood in Japanese land at Peace, which today's rules forbid; `modernize` moves it a tile and his T42 orders for it no longer fit, so even run 0 diverged. Start the war fixtures on the first turn at war (T43).
  - **The 8.9.13 to 8.9.14 difference on these seven is exactly the two modernization genes.** A tree with the AI and core files of 8.9.14 reverted to `a58e80856` equals the current build with `modernization_upgrade` and `modernization_return` at 0 (`--ai-params modern0.json --params-seats all`), run for run on all 448 runs; the stranded-unit egress fix changes nothing here. The genes moved the goal result in 0 to 4 runs of 64 a case.
  - **`cities_lost` in a run report is capped by the keep condition**: a run stops at the first failure, so a mean of 1.46 starting cities lost does not say how many he would have taken.


- **2026-10-28: Fighters (`air_defense=100`) on the fixed gate, and the planner re-ranked.** Plain Hard rivals bomb, 2,048 games: Fighters seat-only +3.2 pp [+1.6, +4.8], rivals-only -1.3 [-2.9, +0.3], all seats +1.0 [-0.6, +2.6]; the war suite is identical with the gene on (64 runs by 21 scenarios, 49% both). The campaign planner reads +1.2 [-0.5, +2.9] in the seat and +1.0 [-1.0, +3.0] as rivals: neutral in full games, as before. The control reproduced master game for game (2,048 of 2,048) in all three batches, including on a binary with the planner merged in (genes off equals master). `air_capture_bundle` and `search_air_orders` are not on master, only on `astra/search-air-execution`, so arms using them need that branch first. Merging a feature branch just for a benchmark binary: take only the AI crate and keep master's war tooling when the war files conflict (`git checkout --ours` on the sim files), because the benchmark builds only `hard_vs_human`. Details: `docs/sim-results/ai-war/baseline.md` W2.0.
- **2026-10-28: Sub-agents' AWS spot launches can be refused by the permission system as real-money actions,** even within an approved budget. The gate-fix agent's launches went through, but the door-defense agent's were refused hours later. When a brief needs spot servers, say so and plan a local fallback: a quarter-size local gate (512 games per arm) gives about ±4 pp. If an agent is refused, the user approves the launch; the lead doesn't relaunch it for the agent.
- **2026-10-28: Door defense is neutral in full games and still worth shipping; a four-arm 2,048-game gate on plain Hard rivals now costs about $0.10 and 3 minutes.** Seat -1.1 pp, rivals-only -0.3, all -0.8, every interval across zero, while the war suite gains 6.5 points and an adaptive Sparta's wins halve. The full-game benchmark is dominated by economy and expansion, so a war-only gain shows up there only once wars decide games; judge war genes on the war suite plus "no full-game loss", not on a full-game gain. The old gate's cost (7.78 server-hours) was the Search rivals: with plain Hard rivals a gate runs in 0.15 server-hours.
- **2026-10-28: Search's rollouts model every rival as default Hard, so turning a defence gene on by default changes archived Search reviews, and zeroing it in the test's seat brain does nothing.** `SearchRollout` builds rival brains with `ScriptedBrain::with_difficulty` (built-in genes), so `door_defense` on made the T51 Mongols-partial review prefer Economy over the Campaign (4,704 against 4,530). Seat-side genes (e.g. `modernization_value`) can be zeroed in the archived brain; rival-side behaviour can't, so pin only what the review must still compare.

- **2026-10-29: In a worktree, copy `app/src/wasm-pkg` (or build it with `LEGATUM_OFFLOAD=1 scripts/build-wasm.sh`); never symlink it, and never trust the main checkout's copy.** Vite resolves a symlink to its real path, so a spec that injects a fixture (`await import('/src/test/…')`) gets a second, uninitialised copy of the module and fails with `__wbindgen_free` of undefined. The main checkout's package was also built before Siege became built in, so `browserFixtures.test.ts` saw a Siege offer on a Rifleman; the stale package fails tests that have nothing wrong with them. A `node_modules` symlink is fine.
- **2026-10-29: the siege gear prop is cosmetic and capped by the unit's own era; the combat tier is not.** `siegePropFor` reads the technologies for the tier but the unit's era for the art (an Ancient Archer with Metallurgy draws a catapult, not a bombard). `shotKindFor` is passed the drawn prop, so the animation's missile at a city follows the art (catapult and trebuchet throw stones, a bombard shot) and the two cannot disagree.
- **2026-10-29: a tile-chosen item's tooltip printed its card copy twice.** `renderOption` builds `detail` from the card copy plus `effect`, and a Wonder site's `effect` appended `itemCardText` again after "Replaces ... on this tile ·". Every Wonder site (the Yam Relay Station and Great Works) showed the doubled text. A site's effect now adds only the yield given up; the Yam spec asserts the copy appears once.
- **2026-10-29: tile placement state lives in the store (`place`), and the city panel applies the pick through a ref set after its `if (!d)` early return.** A `useEffect` declared after that return broke every foreign-city render ("Rendered fewer hooks than expected"); the effect now sits above the return and calls `applyPlacePick.current`. Map clicks on a lit tile only set `place.pick`, so Build, Queue and Buy keep using the panel's own `buildNow`/`append`/`toggleBuy`. Also: `TitleScreen.test.tsx`'s autosave test fails about one full-suite run in three under load and passes alone; treat a lone failure there as flaky.
- **2026-10-29: map placement draws its lit tiles under the counters and banners, and only the hovered tile above them.** Drawn last, the lit rings struck through city names and unit tokens. A placed Wonder site gets its own `sites` list on the improve overlay and a gilt double ring, because a thin seat-colour ring vanished into the territory border. Local `npx playwright test e2e/tour` serves whatever `app/dist` was last built (a stale one showed per-tile Yam cards), so run tours on the box.

- **2026-10-30: Focus fire and stragglers (genes `focus_fire`, `gather_hold`, off; `claude/focus-fire`; `docs/sim-results/ai-war/w24-focus/`): small real gains, and the AI's losses are mostly positional, not spread fire.** (1) *Where units die:* a temporary pass trace (each order tagged with the `plan_military` pass that gave it) found that on the turn of death units are mostly already retreating (`recover_city_fire` 29%, `recover_wounded` 9%) or defending (`defend_cities` 18%); the pass that put them there the turn before was `defend_cities`, `siege_war`, `press_strike` or `campaign`. A retreat order can't save a unit inside a walled city's range, since the strike fires before movement. Judge a straggler fix by the pass of the turn before. (2) *Held-out seeds (runs 64-191) with both genes:* exchange 1.14 to 1.20, losses -4.5%, units lost per capture 8.77 to 8.18, Mongols Chur T137 17% to 32%; mean goal +0.4. Focus alone moves kills more than losses (in-sample exchange 1.16), the straggler hold moves losses (1.19); together 1.21. (3) *The 53:3 fixture (Japan T142) does not move* (73% to 71%, exchange 1.28 to 1.29): its losses come from defence passes and the door's own strikes, which run before focus fire. (4) *Doubling the kill weight (`focus_fire` 200) is worse than 100* (in-sample losses 5,567 to 5,644, fewer kills; Mongol bombers T150 losses 422 to 488), so the kill prize at cost plus threat is about right. (5) *Exempting moves within two tiles of an own city from the hold* (instead of one) gave back most of Berlin T65's gain (losses 110 to 172 of 173): defenders walking to the front one at a time die like attackers. (6) War-suite runs report engagement shape now (`attack_groups`, `lone_attack_groups`, `units_hit`, `units_hit_killed`, `isolated_losses`). (7) On this master, `war-golden-horde-thin` (the `--check` attack case, floor 30%) reads 0% locally with the genes off, and `war-walls-rise` 0%: the attack check is already failing before this branch.

On 76 held-out Hard self-play games (12,211 seat-positions), the estimate Hard's plan reads has Brier skill −33% against uniform (−80% at T1–60, +3% after T200), and the fitted Search-leaf weights −41%. The weights were fitted 10-04 at +25% skill, before VP v2 zeroed population and territory and moved the crowns. Ranking moved far less (the seat with the top estimate is the eventual winner 42.4% of the time against 43.3%), so the plan's *choices* may change less than its numbers. But several genes are fixed charges in chance units (`peace_credibility`, `campaign_commit`, 300 each), and a calibrated estimate's smaller differences let them weigh more. - 2026-10-30: **Why the designer out-economies Hard as well as out-fighting it.** Source: five of his recent wins (Japan 10-26, Athens 10-27, Sparta 10-27, Swiss 10-28, Mongols 10-30), using `history.empires` series and tape build orders; scripts in the lead's scratchpad (`econ/series.py`, `econ/builds.py`).
  - **He builds almost no army early.** In his first 60 turns he queued Walls, Granary or Farm, Settler, Market and Laboratory, with 0 to 2 military units. The AIs' production orders in that window name 6 to 15 unit items each.
    - **Correction (2026-10-31, coach):** production orders overcount units, because an AI that switches back to a Soldier repeatedly counts each time. In the Mongols game the AIs actually trained 2 to 4 military units by T60, against his 2. The robust measures are army strength (his T50 army was a third to half of the AI median in the Japan, Athens and Swiss games, and equal in the Mongols game) and upkeep paid: 76 Gold by T100 for him, against 225 to 405 for the AIs.
  - **His army strength stays far below theirs** until he needs it. At T75 it was 31 to 73 against an AI median of 92 to 128.
  - **He banks Gold.** His treasury at T50 was 160 to 421, against an AI median of 21 to 64.
  - **He converts Gold to army in a few turns.** His army jumps at T100 to T150 to 492 to 670, about the AI's best.
  - **Cities and techs stay level to T50** (tech diffusion), then he pulls ahead. At T100 he had 5 to 14 cities against an AI median of 0 to 6. Population, and science from about T75, follow the cities.
  - **Correction (2026-10-31, army-intent census, 512 games):** at T50 the AI's army is near its defensive minimum (3.05 armed against a minimum of 2.41). Idle upkeep by T50 is about 6 Gold, so his T50 Gold lead does *not* come from the AI's army. The idle army grows later: 54% of all AI upkeep is paid with nothing marching, and by T100 the share idle reaches 76 of 167 Gold. The source of the early Gold gap is still open. Candidates are his Markets against the AI's purchases (tile improvements and buys) and spending style; measure income against spending before claiming it.
  - **The AI's army is pure cost** (mid-game onward). It pays production, plus 1 Gold a turn per unit beyond 2 (3 for the Swiss), against about 13 Gold of income. It never uses that army to punish an empty empire, so he wins the economy *because* the AI pays for an army it doesn't use.
  - **Design read:** the rock-paper-scissors loop is broken on the AI side. Greedy expansion should lose to a rush, and nobody rushes him.
  - **Levers:** two candidates.
    - The AI's value for standing army against economy. The step 3 evaluator should learn this from outcomes instead of hand weights.
    - The AI actually punishing an undefended neighbour.
  - **Also seen:** AI expansion stalls after about T75, at a median 4 to 6 cities.
